knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Rates of the Inexact Semismooth Levenberg–Marquardt Newton Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local well-definedness and linear, superlinear, and quadratic rates controlled by forcing and regularization parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), with \(\Omega\) open, be semismooth at \(x^*\in\Omega\), satisfy \(G(x^*)=0\), and have every matrix in \(\partial G(x^*)\) nonsingular. There exist \(\bar\eta,\bar\sigma,\delta>0\) such that, if \(\eta_k\leq\bar\eta\) and \(\sigma_k\leq\bar\sigma\) for every \(k\), then for \(x^0\in B(x^*,\delta)\) the inexact Levenberg–Marquardt Newton method is well defined and every generated sequence converges Q-linearly to \(x^*\). If additionally \(\eta_k\to0\) and \(\sigma_k\to0\), the convergence is Q-superlinear. If, moreover, \(G\) is strongly semismooth at \(x^*\) and there exist \(\widetilde\eta,\widetilde\sigma>0\) such that \[\eta_k\leq\widetilde\eta\|(H^k)^TG(x^k)\|,\qquad\sigma_k\leq\widetilde\sigma\|(H^k)^TG(x^k)\|\quad\forall k,\] then the convergence is Q-quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a nonsingular semismooth root, uniformly small forcing and regularization parameters give a well-defined Q-linearly convergent inexact Levenberg–Marquardt Newton iteration. Vanishing parameters give Q-superlinear convergence; residual-proportional parameters and strong semismoothness give Q-quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^0\in B(x^*,\delta)\Rightarrow x^k\xrightarrow{Q\text{-linear}}x^*;\quad \eta_k,\sigma_k\to0\Rightarrow Q\text{-superlinear};\quad \substack{G\text{ strongly semismooth},\ \eta_k,\sigma_k=O(\|(H^k)^TG(x^k)\|)}\Rightarrow Q\text{-quadratic}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semismooth Inexact Newton Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-step semismooth Newton iteration using a relative residual tolerance for each generalized linearized system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given $x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and a sequence $\{\eta_k\}$ with $\eta_k\geq0$, set $k=0$. If $G(x^k)=0$, stop. Otherwise select $H^k\in\partial G(x^k)$ and find $d^k,r^k\in\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfying $G(x^k)+H^k d^k=r^k$ and $\|r^k\|\leq\eta_k\|G(x^k)\|$. Set $x^{k+1}=x^k+d^k$ and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each nonterminal iterate, select a generalized Jacobian matrix, solve the Newton equation to relative residual tolerance ηₖ, and take the full computed step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G(x^k)+H^k d^k=r^k,\quad \|r^k\|\leq\eta_k\|G(x^k)\|,\quad x^{k+1}=x^k+d^k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semismooth Inexact Levenberg–Marquardt Newton Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized generalized-Newton iteration with relative residual control in the normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and nonnegative sequences \(\{\sigma_k\}\) and \(\{\eta_k\}\), repeat while \(G(x^k)\ne0\): select \(H^k\in\partial G(x^k)\), choose \(r^k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \[\|r^k\|\leq\eta_k\|(H^k)^TG(x^k)\|,\] find \(d^k\) satisfying \[\bigl((H^k)^TH^k+\sigma_kI\bigr)d^k=-(H^k)^TG(x^k)+r^k,\] and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+d^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each non-root iterate, select a generalized Jacobian, solve an inexact regularized normal equation subject to a relative residual bound, and update by the resulting direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl((H^k)^TH^k+\sigma_kI\bigr)d^k=-(H^k)^TG(x^k)+r^k,\qquad x^{k+1}=x^k+d^k

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\) uniformly in \(k\).

source_refs.locator: 7.5 Semismooth Newton Methods p. 692

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact semismooth Newton step satisfies \[V_kd_k=-F(x_k)+r_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|.\] A fixed forcing regime requires a constant \(\bar\eta\in[0,1)\), independent of \(k\), such that \(0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta\) at every nonterminal iteration. Thus each linearized system is solved only to a uniformly prescribed relative residual accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed forcing regime bounds every relative linear-solve residual by one iteration-independent constant strictly below one.

children.title: Vanishing Forcing Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Forcing Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotically exact relative-residual forcing regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For steps satisfying \[V_kd_k=-F(x_k)+r_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|,\] a vanishing forcing regime imposes \(0\leq\eta_k<1\) and \(\eta_k\to0\). Consequently, \(\|r_k\|=o(\|F(x_k)\|)\), so the linearized equations are solved increasingly accurately relative to the nonlinear residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vanishing forcing regime sends the prescribed relative residual tolerance to zero, which makes the linear-solve residual negligible relative to the nonlinear residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_k\to0\), which implies \(\|r_k\|=o(\|F(x_k)\|)\).

notation.meaning: Residual of the inexact Newton equation

children.title: Adaptive Forcing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Accuracy regimes adjusted using observed local model behavior.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq\eta_{k+1}\leq\eta_{\max}<1\), with accuracy tightened when the observed model defect decreases.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-defect-based adaptive forcing with an upper safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), compute \(d_k\) with \(V_kd_k=-F(x_k)+r_k\) and \(\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). Define \[m_k=\frac{\|F(x_{k+1})-F(x_k)-V_kd_k\|}{\|F(x_k)\|},\qquad \eta_{k+1}=\min\{\eta_{\max},\gamma m_k^{\alpha}\}.\] Stop when \(F(x_{k+1})=0\); otherwise use \(\eta_{k+1}\) for the next linear solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The next solve tolerance is selected from the observed nonlinear-model defect and capped below one, tightening as local model agreement improves.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Forcing Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact model-defect update, exponent, normalization, and safeguards are method-dependent and have no cited authoritative source. Source verification is required before this particular adaptive algorithm can be assessed reliably.

children.title: Inexact Linear Convergence
children.top_down_role: Local linear convergence under bounded solve inaccuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Linear Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Q-linear convergence under uniformly bounded relative solve errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), let \(d_k\) satisfy \(\|V_kd_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). There exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\), a forcing threshold \(\eta_*>0\), and \(q\in(0,1)\) such that, whenever \(x_0\in U\) and \(0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<\eta_*\), the iterates are well defined, remain in \(U\), and satisfy \[\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\leq q\|x_k-x^*\|.\] Thus the iterates converge locally Q-linearly to \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly small relative linear-solve errors preserve local Q-linear convergence when the generalized Jacobians are uniformly regular.
assumptions_latex: Every \(V\in\partial F(x)\) is nonsingular for \(x\) near \(x^*\), and the inverses are uniformly bounded.
At iteration \(k\), \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) and \(\|V_kd_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\), where \(0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta\) and \(\bar\eta\) is sufficiently small.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Superlinear Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Q-superlinear convergence with vanishing relative solve error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), choose \(d_k\) satisfying \(\|V_kd_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). If \(x_0\) is sufficiently close to \(x^*\) and \(\eta_k\to0\), then the iterates are well defined, converge to \(x^*\), and satisfy \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|}{\|x_k-x^*\|}=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semismoothness, uniformly regular generalized Jacobians, and vanishing relative solve errors yield local Q-superlinear convergence.
assumptions_latex: Every \(V\in\partial F(x)\) is nonsingular for \(x\) near \(x^*\), and the inverses are uniformly bounded.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Quadratic Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic rate with first-order-decaying forcing parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), choose \(d_k\) satisfying \(\|V_kd_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). If \(x_0\) is sufficiently close to \(x^*\) and \(\eta_k=O(\|F(x_k)\|)\), then the iterates are well defined, converge to \(x^*\), and there is \(C>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(k\), \[\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\leq C\|x_k-x^*\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong semismoothness, uniformly regular generalized Jacobians, and forcing parameters proportional to the nonlinear residual yield local Q-quadratic convergence.

children.title: Residual Merit Functions
children.top_down_role: Merit-function families based on nonsmooth equation residuals.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Psi(x)\geq0\) and \(\Psi(x)=0\) if and only if \(F(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean least-squares merit for a locally Lipschitz equation residual.

source_refs.locator: 7.5 Semismooth Newton Methods p. 692
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The squared residual merit function associated with the equation \(F(x)=0\) is \[\Psi(x)=\frac12\|F(x)\|_2^2.\] It is nonnegative and locally Lipschitz, and its global minimum value is zero whenever the equation has a solution. Moreover, \(\Psi(x)=0\) holds exactly when \(F(x)=0\). Thus decrease of \(\Psi\) measures reduction of the equation residual, although stationarity of \(\Psi\) alone need not imply a zero residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual merit function is one half the squared equation residual; its zeros coincide exactly with solutions, though nonzero stationary points may exist.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Merit Functions

children.title: Complementarity Merit Functions
children.top_down_role: Merit-function families tailored to complementarity equations.

assumptions_latex: The complementarity problem is \(x\geq0\), \(G(x)\geq0\), and \(x_iG_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Psi_{\mathrm{NCP}}(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\) solves the complementarity problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fischer-Burmeister residual representation of nonlinear complementarity.

source_refs.locator: 7.5 Semismooth Newton Methods p. 692
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the Fischer-Burmeister function by \(\phi(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}-a-b\), the residual components by \(\Phi_i(x)=\phi(x_i,G_i(x))\), and the merit function by \[\Psi_{\mathrm{NCP}}(x)=\frac12\|\Phi(x)\|_2^2.\] Since \(\phi(a,b)=0\) exactly when \(a\geq0\), \(b\geq0\), and \(ab=0\), one has \(\Psi_{\mathrm{NCP}}(x)=0\) exactly when \(x\) satisfies all complementarity conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Applying the Fischer-Burmeister function componentwise produces a squared residual merit whose zeros are exactly the complementarity solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Merit Functions

children.title: Dini Stationarity
children.top_down_role: A nonsmooth stationarity framework used in global convergence theory.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed, \(x\in C\), and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is Dini stationary precisely when \(f'_{-}(x;d)\geq0\) for every \(d\in T_C(x)\).

notation.meaning: Contingent tangent cone to the feasible set at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained lower-Dini stationarity on a closed finite-dimensional feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d\in T_C(x)\), define the feasible lower Dini directional derivative by \[f'_{-}(x;d)=\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0,\ d'\to d\\ x+td'\in C}}\frac{f(x+td')-f(x)}{t}.\] The point \(x\) is Dini stationary for minimizing \(f\) over \(C\) when \(f'_{-}(x;d)\geq0\) for every \(d\in T_C(x)\). In the unconstrained case, \(T_C(x)=\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is Dini stationary when its lower Dini directional derivative is nonnegative in every contingent feasible direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Dini Stationarity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Lower- and upper-Dini stationarity conventions differ, and the proposed feasible liminf derivative is not supported by any cited source. An authoritative definition with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Bounded-Level-Set Frameworks
children.top_down_role: Boundedness structures used to support nonlocal convergence arguments.

assumptions_latex: \(\Psi:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is lower semicontinuous and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x_k\}\subseteq L_0\); if \(L_0\) is bounded, then the sequence has an accumulation point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional bounded initial-level-set framework for descent iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial point \(x_0\), define \[L_0=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\Psi(x)\leq\Psi(x_0)\}.\] A bounded-level-set framework assumes that \(L_0\) is bounded. Monotonicity of the merit values then gives \(x_k\in L_0\) for every \(k\). Because lower semicontinuity makes \(L_0\) closed, it is compact in finite dimensions; consequently, every infinite iterate sequence has an accumulation point in \(L_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If descent keeps all iterates in a bounded initial merit level set, compactness guarantees accumulation points for the global convergence analysis.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Level-Set Frameworks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compactness argument is standard and internally correct in finite dimensions, but the record supplies neither a source nor an explicit standard-field rationale. Evidence is required for candidate-review admission.

assumptions_latex: At each nonterminal \(x_k\), a continuous trial path \(p_k:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(p_k(0)=x_k\) and has predicted decrease \(\Delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Psi(x_{k+1})\leq\Psi(x_k)-\sigma t_k\Delta_k<\Psi(x_k)\).

notation.meaning: Continuous search path from the current iterate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo backtracking along a prescribed continuous Newton-type path.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from \(x_0\), stop if \(F(x_k)=0\). Otherwise construct \(p_k\) and choose the smallest integer \(j_k\geq0\) such that, with \(t_k=\beta^{j_k}\), \[\Psi(p_k(t_k))\leq\Psi(x_k)-\sigma t_k\Delta_k.\] Set \(x_{k+1}=p_k(t_k)\) and repeat. The path may interpolate between a safeguarded direction and a semismooth Newton candidate; the acceptance test enforces strict merit decrease at every nonterminal iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A path-search method backtracks along a continuous Newton-type path until an Armijo merit decrease is achieved, then accepts that path point.

children.title: Regularized Path Search
children.top_down_role: Path-search families using regularized equation systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Path Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized generalized-Newton path with residual-merit acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an iterate \(x_k\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) and a continuous regularization schedule \(\lambda_k(t)>0\) for \(t\in[0,1]\). Define the trial path by \[d_k(t)=-(V_k+\lambda_k(t)I)^{-1}F(x_k),\qquad x_k(t)=x_k+d_k(t).\] Search over increasing \(t\) until \(\phi(x_k(t))\leq \phi(x_k)-\sigma\|d_k(t)\|^2\), where \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|^2\) and \(\sigma>0\). Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k(t_k)\); stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trace regularized generalized-Newton trial points and accept the first path parameter producing sufficient residual-merit decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(V_k+\lambda_k(t)I\) is nonsingular along the searched path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) satisfies the prescribed residual-merit decrease.

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of F at x

children.title: Continuation Path Search

knowledge_statements.title: Continuation Path Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictor-corrector continuation for a parameterized nonsmooth equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H(x,\mu)=0\) approximate \(F(x)=0\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\). Starting from \((x_0,\mu_0)\) with \(\mu_0>0\), choose \(0<\theta<1\). At iteration \(k\), predict a trial pair on the solution path, set \(\mu_{k+1}=\theta\,\mu_k\), and correct \(x\) by solving \[D_xH(x_k^{\mathrm p},\mu_{k+1})d_k=-H(x_k^{\mathrm p},\mu_{k+1}),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k^{\mathrm p}+d_k.\] Repeat corrections until the prescribed residual tolerance holds; terminate when both \(\mu_k\leq\varepsilon_bc\) and \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decrease the continuation parameter, predict along the parameterized solution path, and apply Newton corrections until the original residual is small.
assumptions_latex: \(H:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\mu_0]\to\mathbb R^n\) is continuously differentiable in \(x\).
\(D_xH\) is nonsingular at accepted corrector points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an approximate zero of \(F\) reached through decreasing continuation parameters.

notation.meaning: parameterized approximation of the target equation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse Representation of a Residual-Scaling Path
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents the unique path obtained by scaling a nonzero residual through a Lipschitz homeomorphism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $A:U\to V$ be a Lipschitz homeomorphism between open subsets of $\mathbb R^n$. Suppose $x\in U$, $A(x)\neq0$, and $A(x)+\mathbb B(0,\varepsilon)\subset V$ for some $\varepsilon>0$. Set $\bar\tau=\min\{\varepsilon/\|A(x)\|,1\}$. The unique path $p:[0,\bar\tau]\to U$ satisfying $p(0)=x$ and $A(p(\tau))=(1-\tau)A(x)$ for every $\tau\in[0,\bar\tau]$ is $p(\tau)=A^{-1}((1-\tau)A(x))$. Moreover, $p$ is Lipschitz continuous on $[0,\bar\tau]$, and $A$ is a local homeomorphism near $p(\bar\tau)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual-scaling path is uniquely obtained by applying the inverse map to the scaled residual, and this path is Lipschitz continuous.
assumptions_latex: A:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is a Lipschitz homeomorphism between open sets}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(\tau)=A^{-1}((1-\tau)A(x))\text{ is the unique stated path; }p\text{ is Lipschitz, and }A\text{ is locally homeomorphic near }p(\bar\tau).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuation Property Along a Prescribed Right-Hand-Side Path
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines endpoint extendability of every partial solution lift of a prescribed path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mapping $G:\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n$ has the continuation property for a continuous function $q:[0,1]\to\mathbb R^n$ if, whenever $a\in(0,1]$ and a continuous $p:[0,a)\to\Omega$ satisfies $G(p(t))=q(t)$ for all $t\in[0,a)$, the limit $p(a):=\lim_{t\uparrow a}p(t)$ exists, belongs to $\Omega$, and satisfies $G(p(a))=q(a)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every partial continuous lift of the prescribed right-hand-side path must have an endpoint in the domain that still solves the equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[G(p(t))=q(t)\ \forall t\in[0,a)\bigr]\Longrightarrow \exists\,p(a)=\lim_{t\uparrow a}p(t)\in\Omega\text{ with }G(p(a))=q(a).

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Residual Line Searches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo backtracking on the squared residual merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) and \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|^2\). At \(x_k\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) and a direction \(d_k\) satisfying \(V_kd_k=-F(x_k)\). Given \(0<\beta<1\) and \(0<\sigma<1\), select the smallest integer \(j_k\geq0\) such that \[\phi(x_k+\beta^{j_k}d_k)\leq\phi(x_k)+\sigma\beta^{j_k}\phi'(x_k;d_k).\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\beta^{j_k}d_k\), and stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack along a generalized Newton direction until the squared residual satisfies monotone Armijo decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is locally Lipschitz and directionally differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi(x_{k+1})<\phi(x_k)\) whenever \(F(x_k)\neq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonmonotone Line Searches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-memory nonmonotone Armijo search for residual merit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|^2\), and fix an integer \(M\geq1\). Given a descent direction \(d_k\), define \[R_k=\max_{0\leq i\leq\min\{k,M-1\}}\phi(x_{k-i}).\] For \(0<\beta<1\) and \(0<\sigma<1\), select the smallest integer \(j_k\geq0\) such that \[\phi(x_k+\beta^{j_k}d_k)\leq R_k+\sigma\beta^{j_k}\phi'(x_k;d_k).\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\beta^{j_k}d_k\), and stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permit temporary residual-merit increases while requiring Armijo decrease relative to the largest recent merit value.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi'(x_k;d_k)<0\) whenever the stopping condition is not satisfied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi(x_{k+1})\leq R_k+\sigma\beta^{j_k}\phi'(x_k;d_k)<R_k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Transition to Fast Local Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual unit steps and semismooth Newton local rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(F(x_*)=0\), be semismooth near \(x_*\), and have every \(V\in\partial F(x)\) nonsingular with uniformly bounded inverse for \(x\) near \(x_*\). For \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), let \(d_k=-V_k^{-1}F(x_k)\). Suppose \(x_k\to x_*\), and backtracking accepts \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) when \[\|F(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\|^2\leq(1-2\sigma\alpha_k)\|F(x_k)\|^2\] for a fixed \(0<\sigma<\tfrac12\). Then \(\alpha_k=1\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), and \[\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|=o(\|x_k-x_*\|).\] If \(F\) is strongly semismooth near \(x_*\), then \[\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|=O(\|x_k-x_*\|^2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular root, residual Armijo backtracking with a parameter below one half eventually accepts full semismooth Newton steps, yielding superlinear convergence and quadratic convergence under strong semismoothness.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is semismooth near a zero \(x_*\).
Every \(V\in\partial F(x)\) near \(x_*\) is nonsingular, and the inverses are uniformly bounded.
\(x_k\to x_*\), and the displayed residual Armijo rule is used with \(0<\sigma<\tfrac12\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eventually \(\alpha_k=1\), with superlinear convergence and quadratic convergence under strong semismoothness.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Trust-Region Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-Jacobian model of squared residual within a trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), an iterate \(x_k\), and \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), define \[m_k(d)=\tfrac12\|F(x_k)+V_kd\|^2,\qquad \|d\|\leq\Delta_k.\] A trial step \(d_k\) approximately minimizes this model in the trust-region ball of radius \(\Delta_k>0\). For \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|^2\), define \[\operatorname{pred}_k=m_k(0)-m_k(d_k),\qquad \operatorname{ared}_k=\phi(x_k)-\phi(x_k+d_k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearize the nonsmooth residual with a generalized Jacobian, minimize its squared norm in a trust-region ball, and compare predicted with actual residual-merit reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k\), \(\operatorname{pred}_k\), and \(\operatorname{ared}_k\) form the trust-region model-quality interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order global convergence of residual trust-region iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let trial steps satisfy a uniform fraction of Cauchy decrease for \(m_k\), and accept them when \(\rho_k=operatorname{ared}_k/\operatorname{pred}_k\geq\eta\), with standard radius contraction after rejection and possible expansion after very successful steps. Suppose the initial residual level set is compact, the selected matrices \(V_k\) are bounded, and the model errors are first-order accurate uniformly on that set. Then \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|V_k^TF(x_k)\|=0.\] If the stationarity measure is uniformly continuous along the iterates, the limit is zero. If every stationary accumulation point is a zero of \(F\), every accumulation point solves \(F(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard ratio-based trust-region updates drive the generalized residual stationarity measure to zero under compactness and accurate models.
assumptions_latex: The initial residual level set is compact and \(V_k\) is bounded.
Trial steps achieve a uniform fraction of Cauchy decrease.
Model errors are uniformly first-order accurate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\liminf_k\|V_k^TF(x_k)\|=0\), with root convergence under the stated stationarity-to-root condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Implementable Decrease Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable fraction-of-Cauchy-decrease test for residual models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[m_k(d)=\tfrac12\|F(x_k)+V_kd\|^2\] define \(g_k=V_k^TF(x_k)\). A step \(d_k\) with \(\|d_k\|\leq\Delta_k\) satisfies a fraction-of-Cauchy-decrease condition if, for a fixed \(0<\kappa\leq1\), \[m_k(0)-m_k(d_k)\geq\frac{\kappa}{2}\|g_k\|\min\left\{\Delta_k,\frac{\|g_k\|}{\|V_k^TV_k\|}\right\}.\] Here the matrix norm is the operator norm induced by the vector norm. The condition is computable before evaluating \(F(x_k+d_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Require the computed feasible step to obtain a fixed fraction of a computable Cauchy reduction for the quadratic residual model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality certifies adequate predicted decrease using computable quantities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient step-size bounds for generalized Cauchy-point tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives explicit sufficient bounds for the model-decrease and trust-region tests defining the generalized Cauchy point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under Assumption 7.13, let \(u_k\in\mathcal K\), \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), and \(\widehat\sigma=\min\{1,2(1-\gamma)/C_B\}\). If \(0<\sigma_k\leq\widehat\sigma\), then \(q_k(\pi_k(\sigma_k))\leq\gamma(g_k,\pi_k(\sigma_k))_U\). Furthermore, for every \(\sigma_k\in(0,1]\), if \(\sigma_k\|g_k\|_U\leq\Delta_k\), then \(\|\pi_k(\sigma_k)\|_U\leq\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the referenced model-bound assumption, every sufficiently small projected-gradient path parameter passes the model-decrease test. A parameter whose unprojected gradient-step norm fits within the trust-region radius also passes the projected-step radius test.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected-gradient generalized Cauchy point and fraction-of-Cauchy-decrease condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a projected-gradient reference step and its implementable predicted-decrease comparison in semismooth-Newton trust-region globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_k\in\mathcal K\) and define \(\chi^P(u)=\|u-P_{\mathcal K}(u-f'(u))\|_U\), where the criticality measure \(\chi\) satisfies \(\theta\chi(u)\leq\chi^P(u)\) for fixed \(\theta>0\). Define \(\pi_k(t)=P_{\mathcal K}(u_k-tg_k)-u_k\). For fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), let \(\sigma_k\) be the largest element of \(\{1,2^{-1},2^{-2},\ldots\}\) such that \(q_k(\pi_k(\sigma_k))\leq\gamma(g_k,\pi_k(\sigma_k))_U\) and \(\|\pi_k(\sigma_k)\|_U\leq\Delta_k\), and set \(s_k^c=\pi_k(\sigma_k)\). A trial step \(s_k\) satisfies the fraction-of-Cauchy-decrease condition when \(\operatorname{pred}_k(s_k)\geq\beta_3\operatorname{pred}_k(s_k^c)\), where \(\beta_3\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The generalized Cauchy point is selected by dyadic backtracking along the projected-gradient path until the model-decrease and trust-region tests hold. A trial step provides a fraction of Cauchy decrease when its predicted reduction is at least a fixed fraction of the reference point's predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s_k^c=\pi_k(\sigma_k),\qquad \operatorname{pred}_k(s_k)\geq\beta_3\operatorname{pred}_k(s_k^c).

children.top_down_role: Recovery of semismooth Newton rates after successful localization.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Transition to Fast Local Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual acceptance of unrestricted semismooth Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\to x_*\), where \(F(x_*)=0\), \(F\) is semismooth, and every generalized Jacobian near \(x_*\) is uniformly nonsingular. Suppose the trust-region method tests \(d_k=-V_k^{-1}F(x_k)\), uses the generalized-Newton residual model, and accepts steps whenever the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio exceeds a fixed threshold below one. Then \(\rho_k\to1\), the trust-region constraint is eventually inactive, and all sufficiently large Newton trial steps are accepted. Consequently, \[\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|=o(\|x_k-x_*\|).\] Strong semismoothness yields quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular solution, model agreement approaches one, the trust region stops restricting Newton steps, and fast local convergence returns.
assumptions_latex: Generalized Jacobians near \(x_*\) are uniformly invertible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k\to1\) and unrestricted Newton steps are eventually accepted, giving superlinear or quadratic convergence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Criticality of the Trust-Region Projected Newton Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global accepted-step and criticality guarantee for Algorithm 7.27.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose Assumption 7.25 holds, \(\gamma_0>0\) or \(\Delta_{\min}=0\), and Algorithm 7.27 does not terminate after finitely many steps at a critical point of (7.6). Then the algorithm generates infinitely many accepted steps \((s_{j_i})\), and \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\chi(u_k)=0.\] In particular, if \(u_k\to\bar u\), then \(\bar u\) is a critical point of (7.6).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumption 7.25 and the stated alternative on gamma zero or the minimum trust-region radius, a run that does not terminate finitely at a critical point generates infinitely many accepted steps and has criticality liminf zero. Any limit of the full iterate sequence is critical.
assumptions_latex: \text{Algorithm 7.27 does not terminate finitely at a critical point of (7.6).}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \#\{i:s_{j_i}\text{ is accepted}\}=\infty,\qquad \liminf_{k\to\infty}\chi(u_k)=0,\qquad u_k\to\bar u\Longrightarrow\bar u\text{ is critical for (7.6).}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fast Local Convergence After Trust-Region Globalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region-specific superlinear and order-dependent convergence of Algorithm 7.27.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Assumption 7.25 hold and \(\Delta_{\min}>0\). Suppose Algorithm 7.27 generates an infinite sequence \((u_k)\) such that \(u_k\to\bar u\) and \(\Phi(\bar u)=0\). Assume that \(\Phi\) is \(\partial\Phi\)-semismooth at \(\bar u\) and Lipschitz continuous near \(\bar u\). Further suppose that, whenever \(u_k\) is sufficiently close to \(\bar u\), \(M_k\) is invertible and \(\|M_k^{-1}\|_{U,U}\le C_{M^{-1}}\). Then \((u_k)\) converges q-superlinearly to \(\bar u\). If \(\Phi\) is \(\alpha\)-order semismooth at \(\bar u\), where \(0<\alpha\le1\), then its q-order is at least \(1+\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If Algorithm 7.27 produces an infinite sequence converging to a zero of Phi, Phi is locally Lipschitz and semismooth there, and the selected generalized derivatives have uniformly bounded inverses nearby, then convergence is q-superlinear. Alpha-order semismoothness gives q-order at least one plus alpha.
assumptions_latex: \text{Algorithm 7.27 generates an infinite sequence }(u_k)\text{ with }u_k\to\bar u\text{ and }\Phi(\bar u)=0.
\Phi\text{ is }\partial\Phi\text{-semismooth at }\bar u\text{ and Lipschitz continuous near }\bar u.
u_k\text{ sufficiently close to }\bar u\Longrightarrow M_k\text{ is invertible and }\|M_k^{-1}\|_{U,U}\le C_{M^{-1}}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_k\xrightarrow[q]{\mathrm{superlinear}}\bar u;\qquad \Phi\text{ being }\alpha\text{-order semismooth},\ 0<\alpha\le1\Longrightarrow q\text{-order}\ge1+\alpha.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-Region Projected Newton Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Globalized projected semismooth Newton iteration on a constraint set \(\mathcal K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\eta_1,v\in(0,1)\), \(\Delta_{\min}\ge0\), \(u_0\in\mathcal K\), \(\Delta_0>\Delta_{\min}\), a criticality measure \(\chi\), model Hessians \(B_k\), memory \(m\ge1\), and \(\lambda\in(0,1/m]\). At iteration \(k\), stop if \(\chi(u_k)=0\); otherwise choose \(M_k\in\partial\Phi(u_k)\) and attempt \(M_ks_k^{n,1}=-\Phi(u_k)\). If solvable, project and truncate via \(s_k^{n,2}=P_{\mathcal K}(u_k+s_k^{n,1})-u_k\) and \(s_k^n=\min\{1,\Delta_k/\|s_k^{n,2}\|_U\}s_k^{n,2}\). Use this Newton trial when its residual passes the prescribed reference-residual and condition-(7.11) tests; otherwise compute a safeguarded trial satisfying (7.10) and (7.11). Compute the possibly nonmonotone ratio \(\rho_k\) using Algorithm 7.11, update \(\Delta_{k+1}\) using Algorithm 7.10, accept when the stated ratio tests succeed, and otherwise reject while retaining the iterate and reusable model data. Repeat with the prescribed accepted-step and memory indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method stops at zero criticality. Otherwise it attempts a generalized Newton solve, projects the candidate onto K, truncates it to the trust region, and uses it if residual and model-quality tests succeed. On failure it computes a safeguarded trust-region step. A possibly nonmonotone reduction ratio controls radius updates, acceptance or rejection, and reuse of model information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure generates accepted or rejected trust-region iterates in }\mathcal K\text{ until }\chi(u_k)=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fast Convergence from a Solution Accumulation Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region-specific upgrade from a solution accumulation point to fast convergence of the full Algorithm 7.27 sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Assumption 7.25 hold and \(\Delta_{\min}>0\). Suppose Algorithm 7.27 generates an infinite sequence \((u_k)\) having an accumulation point \(\bar u\) with \(\Phi(\bar u)=0\). Assume that \(\Phi\) is \(\partial\Phi\)-semismooth at \(\bar u\) and Lipschitz continuous near \(\bar u\). Further suppose that, whenever \(u_k\) is sufficiently close to \(\bar u\), \(M_k\) is invertible and \(\|M_k^{-1}\|_{U,U}\le C_{M^{-1}}\), and assume condition (7.33). Then the full sequence \((u_k)\) converges q-superlinearly to \(\bar u\). If \(\Phi\) is \(\alpha\)-order semismooth at \(\bar u\), where \(0<\alpha\le1\), then its q-order is at least \(1+\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumption 7.25, a positive minimum radius, local Lipschitz continuity and semismoothness, uniformly bounded inverses of the selected generalized derivatives, and condition (7.33), a solution accumulation point forces the full Algorithm 7.27 sequence to converge q-superlinearly to that point. Alpha-order semismoothness gives q-order at least one plus alpha.

\Phi\text{ is }\partial\Phi\text{-semismooth at }\bar u\text{ and Lipschitz continuous near }\bar u.
u_k\text{ sufficiently close to }\bar u\Longrightarrow M_k\text{ is invertible and }\|M_k^{-1}\|_{U,U}\le C_{M^{-1}}.

knowledge_statements.title: Smoothing Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton iteration on smooth parameterized approximations of a nonsmooth equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) and let \(H:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\mu_0]\to\mathbb R^n\) be a smooth approximation of \(F\). Choose \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\mu_0>0\), tolerances \(\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_\mu>0\), and \(0<\theta<1\). At iteration \(k\), solve \[D_xH(x_k,\mu_k)d_k=-H(x_k,\mu_k).\] Choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) using a merit-function globalization for \(H(\cdot,\mu_k)\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and, after adequate correction, choose \(0<\mu_{k+1}\leq\theta\mu_k\). Stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_F\) and \(\mu_k\leq\varepsilon_\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply globalized Newton corrections to smooth approximations while reducing the smoothing parameter toward zero, and stop when both the original residual and smoothing parameter are small.
assumptions_latex: The displayed Newton systems are solvable at the generated iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the stopping test is reached, the output satisfies \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_F\) and \(\mu_k\leq\varepsilon_\mu\).

notation.meaning: smooth approximation of the nonsmooth residual

knowledge_statements.title: Newton Methods without Smoothing Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct semismooth Newton iteration using generalized Jacobians and residual line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), repeat while \(\|F(x_k)\|>\varepsilon\): choose a nonsingular \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), compute \(d_k\) from \[V_kd_k=-F(x_k),\] choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) by a residual line-search acceptance rule, and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). No smooth approximation or auxiliary smoothing parameter is introduced. When \(\alpha_k=1\), the update is the direct semismooth Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve generalized-Jacobian Newton systems directly and globalize them by residual line search without introducing a smoothing parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is locally Lipschitz and semismooth.
A nonsingular \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) can be selected at each generated iterate.
The residual line-search rule is well defined for the generated directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the stopping test is reached, the output satisfies \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\).

children.title: Jacobian Regularization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization families for singular or ill-conditioned Newton models.

knowledge_statements.title: Jacobian Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive identity regularization of a semismooth Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), an initial \(\lambda_k>0\), a growth factor \(\gamma>1\), and a conditioning threshold \(\tau>0\). While \(\sigma_{\min}(V_k+\lambda_k I)<\tau\), replace \(\lambda_k\) by \(\gamma\lambda_k\). If the test is met, compute \(d_k\) from
\[(V_k+\lambda_k I)d_k=-F(x_k).\]
For every accepted shift, \(V_k+\lambda_k I\) is nonsingular and
\[\bigl\|(V_k+\lambda_k I)^{-1}\bigr\|_2=\frac{1}{\sigma_{\min}(V_k+\lambda_k I)}\leq\frac{1}{\tau}.\]
A positive shift alone does not ensure nonsingularity for a general nonsymmetric \(V_k\), and the procedure requires a separate condition ensuring that a shift satisfying the test is eventually found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase a positive identity shift until the shifted generalized Jacobian meets a specified smallest-singular-value threshold, then solve the regularized Newton system; positivity of the shift alone does not guarantee success.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\sigma_{\min}(V_k+\lambda_k I)\geq\tau\), then the regularized system is uniquely solvable and \(\|(V_k+\lambda_k I)^{-1}\|_2\leq1/\tau\).

children.title: Non-Descent Newton Directions
children.top_down_role: Newton directions incompatible with the selected merit framework.

assumptions_latex: At \(x\), a Newton direction \(d\) satisfies \(Vd=-F(x)\) for some nonsingular \(V\in\partial F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\Psi^{\circ}(x;d)\geq0\), then \(d\) is not a strict descent direction for \(\Psi\), so an Armijo rule requiring a negative first-order decrease cannot be justified from this direction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of residual-merit descent for a selected generalized Newton direction.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Basic Descent Methods for Smooth Problems p. 89

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A generalized Newton equation may be solvable without producing descent for the chosen merit function. Specifically, let \(d\) solve \(Vd=-F(x)\) with \(V\in\partial F(x)\) nonsingular. If
\[\Psi^{\circ}(x;d)\geq0,\]
then there need not exist arbitrarily small \(t>0\) for which \(\Psi(x+td)<\Psi(x)\). Consequently, a globalization mechanism based solely on an Armijo decrease along \(d\) can reject every sufficiently small trial step; a descent modification, alternative merit function, or fallback direction is then required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solvable generalized Newton system can yield a direction with nonnegative merit derivative, preventing an Armijo descent line search from accepting small steps.
knowledge_statements.title: Non-Descent Newton Directions

children.title: Unbounded Merit Level Sets
children.top_down_role: Loss of bounded-iterate mechanisms in globalization analysis.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(L_0\) is unbounded, merit monotonicity alone does not imply boundedness of \((x_k)\) and therefore does not ensure the existence of an accumulation point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-iterate conclusion lost when the initial merit sublevel set is unbounded.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Level Sets p. 51
source_refs.source_title: Introduction to Nonsmooth Optimization: Theory, Practice and Software

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the initial sublevel set by
\[L_0:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\Psi(x)\leq\Psi(x_0)\}.\]
Merit monotonicity gives \(x_k\in L_0\) for every accepted iterate. If \(L_0\) is unbounded, this inclusion supplies no boundedness guarantee: a sequence can remain in \(L_0\) while \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\). Thus a convergence argument that extracts an accumulation point from merit decrease requires an additional boundedness or coercivity hypothesis; merit decrease by itself is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the initial merit sublevel set is unbounded, decreasing merit does not prevent iterates from escaping to infinity or guarantee accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Merit Level Sets

children.top_down_role: Globalization controls that remain active inside the expected fast local regime.

children.title: Persistent Damping Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local regimes where damping remains active despite proximity to a solution.

assumptions_latex: There is an infinite index set \(K\) and a constant \(\bar t<1\) such that \(t_k\leq\bar t\) for every \(k\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Along \(K\), the method never enters the eventual full-step regime \(t_k=1\); hence any local superlinear-rate theorem requiring eventual full steps is inapplicable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent line-search damping as a boundary of eventual full-step convergence theory.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. General Schemes for Investigating Iterative Methods p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A persistent damping regime occurs when there exist an infinite set \(K\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) and \(\bar t<1\) such that
\[0<t_k\leq\bar t\qquad(k\in K).\]
Then full Newton steps are not eventually accepted. Even if the undamped directions satisfy a local semismooth Newton estimate, that estimate does not by itself establish superlinear convergence of the actual iteration \(x_{k+1}=x_k+t_kd_k\), because the accepted displacement differs from \(d_k\) by the nonvanishing factor \(1-t_k\) along \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If accepted step lengths stay uniformly below one infinitely often, the method never reaches an eventual full-step regime and standard fast-rate results do not apply.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Damping Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. General Schemes for Investigating Iterative Methods p. 37

children.title: Persistent Regularization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local regimes where stabilizing regularization fails to disappear.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Regularization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonvanishing Jacobian regularization excludes local theory premised on asymptotically exact Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A persistent regularization regime occurs when \(R_k\not\to0\). Equivalently, in a finite-dimensional matrix norm, there exist \(\rho>0\) and an infinite set \(K\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) such that
\[\|R_k\|\geq\rho\qquad(k\in K).\]
The directions then solve a Newton equation whose perturbation is not asymptotically negligible. Consequently, a local semismooth Newton theorem requiring \(\|R_k\|\to0\), or a stronger residual-relative decay condition, cannot be applied without a separate result controlling the persistent perturbation. Nonsingularity of \(V_k+R_k\) alone does not supply such control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularization that does not converge to zero remains a nonnegligible perturbation, so fast-rate theory requiring asymptotically exact Newton systems cannot be invoked without additional analysis.
assumptions_latex: The computed direction satisfies \((V_k+R_k)d_k=-F(x_k)\), where \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\).
The matrices are finite-dimensional and \(R_k\not\to0\) in the specified matrix norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A local convergence theorem requiring \(\|R_k\|\to0\), or a stronger residual-relative decay condition, cannot be invoked for this regime without a separate perturbation result.

notation.meaning: infinite index set on which regularization is bounded away from zero

children.title: Fast-Regime Suppression
children.top_down_role: Loss of the expected fast local behavior under persistent safeguards.

knowledge_statements.title: Fast-Regime Suppression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An asymptotically nonnegligible aggregate globalization modification can suppress the fast local Newton mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the pure Newton update satisfies
\[\|x_k+d_k-x_*\|=o(\|x_k-x_*\|).\]
For actual updates \(x_{k+1}=x_k+t_kd_k+r_k\), define the aggregate globalization modification by
\[q_k:=-(1-t_k)d_k+r_k.\]
Then
\[x_{k+1}-x_*=(x_k+d_k-x_*)+q_k.\]
If \(q_k\) is not \(o(\|x_k-x_*\|)\), the accepted iteration does not inherit the displayed superlinear estimate. Conditions on the damping and safeguard terms separately are insufficient unless they also control their aggregate, since those terms may cancel.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fast pure-Newton estimate is suppressed when the combined damping and safeguard modification is not negligible relative to the current error; examining the two modifications separately does not exclude cancellation.
assumptions_latex: The iterates satisfy \(x_k\neq x_*\) on the indices considered and the pure Newton update obeys \(\|x_k+d_k-x_*\|=o(\|x_k-x_*\|)\).
Actual steps satisfy \(x_{k+1}=x_k+t_kd_k+r_k\), and \(q_k:=-(1-t_k)d_k+r_k\) is not \(o(\|x_k-x_*\|)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The actual iterates do not satisfy \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|=o(\|x_k-x_*\|)\) under the stated aggregate-modification condition.

children.title: Safeguard Deactivation Failure
children.top_down_role: Conditions and diagnostics associated with safeguards that do not become inactive.

assumptions_latex: A safeguarded method selects a pure Newton step only when a test \(S_k\) is satisfied.
The iterates converge to \(x_*\), but \(S_k\) fails for infinitely many indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The safeguard does not deactivate eventually, so any convergence theorem conditional on eventual pure Newton steps does not apply to the generated sequence.

notation.meaning: safeguard acceptance predicate at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary for local results requiring eventual selection of pure Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the update use \(d_k=d_k^N\) when the predicate \(S_k\) holds and \(d_k=d_k^S\) otherwise. Safeguard deactivation means that there exists \(k_0\) such that \(S_k\) holds for every \(k\geq k_0\). Deactivation fails precisely when
\[\forall k_0\in\mathbb{N}\;\exists k\geq k_0\text{ such that }S_k\text{ fails}.\]
In that case safeguarded steps occur infinitely often, and a local superlinear-convergence argument that identifies the tail iteration with the pure semismooth Newton method has an unmet hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the safeguard test keeps failing arbitrarily late, safeguarded steps occur infinitely often and eventual pure-Newton convergence theory is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.title: Safeguard Deactivation Failure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical formulation is coherent and the failure-boundary kind fits, but the record supplies no citation for the safeguard predicate, its algorithmic interpretation, or the local theorem whose hypothesis is said to fail.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: MFBLSA inherits the Fischer–Burmeister line-search convergence guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers all four global and local conclusions of Theorem 9.1.29 to infinite sequences generated by MFBLSA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n be continuously differentiable, let T be a linear Newton approximation scheme for \mathbf F_{\mathrm{FB}}, and let \{x^k\} be an infinite sequence generated by MFBLSA. Then statements (a)--(d) of Theorem 9.1.29 hold for \{x^k\}: accumulation points are stationary for \theta_{\mathrm{FB}}; FB-regular accumulation points solve \operatorname{NCP}(F); an isolated limit point attracts the whole sequence; and the stated generalized-Jacobian inclusion and nonsingularity assumptions at a solution limit point yield whole-sequence convergence, eventual Newton directions and unit steps, and Q-superlinear convergence, strengthened to Q-quadratic convergence when JF is locally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every global and local convergence conclusion of Theorem 9.1.29 also holds for iterates generated by MFBLSA, including stationary accumulation points, solution identification under FB regularity, whole-sequence convergence, eventual unit Newton steps, and the stated superlinear or quadratic rates.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is a linear Newton approximation scheme for }\mathbf F_{\mathrm{FB}}
\{x^k\}\text{ is an infinite sequence generated by MFBLSA}
\text{The additional hypotheses attached to the respective conclusions of Theorem 9.1.29 hold}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Statements (a)--(d) of Theorem 9.1.29 remain valid for }\{x^k\}\text{ generated by MFBLSA.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global and local convergence of the Fischer–Burmeister Newton line-search algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationary accumulation points, solution identification under FB regularity, whole-sequence convergence, eventual Newton steps, and local convergence rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n be continuously differentiable, let T be a linear Newton approximation scheme for \mathbf F_{\mathrm{FB}}, and let \{x^k\} be an infinite sequence generated by Algorithm 9.1.10. Every accumulation point of \{x^k\} is stationary for \theta_{\mathrm{FB}}, and every FB-regular accumulation point solves \operatorname{NCP}(F). If \{x^k\} has an isolated limit point, the whole sequence converges to that point. If x^* is a solution of \operatorname{NCP}(F) and a limit point, T(x)\subseteq\partial\mathbf F_{\mathrm{FB}}(x) near x^*, and every matrix in T(x^*) is nonsingular, then x^k\to x^*. If additionally p>2 and \gamma<\tfrac12, eventually d^k solves system (9.1.5), unit steps are accepted, and convergence is Q-superlinear; if JF is Lipschitz continuous near x^*, convergence is Q-quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For Algorithm 9.1.10, every accumulation point is stationary for the Fischer–Burmeister merit function, and an FB-regular accumulation point solves the NCP. An isolated limit point attracts the whole sequence. At a solution limit point, generalized-Jacobian inclusion and nonsingularity yield whole-sequence convergence; the additional parameter conditions give eventual unit Newton steps and Q-superlinear convergence, strengthened to Q-quadratic convergence when the Jacobian of F is locally Lipschitz.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is a linear Newton approximation scheme for }\mathbf F_{\mathrm{FB}}
\{x^k\}\text{ is an infinite sequence generated by Algorithm 9.1.10}

x^*\in\operatorname{SOL}(\operatorname{NCP}(F))\text{ is a limit point},\quad T(x)\subseteq\partial\mathbf F_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)\text{ near }x^*,\quad H\text{ is nonsingular for every }H\in T(x^*)\text{ for the local conclusions}
JF\text{ is Lipschitz continuous near }x^*\text{ for Q-quadratic convergence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{acc}\{x^k\}\subseteq\operatorname{stat}(\theta_{\mathrm{FB}}),\qquad x^*\text{ FB-regular}\Rightarrow x^*\in\operatorname{SOL}(\operatorname{NCP}(F)),\qquad x^k\to x^*\text{ under either stated whole-sequence condition, with the stated eventual-step and rate conclusions under their additional assumptions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fischer–Burmeister and Perturbed Fischer–Burmeister Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the scalar Fischer–Burmeister mapping and its perturbed form. Although the source declares the latter on all of R^3, its displayed real-valued formula requires a nonnegative radicand.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Fischer--Burmeister function is \(\Phi:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\) defined by \(\Phi(a,b)=a+b-\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\). The perturbed Fischer--Burmeister expression is \(\Phi(a,b,\varepsilon)=a+b-\sqrt{a^2+b^2+\varepsilon}\); as a real-valued expression, it is defined when \(a^2+b^2+\varepsilon\ge 0\), in particular for \(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Fischer–Burmeister function equals a+b minus the Euclidean norm of (a,b). Its perturbed expression adds epsilon under the square root and is real-valued only when the radicand is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi(a,b)=a+b-\sqrt{a^2+b^2},\qquad \Phi(a,b,\varepsilon)=a+b-\sqrt{a^2+b^2+\varepsilon}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fischer–Burmeister Regularity and Merit Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the Fischer–Burmeister NCP function, its regularity, and its squared-residual merit construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Fischer–Burmeister function \[\phi^{FB}(x_1,x_2)=x_1+x_2-\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2}\] is an NCP function. It is Lipschitz continuous and first-order semismooth on \(\mathbb R^2\), is \(C^\infty\) on \(\mathbb R^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}\), and its square \((\phi^{FB})^2\) is continuously differentiable on \(\mathbb R^2\). If \(F:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable and \(\Phi_i^{FB}(u)=\phi^{FB}(u_i,F_i(u))\), then \[\Psi(u)=\frac12\,\Phi^{FB}(u)^T\Phi^{FB}(u)\] is a continuously differentiable merit function for \(\Phi^{FB}(u)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Fischer–Burmeister function is Lipschitz and first-order semismooth, is smooth away from the origin, and has a continuously differentiable square. Consequently, for continuously differentiable F, the squared norm of its componentwise residual is a continuously differentiable merit function.
assumptions_latex: F:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^m\text{ is continuously differentiable}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Psi(u)=\tfrac12\Phi^{FB}(u)^T\Phi^{FB}(u)\in C^1

children.title: Fischer-Burmeister Equation Representation
children.top_down_role: Equation-level Fischer-Burmeister representation of complementarity.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complementarity system \(a\geq0\), \(b\geq0\), and \(a^{\mathsf T}b=0\) is equivalent to \(\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a,b)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise finite-dimensional representation using the nonnegative-complementarity sign convention.

source_refs.locator: 7.5 Semismooth Newton Methods p. 692
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(s,t):=\sqrt{s^2+t^2}-s-t\]
and \(\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a,b)_i:=\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a_i,b_i)\). For every scalar pair,
\[\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(s,t)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad s\geq0,\quad t\geq0,\quad st=0.\]
Therefore
\[\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a,b)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a\geq0,\quad b\geq0,\quad a^{\mathsf T}b=0.\]
For a nonlinear complementarity problem with \(a=x\) and \(b=F(x)\), its solutions are exactly the zeros of \(x\mapsto\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x,F(x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The componentwise Fischer-Burmeister residual vanishes exactly when both vectors are nonnegative and complementary.
knowledge_statements.title: Fischer-Burmeister Equation Representation

knowledge_statements.title: Fischer-Burmeister Generalized-Jacobian Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar Clarke generalized-Jacobian formula underlying componentwise Fischer-Burmeister systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \((s,t)\neq(0,0)\), put \(r:=\sqrt{s^2+t^2}\). Then
\[\partial_C\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(s,t)=\left\{\left(\frac{s}{r}-1,\frac{t}{r}-1\right)\right\}.\]
At the origin,
\[\partial_C\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(0,0)=\{(u-1,v-1):u^2+v^2\leq1\}.\]
The limiting gradients at the origin correspond to \(u^2+v^2=1\), while the Clarke generalized Jacobian is their convex hull, namely the translated closed unit disk. For a componentwise Fischer-Burmeister residual paired with smooth mappings, generalized-Jacobian matrices are assembled from these scalar selections using an applicable generalized chain rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Away from the origin the Fischer-Burmeister derivative is unique. At the origin the limiting gradients form a translated unit circle, whose convex hull is the Clarke generalized-Jacobian disk.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Away from \((0,0)\), the Clarke generalized Jacobian is the singleton containing the classical gradient; at \((0,0)\), it is \(\{(u-1,v-1):u^2+v^2\leq1\}\), the convex hull of the limiting-gradient circle.

children.title: Fischer-Burmeister Merit Framework
children.top_down_role: Merit-function families derived from the Fischer-Burmeister residual.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(\Psi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)=\tfrac12\|H(x)\|^2\) is nonnegative, and \(\Psi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)=0\) holds exactly at solutions of the nonlinear complementarity problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Squared Euclidean residual merit function for nonlinear complementarity.

source_refs.locator: 7.5 Semismooth Newton Methods p. 692
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the residual and merit function by
\[H(x):=\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x,F(x)),\qquad \Psi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x):=\frac12\|H(x)\|_2^2.\]
Then \(\Psi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)\geq0\) for every \(x\), and
\[\Psi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\geq0,\quad F(x)\geq0,\quad x^{\mathsf T}F(x)=0.\]
Although \(H\) is generally nonsmooth at biactive components, its squared residual is the canonical scalar merit quantity used to compare trial points and to formulate descent or sufficient-decrease tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared norm of the Fischer-Burmeister residual is nonnegative and vanishes exactly at complementary solutions, making it a natural globalization merit function.
knowledge_statements.title: Fischer-Burmeister Merit Framework

children.title: Minimum-Function Reformulation
children.top_down_role: Complementarity equations constructed from componentwise minimum mappings.

assumptions_latex: Minimum and inequalities are interpreted componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equation \(M(a,b)=0\) is equivalent to \(a\geq0\), \(b\geq0\), and \(a^{\mathsf T}b=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise minimum equation for nonnegative complementarity.

source_refs.locator: 7.5 Semismooth Newton Methods p. 692
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the componentwise minimum mapping by
\[M(a,b)_i:=\min\{a_i,b_i\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\]
For each component, \(\min\{a_i,b_i\}=0\) holds exactly when \(a_i\geq0\), \(b_i\geq0\), and \(a_ib_i=0\). Hence
\[M(a,b)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a\geq0,\quad b\geq0,\quad a^{\mathsf T}b=0.\]
In particular, the nonlinear complementarity problem for \(F\) is equivalently the nonsmooth equation \(M(x,F(x))=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The componentwise minimum of two vectors vanishes exactly when they are nonnegative and complementary, yielding an equation reformulation of complementarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Function Reformulation

knowledge_statements.title: General C-Function Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic componentwise reformulation generated by any exact scalar complementarity function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A scalar complementarity function is a mapping \(\phi:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying
\[\phi(s,t)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad s\geq0,\quad t\geq0,\quad st=0.\]
Its componentwise residual for the nonlinear complementarity problem is
\[H_\phi(x)_i:=\phi(x_i,F_i(x)),\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\]
Consequently,
\[H_\phi(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\geq0,\quad F(x)\geq0,\quad x^{\mathsf T}F(x)=0.\]
Additional assumptions such as local Lipschitz continuity or semismoothness of \(\phi\) are needed only when derivative-based solution methods are applied to this exact reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any scalar function whose zeros exactly encode nonnegative complementarity produces, componentwise, an equation system equivalent to the nonlinear complementarity problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zeros of \(H_\phi(x)=(\phi(x_i,F_i(x)))_{i=1}^n\) coincide exactly with solutions of the nonlinear complementarity problem for \(F\).

notation.meaning: residual induced by the complementarity function

children.title: Smoothed NCP Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Parameterized smooth approximations of complementarity equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Smoothed NCP Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard smooth Fischer-Burmeister approximation with positive smoothing parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable, and let \(\mu>0\). For \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}\), define \(\phi_\mu(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2+2\mu^2}-a-b\), and for \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), define \(\Phi_\mu(x)_i=\phi_\mu(x_i,F_i(x))\). Then \(\Phi_\mu\) is continuously differentiable, and \(\phi_\mu(a,b)=0\) holds exactly when \(a>0\), \(b>0\), and \(ab=\mu^2\). As \(\mu\downarrow0\), \(\phi_\mu\) converges locally uniformly on \(\mathbb{R}^2\) to \(\phi_0(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}-a-b\), and \(\Phi_\mu\) converges locally uniformly on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) to \(\Phi_0\). Moreover, \(\Phi_0(x)=0\) holds exactly when \(x\ge0\), \(F(x)\ge0\), and \(x_iF_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive smoothing parameter, the smoothed Fischer-Burmeister residual is continuously differentiable when the underlying mapping is continuously differentiable. Its scalar zeros are positive pairs with product equal to the squared smoothing parameter, and it converges locally uniformly to the exact nonlinear-complementarity residual as the parameter tends to zero.
assumptions_latex: The complementarity convention is \(x\ge0\), \(F(x)\ge0\), and \(x_iF_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: As \(\mu\downarrow0\), \(\Phi_\mu\to\Phi_0\) locally uniformly on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\Phi_0(x)=0\) is equivalent to the nonlinear complementarity conditions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Fischer-Burmeister residual \(\Phi\) is pointwise Fischer-Burmeister regular at a solution \(\bar x\) when every matrix \(V\in\partial_C\Phi(\bar x)\) is nonsingular. Equivalently, because \(\partial_C\Phi(\bar x)\) is compact, there exists \(\gamma>0\) such that \(\sigma_{\min}(V)\ge\gamma\) for every \(V\in\partial_C\Phi(\bar x)\). This condition concerns only Newton models admitted at \(\bar x\); it does not by itself quantify models selected at nearby points unless outer semicontinuity of the selected approximation family is also imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise Fischer-Burmeister regularity requires every generalized Jacobian matrix admitted at the solution to be invertible, uniformly over the compact pointwise matrix set.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Fischer-Burmeister Regularity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Nonsingularity of every Clarke generalized Jacobian matrix is a precise pointwise condition, but the supplied material does not establish that this condition is what the cited source calls Fischer-Burmeister regularity. That term has specialized uses in complementarity theory, so the mathematical identification cannot be accepted without inspecting the cited section.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The residual \(\Phi\) is sequentially Fischer-Burmeister regular at \(\bar x\) relative to \(\mathcal M\) when, for every sequence \(x^k\to\bar x\) and every selection \(V_k\in\mathcal M(x^k)\), there exist \(k_0\) and \(M<\infty\), possibly depending only on a fixed neighborhood but not on the selections, such that \(V_k\) is nonsingular and \(\|V_k^{-1}\|\le M\) for all \(k\ge k_0\). Equivalently, no such sequence can satisfy \(\sigma_{\min}(V_k)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential regularity rules out nearby sequences of admissible Fischer-Burmeister Newton matrices whose smallest singular values approach zero.

children.title: NCP Newton-Approximation Nonsingularity
children.top_down_role: Nonsingularity families for complementarity-specific Newton approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: NCP Newton-Approximation Nonsingularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform local nonsingularity condition for the nonempty Newton-approximation family used by an NCP method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be an NCP residual with \(\Phi(\bar x)=0\), and suppose \(\mathcal M(x)\subset\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonempty for every \(x\) in a neighborhood of \(\bar x\). The family \(\mathcal M\) is uniformly nonsingular at \(\bar x\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\gamma>0\) such that \(\sigma_{\min}(V)\ge\gamma\) for every \(x\in U\) and every \(V\in\mathcal M(x)\). With the Euclidean operator norm, this is equivalent to invertibility of every such \(V\) together with \(\sup\{\lVert V^{-1}\rVert:x\in U,\ V\in\mathcal M(x)\}\le\gamma^{-1}\). Consequently, for every \(x\in U\) and \(V\in\mathcal M(x)\), the Newton equation \(Vd=-\Phi(x)\) has a unique solution satisfying \(\lVert d\rVert\le\gamma^{-1}\lVert\Phi(x)\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty complementarity Newton family is uniformly nonsingular at a solution when every nearby approximation matrix has smallest singular value bounded away from zero. Equivalently, all nearby Newton equations have unique steps and uniformly bounded inverse operators.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is an NCP residual and \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(\Phi(\bar x)=0\).
\(\mathcal M(x)\subset\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonempty for every \(x\) near \(\bar x\).
Singular values and operator norms are induced by the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All Newton systems generated sufficiently near \(\bar x\) have unique solutions with uniformly bounded inverse operators.

notation.meaning: Nonempty family of complementarity-specific Newton approximations.
Smallest singular value of a matrix.

children.title: Strict-Complementarity Regime
children.top_down_role: Complementarity geometry under strict activity separation.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict complementarity holds exactly when no index has \(x_i=y_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional componentwise complementarity with no biactive indices.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A complementary pair \((x,y)\) lies in the strict-complementarity regime when \(x_i+y_i>0\) for every \(i\). Under \(x_i\ge0\), \(y_i\ge0\), and \(x_i y_i=0\), this is equivalent to the disjoint partition \(\{1,\ldots,n\}=I_x\mathbin{\dot\cup}I_y\), where \(I_x=\{i:x_i>0,\ y_i=0\}\) and \(I_y=\{i:x_i=0,\ y_i>0\}\). Thus each complementarity pair lies on exactly one smooth branch, and the active branch is locally stable under sufficiently small complementary perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity means every complementary pair has exactly one positive member, so there are no indices at which both members vanish.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Complementarity Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A complementary pair \((x,y)\) lies in the degenerate complementarity regime when its biactive set \(I_0=\{i:x_i=0,\ y_i=0\}\) is nonempty. At every \(i\in I_0\), both branches \(x_i=0\) and \(y_i=0\) meet, so the local complementarity set is not a single smooth manifold at that component. For Fischer-Burmeister and minimum-function reformulations, these are exactly the indices at which the scalar NCP function is evaluated at its nonsmooth junction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementarity is degenerate when at least one pair has both entries zero, where its two active branches meet.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The scalar complementarity set decomposes as \(K=K_a\cup K_b\cup\{(0,0)\}\), where \(K_a=\{(a,0):a>0\}\) and \(K_b=\{(0,b):b>0\}\). Each of \(K_a\) and \(K_b\) is a smooth one-dimensional stratum, while their closures intersect only at \((0,0)\). Hence a continuous path in \(K\) that changes from the branch with \(a>0\) to the branch with \(b>0\) must pass through \((0,0)\). For \(n\) pairs, regime transitions occur when at least one component enters its biactive stratum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two strict scalar complementarity branches meet only at the degenerate origin, so every branch change must pass through degeneracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsingularity-Loss Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral characterization of the boundary of the region where a nonempty complementarity Newton family is locally uniformly nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^q\), and let \(\mathcal M(z)\subset\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonempty for every \(z\in D\). Define \(m(z)=\inf_{V\in\mathcal M(z)}\sigma_{\min}(V)\) and the locally uniformly nonsingular region \(\mathcal R=\{z\in D:\text{there exist a relative neighborhood }U\text{ of }z\text{ and }\gamma>0\text{ such that }m(w)\ge\gamma\text{ for every }w\in U\}\). A point \(\bar z\in D\) lies on the relative boundary \(\partial_D\mathcal R\) only if it is approached by points of \(\mathcal R\) and there exist \(z^k\to\bar z\) in \(D\) and \(V_k\in\mathcal M(z^k)\) such that \(\sigma_{\min}(V_k)\to0\). Conversely, a point approached both by \(\mathcal R\) and by such a singular-value-collapse sequence lies in \(\partial_D\mathcal R\). Along the collapse sequence, either some \(V_k\) is singular, or, after restricting to invertible matrices, \(\lVert V_k^{-1}\rVert=1/\sigma_{\min}(V_k)\to\infty\). Degenerate complementarity indices may enlarge \(\mathcal M(z)\), but they do not alone imply singular-value collapse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The loss boundary separates parameters with a locally uniform singular-value margin from parameters admitting nearby Newton matrices whose smallest singular values collapse to zero. At collapse, matrices are singular or their inverse norms diverge; complementarity degeneracy alone does not force this behavior.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M(z)\subset\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonempty for every \(z\in D\).
Singular values and operator norms are induced by the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relative boundary \(\partial_D\mathcal R\) is characterized by approach from the locally uniformly nonsingular region together with nearby admissible matrices whose smallest singular values approach zero.

notation.meaning: Least singular-value margin of the approximation family.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: FB-Regular Point for a Mixed Complementarity Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise regularity defined through the reduced Jacobian and sign-restricted vectors associated with the Fischer–Burmeister merit formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A point (u,v)\in\mathbb{R}^{n_1+n_2} is FB regular for \operatorname{MiCP}(G,H), equivalently for \theta_{\mathrm{FB}}^{\mathrm{mcp}}, if J_uG(u,v) is nonsingular and, for every nonzero z\in\mathbb{R}^{n_2} satisfying z_{\mathcal C}=0,\ z_{\mathcal P}>0,\ z_{\mathcal N}<0, there exists a nonzero y\in\mathbb{R}^{n_2} satisfying y_{\mathcal C}=0,\ y_{\mathcal P}\ge0,\ y_{\mathcal N}\le0 and z^T\bigl(M(u,v)/J_uG(u,v)\bigr)y\ge0, where M(u,v)=\begin{bmatrix}JG(u,v)\\JH(u,v)\end{bmatrix} and M/J_uG is the Schur complement of J_uG in M.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is FB regular when its G block Jacobian is nonsingular and every nonzero vector with the prescribed strict signs admits a nonzero oppositely sign-restricted test vector whose pairing through the reduced Schur-complement Jacobian is nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: \forall z\ne0:\ z_{\mathcal C}=0,\ z_{\mathcal P}>0,\ z_{\mathcal N}<0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists y\ne0:\ y_{\mathcal C}=0,\ y_{\mathcal P}\ge0,\ y_{\mathcal N}\le0,\quad z^T\bigl(M(u,v)/J_uG(u,v)\bigr)y\ge0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semismoothness and Linear Newton Approximation of the MiCP Fischer–Burmeister Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity and Newton-facing representation of the Fischer–Burmeister residual and merit function for a mixed complementarity problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{n_1} and H:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{n_2} be continuously differentiable. Then \mathbf F_{\mathrm{FB}}^{\mathrm{mcp}} is semismooth and \theta_{\mathrm{FB}}^{\mathrm{mcp}} is continuously differentiable. If G and H have Lipschitz-continuous derivatives, then \mathbf F_{\mathrm{FB}}^{\mathrm{mcp}} is strongly semismooth. If g_{\mathrm{FB}} is a linear Newton approximation of \psi_{\mathrm{FB}}, then \mathcal A(u,v)=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}J_uG(u,v)&J_vG(u,v)\\D_bJ_uH(u,v)&D_a+D_bJ_vH(u,v)\end{pmatrix}\right\}, where the ith diagonal entries of D_a and D_b are respectively the two components of some \xi_i\in g_{\mathrm{FB}}(v_i,H_i(u,v)), is a linear Newton approximation scheme for \mathbf F_{\mathrm{FB}}^{\mathrm{mcp}}. If g_{\mathrm{FB}}(a,b)\subseteq\partial\psi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a,b), then \nabla\theta_{\mathrm{FB}}^{\mathrm{mcp}}(u,v)=A^T\mathbf F_{\mathrm{FB}}^{\mathrm{mcp}}(u,v) for every A\in\mathcal A(u,v).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For continuously differentiable MiCP data, the Fischer–Burmeister residual is semismooth and its merit function is continuously differentiable. Lipschitz-continuous derivatives give strong semismoothness. Scalar linear Newton approximations induce the displayed block approximation, and subgradient-contained choices yield the merit gradient by transposed residual multiplication.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ and }H\text{ have Lipschitz-continuous derivatives for strong semismoothness}
g_{\mathrm{FB}}\text{ is a linear Newton approximation of }\psi_{\mathrm{FB}}\text{ for the approximation scheme}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf F_{\mathrm{FB}}^{\mathrm{mcp}}\text{ is semismooth},\quad \theta_{\mathrm{FB}}^{\mathrm{mcp}}\in C^1,\quad \nabla\theta_{\mathrm{FB}}^{\mathrm{mcp}}(u,v)=A^T\mathbf F_{\mathrm{FB}}^{\mathrm{mcp}}(u,v)\ \forall A\in\mathcal A(u,v),\text{ with strong semismoothness under Lipschitz-continuous derivatives.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient Conditions for Nonsingularity of the MiCP Fischer–Burmeister Newton Scheme
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise block-Jacobian and Schur-complement conditions ensuring that every matrix in the linear Newton approximation is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{n_1} and H:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{n_2} be continuously differentiable, fix (u,v), and let \bar\alpha=\gamma\cup\beta\cup\delta. Suppose that for every \widetilde\gamma with \gamma\subseteq\widetilde\gamma\subseteq\gamma\cup\beta, the matrix \begin{pmatrix}J_uG&J_{v_{\widetilde\gamma}}G\\J_uH_{\widetilde\gamma}&J_{v_{\widetilde\gamma}}H_{\widetilde\gamma}\end{pmatrix} is nonsingular. Suppose also that the Schur complement of \begin{pmatrix}J_uG&J_{v_\gamma}G\\J_uH_\gamma&J_{v_\gamma}H_\gamma\end{pmatrix} in \begin{pmatrix}J_uG&J_{v_{\bar\alpha}}G\\J_uH_{\bar\alpha}&J_{v_{\bar\alpha}}H_{\bar\alpha}\end{pmatrix} is a P_0\text{-matrix}. Then every matrix in the linear Newton scheme \mathcal A(u,v) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed point, nonsingularity of all intermediate active-index block Jacobians, together with a P0 Schur-complement condition on the complementary block, guarantees nonsingularity of the Fischer–Burmeister linear Newton scheme.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ is nonsingular for every }A\in\mathcal A(u,v).
