knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Semismoothness of the Quadratic B-Function Box Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semismoothness transfer from the scalar quadratic B-function to a componentwise box-complementarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any scalars \tau<\tau', \phi_{\mathrm Q}(\tau,\tau';\cdot,\cdot) is a strongly semismooth B-function. Let F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n be continuously differentiable and let a,b\in\mathbb{R}^n satisfy a\le b. Define \bigl(\mathbf F_{\mathrm Q}^{\mathrm{box}}(x)\bigr)_i=\phi_{\mathrm Q}(a_i,b_i;x_i,F_i(x)) for i=1,\ldots,n. Then \mathbf F_{\mathrm Q}^{\mathrm{box}} is semismooth on \mathbb{R}^n. If JF is locally Lipschitz continuous, then \mathbf F_{\mathrm Q}^{\mathrm{box}} is strongly semismooth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic scalar B-function is strongly semismooth. Applying it componentwise to a continuously differentiable box-complementarity mapping produces a semismooth residual; a locally Lipschitz Jacobian of the underlying mapping gives strong semismoothness.
assumptions_latex: JF\text{ is locally Lipschitz continuous for the strong-semismoothness conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi_{\mathrm Q}\text{ is a strongly semismooth B-function};\quad \mathbf F_{\mathrm Q}^{\mathrm{box}}\text{ is semismooth, and is strongly semismooth if }JF\text{ is locally Lipschitz continuous}.

children.title: One-Sided Bounded Complementarity
children.top_down_role: Complementarity systems with finite lower or upper bounds only.

assumptions_latex: Each variable has either a finite lower bound only or a finite upper bound only.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each one-sided bound condition is equivalent to a scalar complementarity relation after an affine sign change.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise lower-only and upper-only bounded complementarity conditions.

source_refs.locator: 9.4.2 Mixed complementarity problems p. 866
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i\in L\) with finite lower bound \(\ell_i\), one-sided bounded complementarity is \(x_i-\ell_i\ge0\), \(F_i(x)\ge0\), and \((x_i-\ell_i)F_i(x)=0\). For \(i\in U\) with finite upper bound \(u_i\), it is \(u_i-x_i\ge0\), \(-F_i(x)\ge0\), and \((u_i-x_i)(-F_i(x))=0\). Thus both cases reduce to the standard nonnegative complementarity template by using the slack \(x_i-\ell_i\) or \(u_i-x_i\) and applying the corresponding sign to \(F_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower-only and upper-only bound conditions both become standard nonnegative complementarity after choosing the appropriate slack and residual sign.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Bounded Complementarity

children.title: Mixed Complementarity Problems
children.top_down_role: Systems combining free, bounded, and complementary variables.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A mixed complementarity solution enforces the residual sign dictated by whether each variable is lower-active, interior, or upper-active.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite-dimensional mixed complementarity problem with finite, infinite, or absent bounds.

source_refs.locator: 9.4.2 Mixed complementarity problems p. 866
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mixed complementarity problem \(\operatorname{MCP}(F,\ell,u)\) is to find \(x\in[\ell,u]\) such that, for every \(i\), \(F_i(x)\ge0\) if \(x_i=\ell_i\), \(F_i(x)=0\) if \(\ell_i<x_i<u_i\), and \(F_i(x)\le0\) if \(x_i=u_i\). Conditions involving an infinite endpoint are omitted. In particular, a free variable with \(\ell_i=-\infty\) and \(u_i=+\infty\) satisfies \(F_i(x)=0\), while one-sided variables reduce to lower- or upper-bound complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed complementarity problem combines equations for free or interior variables with signed residual conditions at finite lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Complementarity Problems

children.title: Box-Constrained Variational Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Projection and complementarity equations for box-constrained variational inequalities.

assumptions_latex: \(B=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty box, allowing infinite endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The box variational inequality is equivalent to a projection fixed-point equation and to componentwise mixed complementarity conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection representation of a finite-dimensional variational inequality over a box.

source_refs.locator: 9.4.2 Mixed complementarity problems p. 866
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in B\), the variational inequality \(\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\) for every \(y\in B\) holds if and only if \(x=P_B(x-\alpha F(x))\). Componentwise, this is equivalent to \(F_i(x)\ge0\) when \(x_i=\ell_i\), \(F_i(x)=0\) when \(\ell_i<x_i<u_i\), and \(F_i(x)\le0\) when \(x_i=u_i\), with nonexistent endpoint cases omitted. Therefore the residual \(R_\alpha(x)=x-P_B(x-\alpha F(x))\) vanishes exactly at the box-constrained variational-inequality solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box variational inequality is exactly a projected fixed point, equivalently a mixed complementarity system determined componentwise by active bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Box-Constrained Variational Inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Basic Newton Method for Variational Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semismooth Newton applied to an equation equivalent to a finite-dimensional variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an equation mapping \(H:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) whose zeros are exactly the solutions of the target variational inequality, choose \(z^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\). At iteration \(k\), stop and return \(z^k\) if \(H(z^k)=0\). Otherwise select \(V_k\in\partial H(z^k)\), solve \(V_kd^k=-H(z^k)\), and set \(z^{k+1}=z^k+d^k\). Here \(\partial H\) is a specified generalized Jacobian. If the linear system is singular or inconsistent, the basic method declares failure; damping or regularization belongs to a globalized variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply generalized Newton steps to a nonsmooth equation equivalent to the variational inequality, stopping at zero residual and declaring failure when the Newton system cannot be solved.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is locally Lipschitz and semismooth on a neighborhood of the iterates.
The chosen equation satisfies \(H(z)=0\) exactly when its associated point solves the variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^{k+1}=z^k-V_k^{-1}H(z^k)\) whenever \(V_k\) is nonsingular.

notation.meaning: Specified generalized Jacobian of the equation mapping at z.

knowledge_statements.title: Fischer-Burmeister KKT Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fischer–Burmeister reformulation for polyhedral variational inequalities in inequality form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax-b\geq0\}\), define \(s(x)=Ax-b\), and introduce \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Form \(H(x,\lambda)=(F(x)-A^{\mathsf T}\lambda,\Phi(\lambda,s(x)))\), where \(\Phi_i(\lambda,s)=\sqrt{\lambda_i^2+s_i^2}-\lambda_i-s_i\). Starting from \((x^0,\lambda^0)\), stop when \(H(x^k,\lambda^k)=0\); otherwise choose \(V_k\in\partial H(x^k,\lambda^k)\), solve \(V_k(d_x^k,d_\lambda^k)=-H(x^k,\lambda^k)\), and update \((x^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1})=(x^k,\lambda^k)+(d_x^k,d_\lambda^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode KKT complementarity with the Fischer–Burmeister function and apply a generalized Newton step to the resulting square nonsmooth system.
assumptions_latex: The KKT system characterizes the variational inequality on \(K\), for example under an applicable constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H(x,\lambda)=0\) implies \(F(x)-A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\), \(s(x)\geq0\), \(\lambda\geq0\), and \(\lambda_i s_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Function KKT Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-function reformulation for polyhedral variational inequalities in inequality form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax-b\geq0\}\), set \(s(x)=Ax-b\), and define \(H_{\min}(x,\lambda)=(F(x)-A^{\mathsf T}\lambda,M(\lambda,s(x)))\), with \(M_i(\lambda,s)=\min\{\lambda_i,s_i\}\). Choose \((x^0,\lambda^0)\). At iteration \(k\), return \((x^k,\lambda^k)\) when \(H_{\min}(x^k,\lambda^k)=0\); otherwise select \(V_k\in\partial H_{\min}(x^k,\lambda^k)\), solve \(V_kd^k=-H_{\min}(x^k,\lambda^k)\), and set \((x^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1})=(x^k,\lambda^k)+d^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent KKT complementarity by componentwise minima and apply generalized Newton iterations to the resulting piecewise-smooth equation.
assumptions_latex: The KKT conditions characterize the variational inequality on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_{\min}(x,\lambda)=0\) is equivalent to stationarity together with \(s(x)\geq0\), \(\lambda\geq0\), and \(\lambda_i s_i(x)=0\) for all \(i\).

children.title: Normal-Map VI Equations
children.top_down_role: Normal-map reductions of variational inequalities to nonsmooth equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Map VI Equations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean normal-map equation for a variational inequality on a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty closed convex set \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(P_K\) be the Euclidean projector and define the normal map \(F_K:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) by \[F_K(z)=F(P_Kz)+z-P_Kz.\] A point \(z\) satisfies \(F_K(z)=0\) if and only if \(x=P_Kz\) satisfies \[\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\qquad\text{for every }y\in K.\] Conversely, every solution \(x\) of this variational inequality generates the normal-map zero \(z=x-F(x)\), for which \(P_Kz=x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the normal-map variable onto the feasible set; zeros of the resulting equation correspond exactly to variational-inequality solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is defined at every projected point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_K(z)=0\iff x=P_Kz\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\).

children.title: Projected-Residual VI Equations
children.top_down_role: Projection-based residual equations for constrained variational systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Residual VI Equations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point residual equation using Euclidean projection and a positive stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau>0\), define the projected residual \[R_\tau(x)=x-P_K\bigl(x-\tau F(x)\bigr),\qquad x\in K.\] Then \(x\) solves the variational inequality \[\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\qquad\text{for every }y\in K\] if and only if \(R_\tau(x)=0\). Thus the constrained variational inequality is represented by a generally nonsmooth equation in the primal variable. The zero set is independent of the chosen positive value of \(\tau\), although conditioning and generalized derivatives may depend on it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point solves the variational inequality exactly when it is unchanged by projection after a positive forward step along negative F.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_\tau(x)=0\iff x\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\).

children.title: Regularized Gap Function
children.top_down_role: Regularized gap-function representation for variational inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Gap Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratically regularized primal gap for a finite-dimensional variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c>0\), define \[g_c(x)=\max_{y\in K}\left\{\langle F(x),x-y\rangle-\frac{c}{2}\lVert x-y\rVert^2\right\},\qquad x\in K.\] The maximizer is unique and equals \(y_c(x)=P_K(x-c^{-1}F(x))\). Moreover, \(g_c(x)\geq0\) for every \(x\in K\), and \[g_c(x)=0\iff x=y_c(x)\iff \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\quad\text{for every }y\in K.\] Hence \(g_c\) is an exact nonnegative merit function for the variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regularized gap maximizes linearized VI violation minus a quadratic penalty; it is nonnegative and vanishes exactly at VI solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_c(x)\geq0\) and \(g_c(x)=0\iff x\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\).

notation.meaning: Regularized gap function with parameter c.

children.title: Linearized Gap Function
children.top_down_role: Linearized gap-function representation for variational inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearized Gap Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unregularized primal gap obtained by maximizing the linearized variational-inequality residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the linearized gap function by \[g(x)=\max_{y\in K}\langle F(x),x-y\rangle,\qquad x\in K.\] Because \(y=x\) is admissible, \(g(x)\geq0\). Furthermore, \[g(x)=0\iff \langle F(x),x-y\rangle\leq0\quad\text{for every }y\in K\iff \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\quad\text{for every }y\in K.\] Thus its zeros are exactly the solutions of the variational inequality. Compactness of \(K\) ensures that the displayed maximum is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximal linearized VI violation is a nonnegative gap whose zeros are precisely the variational-inequality solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x)\geq0\) and \(g(x)=0\iff x\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\).

children.title: D-Gap Merit Function

knowledge_statements.title: D-Gap Merit Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Difference of two regularized gaps with distinct positive regularization parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<a<b\), let \(g_a\) and \(g_b\) be the regularized gap functions and define \[G_{a,b}(x)=g_a(x)-g_b(x),\qquad x\in K.\] If \(y_c(x)=P_K(x-c^{-1}F(x))\), then \[G_{a,b}(x)\geq\frac{b-a}{2}\lVert x-y_b(x)\rVert^2\geq0.\] Consequently, \[G_{a,b}(x)=0\iff x=y_b(x)\iff x\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(K,F).\] The D-gap therefore supplies a finite, exact merit function without requiring boundedness of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting two regularized gaps with increasing penalty parameters yields a nonnegative merit function that vanishes exactly at VI solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_{a,b}(x)\geq0\) and \(G_{a,b}(x)=0\iff x\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\).

children.title: Merit-Based VI Algorithms
children.top_down_role: Global algorithm families organized by variational-inequality merit functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Merit-Based VI Algorithms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo-globalized descent framework for an exact variational-inequality merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^0\in K\), parameters \(\beta\in(0,1)\), \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), and an exact merit function \(\Psi:K\to[0,\infty)\), repeat: if \(\Psi(x^k)=0\), return \(x^k\). Choose a feasible direction \(d^k\) satisfying \(\Psi^{\circ}(x^k;d^k)<0\). Select the smallest integer \(j_k\geq0\) such that \(x^k+\beta^{j_k}d^k\in K\) and \[\Psi(x^k+\beta^{j_k}d^k)\leq\Psi(x^k)+\sigma\beta^{j_k}\Psi^{\circ}(x^k;d^k).\] Set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\beta^{j_k}d^k\). If no acceptable step exists, declare globalization failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly choose a feasible merit-descent direction and use Armijo backtracking; stop when the exact VI merit function reaches zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\Psi\) is locally Lipschitz, nonnegative, and satisfies \(\Psi(x)=0\) exactly at variational-inequality solutions.
Each nonterminal iterate admits the stipulated feasible descent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted nonterminal step satisfies \(\Psi(x^{k+1})<\Psi(x^k)\), while termination at zero returns a variational-inequality solution.

notation.meaning: Clarke directional derivative of the merit function.

knowledge_statements.title: Active Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active constrained coordinates for mixed lower-bound and structurally free variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the coordinate set be the disjoint union \(\{1,\ldots,n\}=C\mathbin{\dot\cup}U\), where coordinates in \(C\) have lower bounds \(x_i\geq\ell_i\) and coordinates in \(U\) are structurally free. For a feasible point \(x\), its active partition is \[\mathcal A(x)=\{i\in C:x_i=\ell_i\}.\] These are precisely the constrained coordinates lying on their bounds. Together with the inactive constrained partition \(\mathcal I(x)=\{i\in C:x_i>\ell_i\}\) and the free partition \(\mathcal F=U\), it yields a disjoint partition of all coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active partition consists of bound-constrained coordinates currently equal to their lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i\in C:x_i=\ell_i\}\).

notation.meaning: Index set of structurally free coordinates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Sided Index Stability and Piecewise Analyticity for a P-Matrix LCS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local constancy of complementarity index partitions and finite-horizon regularity for the unique solution of the referenced initial-value linear complementarity system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D$ be a $P$-matrix, and let $(x(t),u(t))$ be the unique solution pair of the initial-value LCS (2.11). For every $t_*>0$, there exist $\varepsilon>0$ and index triples $(\alpha_{t_*}^-,\beta_{t_*}^-,\gamma_{t_*}^-)$ and $(\alpha_{t_*}^+,\beta_{t_*}^+,\gamma_{t_*}^+)$ such that $(\alpha(t),\beta(t),\gamma(t))=(\alpha_{t_*}^-,\beta_{t_*}^-,\gamma_{t_*}^-)$ for all $t\in[t_*-\varepsilon,t_*)$ and $(\alpha(t),\beta(t),\gamma(t))=(\alpha_{t_*}^+,\beta_{t_*}^+,\gamma_{t_*}^+)$ for all $t\in(t_*,t_*+\varepsilon]$. Consequently, for every $\mathcal T>0$, $x$ and $u$ are continuous and piecewise analytic on $[0,\mathcal T]$: there is a finite partition $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_N=\mathcal T$ such that both functions are analytic on every $(t_{i-1},t_i)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the unique solution of the referenced P-matrix linear complementarity system, the complementarity index partition is constant on sufficiently small punctured intervals immediately before and after every positive time. On each finite horizon, both solution components are continuous and analytic between finitely many partition times.
assumptions_latex: (x(t),u(t))\text{ is the unique solution pair of the initial-value LCS (2.11).}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall t_*>0\ \exists\varepsilon>0\text{ such that }(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\text{ is separately constant on }[t_*-\varepsilon,t_*)\text{ and }(t_*,t_*+\varepsilon];\quad \forall\mathcal T>0,\ x,u\text{ are continuous and piecewise analytic on }[0,\mathcal T]\text{ with a finite analytic partition.}

knowledge_statements.title: Inactive Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictly interior constrained coordinates for mixed lower-bound and structurally free variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) index coordinates with lower bounds \(x_i\geq\ell_i\), and let \(U\) index structurally free coordinates, with \(C\mathbin{\dot\cup}U=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). For a feasible point \(x\), its inactive partition is \[\mathcal I(x)=\{i\in C:x_i>\ell_i\}.\] Thus an inactive coordinate is constrained in the model but its bound is locally slack at \(x\). It is distinct from the free partition \(\mathcal F=U\), whose coordinates possess no such bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inactive partition contains constrained coordinates lying strictly above their lower bounds; structurally unconstrained coordinates are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I(x)=\{i\in C:x_i>\ell_i\}\).

children.title: Free Partition

knowledge_statements.title: Free Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structurally unbounded coordinates in a mixed bound-constrained variable partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\{1,\ldots,n\}=C\mathbin{\dot\cup}U\), where coordinates indexed by \(C\) obey lower bounds \(x_i\geq\ell_i\) and coordinates indexed by \(U\) have no corresponding bound. The free partition is \[\mathcal F=U.\] It is independent of the current feasible point. For every feasible \(x\), defining \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i\in C:x_i=\ell_i\}\) and \(\mathcal I(x)=\{i\in C:x_i>\ell_i\}\) gives \[\{1,\ldots,n\}=\mathcal A(x)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal I(x)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal F.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The free partition contains coordinates having no modeled bound and is independent of the current iterate.
assumptions_latex: Only coordinates in \(C\) carry the lower bounds \(x_i\geq\ell_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F=U\) and \(\mathcal A(x)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal I(x)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal F=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

notation.meaning: Index set of structurally unbounded coordinates.

children.title: Partition-Transition Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces where components change partition status.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Transition Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-index switching-score description of interfaces between active-set partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be a topological space, let \(m\in\mathbb N\), and let \(s_i:U\to\mathbb R\) be continuous for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Define \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i:s_i(x)>0\}\), \(\mathcal I(x)=\{i:s_i(x)<0\}\), and \(\Gamma_i=\{x\in U:s_i(x)=0\}\). The set \(\Gamma_i\) is the partition-transition interface for index \(i\). If a continuous path \(\gamma:[0,1]\to U\) satisfies \(s_i(\gamma(0))s_i(\gamma(1))<0\), then \(\gamma([0,1])\cap\Gamma_i\neq\varnothing\). Moreover, the complete sign partition is locally constant at every \(x\in U\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^m\Gamma_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many continuous switching scores, the transition interface for an index is its zero set. A path whose endpoint scores have opposite signs crosses that interface, and the complete sign partition is locally constant away from all interfaces.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is a topological space and \(m\in\mathbb N\).
For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), the switching score \(s_i:U\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Gamma_i=s_i^{-1}(0)\) is the interface across which index \(i\) may change partition, and the finite sign partition is locally constant away from \(\bigcup_{i=1}^m\Gamma_i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT degeneracy for smooth finite-dimensional inequality constraints inside active-set methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\leq0\) for \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT pair with \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb R_+^m\). Define \[\mathcal D(x^*,\lambda^*):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:g_i(x^*)=0\ \text{and}\ \lambda_i^*=0\}.\] Its elements are the degenerate active indices. The remaining indices comprise \(\mathcal A_+(x^*,\lambda^*)=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0,\ \lambda_i^*>0\}\) and \(\mathcal I(x^*)=\{i:g_i(x^*)<0\}\). Strict complementarity holds exactly when \(\mathcal D(x^*,\lambda^*)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite inequality-constrained problem, a degenerate index is an active constraint whose KKT multiplier is zero; strict complementarity holds exactly when no such index exists.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), define the problem \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\leq0\).
\((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a KKT pair with \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb R_+^m\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the parametric problem \(\min_{x\geq0}\tfrac12(x-t)^2\), the unique KKT solution is \[x^*(t)=\max\{t,0\},\qquad \lambda^*(t)=\max\{-t,0\}.\] For \(t<0\), the lower bound is active with positive multiplier; for \(t>0\), it is inactive; and at \(t=0\), both \(x^*(0)\) and \(\lambda^*(0)\) vanish. Consequently every neighborhood of \(t=0\) contains parameters with different active partitions. Thus strict-complementarity failure is a boundary at which finite or locally constant activity identification cannot be inferred from proximity alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projection solution max(t,0) changes activity across t=0, where both the variable and multiplier vanish; proximity alone therefore cannot identify a constant active set.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Identification Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT pair, and let \(I(x^*)=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\). If the Mangasarian--Fromovitz constraint qualification holds at \(x^*\), then the critical cone \(K(x^*,\lambda^*)=T_\Omega(x^*)\cap
abla f(x^*)^\perp\) has the representation \[K(x^*,\lambda^*)=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:
abla g_i(x^*)^	op d=0\ 	ext{when}\ \lambda_i^*>0,\quad 
abla g_i(x^*)^	op d\leq0\ 	ext{when}\ i\in I(x^*),\ \lambda_i^*=0\}.\] Thus positive-multiplier active constraints impose equalities on critical directions, whereas degenerate active constraints impose one-sided inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under MFCQ, positive-multiplier active constraints impose directional equalities in the critical cone, while zero-multiplier active constraints impose directional inequalities.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \((x^0,\lambda^0)\). At iteration \(k\), set \(\mathcal A_k=\{i:\lambda_i^k-cx_i^k>0\}\) and \(\mathcal I_k=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\mathcal A_k\). Impose \(x_{\mathcal A_k}^{k+1}=0\) and \(\lambda_{\mathcal I_k}^{k+1}=0\), solve the reduced system \[H_{\mathcal I_k\mathcal I_k}x_{\mathcal I_k}^{k+1}=q_{\mathcal I_k},\] and recover \(\lambda_{\mathcal A_k}^{k+1}=H_{\mathcal A_k\mathcal I_k}x_{\mathcal I_k}^{k+1}-q_{\mathcal A_k}\). Stop when the partition is unchanged and the KKT residual meets tolerance; otherwise repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify indices by a primal-dual switching score, solve only for inactive primal variables, recover active multipliers, and stop after partition stabilization and KKT convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Constraint Primal-Dual Active Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local bilateral-bound primal-dual active-set equations near a KKT point, where lower and upper switching tests do not conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\ell\leq x\leq u\), define \(L_i=\lambda_i^\ell-c(x_i-\ell_i)\) and \(U_i=\lambda_i^u-c(u_i-x_i)\). In a neighborhood where \(L_i\) and \(U_i\) are not simultaneously positive, set \(\mathcal A^\ell=\{i:L_i>0\}\), \(\mathcal A^u=\{i:U_i>0\}\), and \(\mathcal F=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus(\mathcal A^\ell\cup\mathcal A^u)\), using a fixed rule for zero-score ties. Solve \[x_i=\ell_i,\ \lambda_i^u=0\ \text{on}\ \mathcal A^\ell;\qquad x_i=u_i,\ \lambda_i^\ell=0\ \text{on}\ \mathcal A^u;\qquad \lambda_i^\ell=\lambda_i^u=0\ \text{on}\ \mathcal F,\] together with \(\nabla f(x)-\lambda^\ell+\lambda^u=0\). Update the partition and stop when it is unchanged and the KKT residual meets the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally, bilateral bounds define disjoint lower-active, upper-active, and free sets. The method fixes active variables, zeros the multiplier of the opposite bound, zeros both multipliers on free indices, and solves stationarity until the partition and KKT residual converge.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable, and \(\ell_i<u_i\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
The iteration is local to a neighborhood in which the lower and upper switching scores are not simultaneously positive for any index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The disjoint sets \(\mathcal A^\ell\), \(\mathcal A^u\), and \(\mathcal F\), together with the opposite-multiplier zero conditions, define the local bilateral-bound primal-dual active-set equations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-dual active-set iteration for bilateral PDE control bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specialized active-set algorithm for a bilaterally bound-constrained elliptic control problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given $(u_0,\lambda_0)$, $k_{\max}$, and $c>0$, define at iteration $k$ the sets
\[\mathcal A_k^L=\{x\in\Omega:\lambda_k(x)+c(u_k(x)-\underline u(x))<0\},\qquad \mathcal A_k^H=\{x\in\Omega:\lambda_k(x)+c(u_k(x)-\bar u(x))>0\},\]
with $\mathcal A_k=\mathcal A_k^L\cup\mathcal A_k^H$ and $\mathcal I_k=\Omega\setminus\mathcal A_k$. Solve
\[-\Delta y_k=f_k+g,\quad y_k=0,\qquad -\Delta p_k=-(y_k-z),\quad p_k=0,\]
where
\[f_k(x)=\begin{cases}\underline u(x),&x\in\mathcal A_k^L,\\ p_k(x)/v,&x\in\mathcal I_k,\\ \bar u(x),&x\in\mathcal A_k^H,\end{cases}\]
then set $\lambda_{k+1}=p_k-vu_k$ and increment $k$. Stop when the active set stabilizes or $k=k_{\max}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, classify points as lower-active, upper-active, or inactive using the multiplier and a positive classification parameter. Solve the coupled state-adjoint elliptic system with the control fixed at its appropriate bound on active regions and equal to the adjoint divided by v on the inactive region, update the multiplier, and stop when the active partition stabilizes or the iteration limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The iteration produces a primal-dual active-set approximation for the bilateral control constraints.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Componentwise complementarity satisfies \[a\geq0,\quad b\geq0,\quad a_i b_i=0\ \text{for all}\ i\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Phi_{\min}(a,b):=\min\{a,b\}=0.\] It is also equivalent to \[\Phi_{\max}(a,b):=a-\max\{0,a-b\}=0.\] If \(a_i\neq b_i\), both equations select the same differentiable branch and therefore the same active-set Newton row. When \(a_i=b_i\), both are nonsmooth and equivalence of a particular Newton step additionally requires compatible generalized-derivative selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative complementarity is equivalent to either a componentwise min equation or an associated max equation; their Newton branches agree away from ties.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the full Newton equations \[A\Delta u+B\Delta v=-r_u,\qquad C\Delta u+D\Delta v=-r_v.\] If \(D\) is nonsingular, then \(\Delta v=-D^{-1}(r_v+C\Delta u)\), and \(\Delta u\) is determined by the reduced system \[(A-BD^{-1}C)\Delta u=-r_u+BD^{-1}r_v.\] Conversely, every solution of this reduced system, followed by the displayed recovery formula, solves the full system. Thus exact elimination preserves the Newton step whenever the eliminated block and the Schur complement are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible Newton block can be eliminated exactly, producing a Schur-complement system whose solution reconstructs the same full Newton step.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block generalized-Newton system for finite-dimensional complementarity residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable and define \(H(x,\lambda)=(F(x)-\lambda,\min\{x,\lambda\})\), where the minimum is componentwise. For every \(i\), select \((\alpha_i,\beta_i)\in\partial_C\min(x_i,\lambda_i)\), and set \(D_x=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha_i)\) and \(D_\lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\beta_i)\). Thus \(\alpha_i,\beta_i\ge0\) and \(\alpha_i+\beta_i=1\), with \((\alpha_i,\beta_i)=(1,0)\) when \(x_i<\lambda_i\) and \((\alpha_i,\beta_i)=(0,1)\) when \(x_i>\lambda_i\). A full semismooth Newton step \((d_x,d_\lambda)\) solves \[\begin{pmatrix}F'(x)&-I\\D_x&D_\lambda\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}d_x\\d_\lambda\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}F(x)-\lambda\\\min\{x,\lambda\}\end{pmatrix}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full Newton formulation simultaneously updates primal and multiplier variables using a jointly selected generalized derivative of the componentwise minimum residual.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable near the current iterate.
A generalized-gradient pair is selected for every component of the minimum map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((d_x,d_\lambda)\) is the unique solution of the displayed full primal-dual Newton system whenever its block matrix is nonsingular.

notation.meaning: diagonal matrices formed from joint generalized-derivative selections for the minimum map

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic correspondence between pure-selection full and reduced Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the full system, choose a partition \(\mathcal A\cup\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) such that the minimum derivative selects \(x_i\) on \(\mathcal A\) and \(\lambda_i\) on \(\mathcal I\). Then \(d_{x,\mathcal A}=-x_{\mathcal A}\) and \(d_{\lambda,\mathcal I}=-\lambda_{\mathcal I}\). Substitution into the stationarity rows gives \[F'(x)_{\mathcal I\mathcal I}d_{x,\mathcal I}=-(F(x)-\lambda)_{\mathcal I}+d_{\lambda,\mathcal I}-F'(x)_{\mathcal I\mathcal A}d_{x,\mathcal A}.\] After solving this reduced system, recover \(d_{\lambda,\mathcal A}=(F(x)-\lambda)_{\mathcal A}+F'(x)_{\mathcal A,:}d_x\). Thus elimination and reconstruction reproduce the full step exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pure active/inactive derivative selections permit exact elimination of fixed primal and multiplier components; solving and reconstructing yields the same full Newton step.
assumptions_latex: \(D_x,D_\lambda\) make complementary zero-one selections on \(\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced solution and recovered variables equal the unique solution of the full Newton system.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence-Breakdown Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions limiting the pure-selection reduced-system representation and uniqueness of its Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The coordinate-fixing reduction based on a partition \(\mathcal A\cup\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) requires a pure minimum-derivative selection: \((D_x)_{ii}=1\) and \((D_\lambda)_{ii}=0\) on \(\mathcal A\), and the reverse on \(\mathcal I\). A fractional selection at a tied component \(x_i=\lambda_i\) replaces coordinate fixing by a linear relation between \(d_{x,i}\) and \(d_{\lambda,i}\), so that this particular active/inactive reduced system no longer represents the full system. Under a pure selection, elimination and reconstruction still give a bijection between the solution sets of the full and reduced systems. Nonsingularity of \(F'(x)_{\mathcal I\mathcal I}\) is additionally required for that corresponding step to be unique; if this block is singular, both formulations may be inconsistent or may admit multiple corresponding solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fractional tie selections invalidate the stated coordinate-fixing reduction, while a singular inactive Jacobian block removes unique solvability but not the pure-selection solution-set correspondence.
assumptions_latex: The complementarity residual is represented by the componentwise minimum map.
The reduced system is the active/inactive coordinate-elimination system associated with a pure derivative selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pure derivative selection is required for the stated coordinate reduction, and nonsingularity of \(F'(x)_{\mathcal I\mathcal I}\) is required for a unique corresponding Newton step.

knowledge_statements.title: Function-Space Active-Set Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise box-constraint equivalence for projection residuals on function spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=L^p(\Omega)\), let \(a,b\in L^\infty(\Omega)\) satisfy \(a<b\) almost everywhere, and let \(G:U\to U\). For \(c>0\), define \(R(u)=u-P_{[a,b]}(u-cG(u))\). With \(w=u-cG(u)\), set \(\mathcal A_a=\{w\le a\}\), \(\mathcal A_b=\{w\ge b\}\), and \(\mathcal I=\{a<w<b\}\), modulo null sets. A pointwise Newton derivative of the projection imposes \(u+d=a\) on \(\mathcal A_a\), \(u+d=b\) on \(\mathcal A_b\), and the linearized equation \(G(u)+G'(u)d=0\) on \(\mathcal I\). These are precisely the primal-dual active-set update equations for the same partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton derivative of the pointwise box projection produces the same bound fixing and inactive linearized equation as a function-space active-set update.
assumptions_latex: The projection superposition operator is Newton differentiable between the chosen function spaces.
\(G\) is Newton differentiable and the inactive linearized operator is invertible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection-residual Newton step and the primal-dual active-set step coincide almost everywhere for the same derivative selection.

children.title: Equivalence Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Representation and degeneracy regimes disrupting direct method identification.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation, regularity, and degeneracy boundaries for identifying active-set and semismooth-Newton iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Direct iteration-by-iteration identification requires the same complementarity representation, the same generalized-derivative selection at switching points, and unique solvability of the selected Newton system. Equivalence may fail if two algebraically equivalent residuals have different generalized Jacobians, if a tie admits incompatible selections, if the selected Newton matrix is singular, or if globalization modifies one step but not the other. In function spaces it may also fail when the pointwise max, min, or projection operator is not Newton differentiable in the asserted domain and codomain norms. Equality of solution sets alone therefore does not imply equality of generated iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent solution equations need not generate equivalent iterations when derivative selections, linear solvability, globalization, or function-space differentiability differ.
assumptions_latex: Two methods encode the same underlying complementarity conditions but may use different residuals or derivative selections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Method equivalence is confined to regimes with compatible representations, compatible selections, and well-posed Newton subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Complementary Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite identification by a convergent primal-dual sequence under a strict sign margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider lower-bound complementarity \(x\ge0\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(x_i\lambda_i=0\). Let \((x^k,\lambda^k)\to(x^*,\lambda^*)\), fix \(c>0\), and classify \(i\) as active when \(s_i^k=x_i^k-c\lambda_i^k\le0\). Suppose strict complementarity holds: for every \(i\), either \(x_i^*>0\) and \(\lambda_i^*=0\), or \(x_i^*=0\) and \(\lambda_i^*>0\). Then \(s_i^*\ne0\) for all \(i\). Hence there exists \(K\) such that, for every \(k\ge K\), the computed active set equals \(\{i:x_i^*=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence plus strict complementarity gives a nonzero classification margin, so the active set is identified after finitely many iterations.
assumptions_latex: Strict complementarity holds at every index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ \mathcal A_k=\{i:x_i^*=0\}\).

notation.meaning: indices classified active at iteration k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convergence preserves every strict limiting sign after finitely many iterations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Polyhedral Identification
children.top_down_role: Finite identification associated with piecewise-linear constraint geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite identification of the minimal active face under polyhedral nondegeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be polyhedral, let \(x^k\in C\) and \(v^k\in N_C(x^k)\), and suppose \((x^k,v^k)\to(x^*,v^*)\). Let \(F\) be the minimal face of \(C\) containing \(x^*\). If \(v^*\in\operatorname{ri}N_C(x^*)\), then the normal pair lies in the locally identifiable stratum associated with \(F\). Consequently, there exists \(K\) such that \(x^k\in\operatorname{ri}F\) for every \(k\ge K\); equivalently, the active inequalities defining the face stabilize finitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedral feasible set, convergence of primal-normal pairs and relative-interior nondegeneracy force finite identification of the limiting face.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty polyhedral convex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ x^k\in\operatorname{ri}F\).

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal cone to C at x
minimal face of C containing the limit point

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: polyhedral normal-cone strata are locally identifiable under relative-interior nondegeneracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The specialized claim that arbitrary convergent pairs in the graph of a polyhedral normal cone eventually enter the relative interior of the limiting minimal face requires an exact identifiable-stratum or polyhedral-normal-cone theorem locator.

children.title: Degenerate Activity Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Set stabilization when activity is not uniquely separated.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Activity Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient hysteresis condition for stabilizing classifications at degenerate indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_i^k=x_i^k-c\lambda_i^k\to s_i^*\), and let \(\tau_k>0\) satisfy \(\tau_k\to0\). Apply the hysteretic rule: declare inactive if \(s_i^k>\tau_k\), active if \(s_i^k<-\tau_k\), and otherwise retain the preceding classification. Suppose every degenerate index satisfies \(s_i^*=0\) and \(|s_i^k|\le\tau_k\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). Then every index with \(s_i^*\ne0\) eventually receives its limiting sign classification, and every degenerate index eventually retains a fixed classification. Thus the entire active set stabilizes after finitely many iterations, although its degenerate portion need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With thresholds tending to zero, hysteresis stabilizes degenerate indices that eventually remain inside the tie band, while separated indices acquire their limiting sign classification.
assumptions_latex: Every zero-limit score eventually remains within its hysteresis band.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ \mathcal A_{k+1}=\mathcal A_k\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: stabilization follows from threshold decay, convergence, retention, and eventual band containment

children.title: Activity Switching Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Persistent switching among competing activity patterns.

children.title: Active-Set Cycling
children.top_down_role: Repeated recurrence of previously visited activity patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact periodic recurrence of active-set states without termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal A_k)_{k\ge0}\) be the active-set sequence produced by an iterative method on a finite index set. The method exhibits active-set cycling from iteration \(K\) with period \(p\ge2\) if \[\mathcal A_{k+p}=\mathcal A_k\quad\text{for every }k\ge K,\] and no smaller positive integer has this property, while at least two sets among \(\mathcal A_K,\ldots,\mathcal A_{K+p-1}\) differ. Cycling is nonterminating when no state in this periodic orbit satisfies the method's stopping criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active-set cycling is a nonconstant periodic repetition of active sets, typically accompanied by failure to meet the stopping test.
assumptions_latex: The active-set sequence is indexed by iterations over a finite constraint index set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cycling is characterized by an eventual minimal period \(p\ge2\) and a nonconstant periodic orbit.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. Pivoting Methods p. 225

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 4. Pivoting Methods p. 225

children.title: Activity Chattering
children.top_down_role: Rapid local switching among closely competing activity classifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Activity Chattering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinitely repeated local switching without requiring an exact periodic orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an index \(i\), let \(a_i^k=1\) when \(i\in\mathcal A_k\) and \(a_i^k=0\) otherwise. Index \(i\) chatters if \[\#\{k\ge0:a_i^{k+1}\ne a_i^k\}=\infty.\] An active-set sequence chatters if at least one index chatters. Unlike cycling, chattering does not require any exact period or repetition of the complete iterate; it may occur when an activity score converges to zero while changing sign infinitely often.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chattering means that at least one constraint switches active status infinitely often, possibly without any periodic repetition of full active sets or iterates.
assumptions_latex: An infinite sequence of active-set classifications is generated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Activity chattering occurs exactly when some binary membership sequence has infinitely many transitions.

notation.meaning: binary activity indicator for index i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: infinite switching is the standard mathematical distinction between chattering and finite stabilization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Switching-Pattern Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Observable signatures used to distinguish persistent switching behaviors.

knowledge_statements.title: Switching-Pattern Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-history diagnostics for periodic cycling and near-boundary chattering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given active sets \(\mathcal A_0,\ldots,\mathcal A_K\), activity scores \(s^0,\ldots,s^K\), a window length \(m\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\), and maximum tested period \(p_{\max}\), compute \(W_i=\sum_{k=K-m}^{K-1}\mathbf1\{\mathbf1_{\mathcal A_{k+1}}(i)\ne\mathbf1_{\mathcal A_k}(i)\}\). Report a period-\(p\) cycle candidate if \(\mathcal A_{K-j}=\mathcal A_{K-j-p}\) for every \(0\le j<p\) and some \(2\le p\le\min\{p_{\max},\lfloor(K+1)/2\rfloor\}\). Report a chattering candidate at index \(i\) if \(W_i\ge2\) and \(\max_{K-m\le k\le K}|s_i^k|\le\varepsilon\). Otherwise report no switching pattern detected. These finite-history outputs are diagnostics, not proofs of future behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Count recent membership changes, compare two available consecutive active-set blocks for a possible cycle, and flag frequently switching indices whose scores remain near the activity boundary.
assumptions_latex: Active sets and compatible activity scores are recorded for all indicated history indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a cycle candidate, a set of chattering candidates, or no detected switching pattern.

notation.meaning: number of recent membership changes for index i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: transition counts and repeated-block tests operationalize the preceding definitions
diagnostic thresholds and decision rules require an algorithmic source

children.title: Stabilization-Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Degenerate or poorly separated regimes where activity patterns do not stabilize.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization-Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp sign-oscillation mechanism preventing finite active-set stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convergent activity score need not yield finite identification when its limit lies on the switching boundary. For one index, take \(s^k=(-1)^k/(k+1)\) and classify it as active exactly when \(s^k\le0\). Then \(s^k\to0\), but the classification changes at every iteration, so no \(K\) satisfies \(\mathcal A_{k+1}=\mathcal A_k\) for all \(k\ge K\). More generally, any index whose score crosses the decision boundary infinitely often prevents stabilization unless a tie-breaking, hysteresis, or comparable safeguarding rule suppresses those crossings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence to a degenerate boundary does not ensure identification: an activity score can approach zero while alternating sign and switching forever.
assumptions_latex: Activity is decided by the sign rule \(s^k\le0\).
No hysteresis or persistent tie-breaking rule is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence \(s^k=(-1)^k/(k+1)\) produces a nonstabilizing active-set classification despite \(s^k\to0\).

notation.meaning: scalar activity score for one constraint

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the explicit alternating sequence directly verifies the claimed failure mechanism

children.title: Globalized Active-Set Methods
children.top_down_role: Active-set families equipped with merit or continuation mechanisms.

children.title: Merit-Globalized Active Sets
children.top_down_role: Active-set methods globalized through complementarity or residual merit functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Merit-Globalized Active Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-merit line-search globalization for a finite-dimensional active-set Newton iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), select an active set and compute a generalized Newton direction \(d_k\) for \(F(x)=0\). Choose the first \(\alpha_k\in\{1,\beta,\beta^2,\ldots\}\), with fixed \(\beta\in(0,1)\), satisfying
\[
\Psi(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\leq \Psi(x_k)+\sigma\alpha_k\Psi'(x_k;d_k),\qquad \sigma\in(0,1).
\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), recompute the active set, and stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|_2\leq\varepsilon\). At every accepted nonterminal iteration, \(\Psi(x_{k+1})<\Psi(x_k)\). If an accumulation point \(\bar x\) is directionally stationary for \(\Psi\), and every directionally stationary point in the relevant level set is a root of \(F\), then \(F(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute an active-set Newton direction and backtrack until the residual merit satisfies the Armijo condition. Every accepted nonterminal step strictly decreases the merit. An accumulation point is a root only when it is directionally stationary and all such stationary points in the relevant level set are roots.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz, and the target system is \(F(x)=0\).
The merit function \(\Psi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|_2^2\) is directionally differentiable, and each accepted Newton or active-set direction \(d_k\) satisfies \(\Psi'(x_k;d_k)<0\) unless \(F(x_k)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every accepted nonterminal iteration, \(\Psi(x_{k+1})<\Psi(x_k)\). If an accumulation point \(\bar x\) is directionally stationary for \(\Psi\), and every directionally stationary point in the relevant level set is a root of \(F\), then \(F(\bar x)=0\).

notation.meaning: Complementarity or residual mapping whose zeros encode the active-set system.

children.title: Continuation Active Sets
children.top_down_role: Active-set methods embedded in regularization or penalty continuation.

assumptions_latex: For each \(\mu>0\), \(F_\mu:X\to Y\) is a regularized or penalized residual map between Banach spaces.
A schedule \(\mu_j\downarrow0\) and tolerances \(\tau_j\downarrow0\) is chosen so that approximate roots remain in the domain of the next-stage local solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a sequence \((x_j,\mu_j)\) satisfying \(\|F_{\mu_j}(x_j)\|_Y\le\tau_j\). If \(x_j\to\bar x\) and the consistency condition \(F_{\mu_j}(x_j)\to F_0(\bar x)\) holds, then \(F_0(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer continuation with an active-set semismooth Newton solve at each parameter value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(\mu_0>0\), an initial point \(x_{-1}\), and sequences \(\mu_j\downarrow0\) and \(\tau_j\downarrow0\). For \(j=0,1,\ldots\), initialize the active-set semismooth Newton solver for \(F_{\mu_j}(x)=0\) at \(x_{j-1}\), perform its active-set updates until
\[
\|F_{\mu_j}(x_j)\|_Y\le\tau_j,
\]
and warm-start the next stage with \(x_j\). Terminate when both \(\mu_j\le\varepsilon_\mu\) and \(\|F_{\mu_j}(x_j)\|_Y\le\varepsilon_F\). Consistency of \(F_\mu\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\) transfers convergent continuation sequences to roots of the limiting system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a sequence of regularized active-set systems, warm-starting each stage from the preceding solution while decreasing both the continuation parameter and inner tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuation Active Sets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the continuation leaf, but no source supports the continuation schedule, warm-start conditions, or limiting consistency claim.

children.title: Obstacle-Problem Active-Set Cross-Index
children.top_down_role: Navigation from active-set theory to obstacle-problem Newton and dual formulations.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a real Hilbert space, \(K=\{v\in V:v\ge\psi\}\), and \(A:V\to V^*\) defines the obstacle variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The obstacle variational inequality, its primal-dual complementarity system, and the projection equation have the same solutions under the stated identification of \(V\) and \(V^*\). Consequently, a semismooth Newton active-set partition is obtained from the sign of \(\lambda-c(u-\psi)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual complementarity representation underlying obstacle-problem active sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The variational inequality
\[
u\in K,\qquad \langle Au-f,v-u\rangle\ge0\quad\text{for every }v\in K
\]
is represented by
\[
Au-f-\lambda=0,
\qquad u-\psi\ge0,
\qquad \lambda\ge0,
\qquad \langle\lambda,u-\psi\rangle=0.
\]
Whenever the pointwise positive part is defined in the chosen function-space realization, complementarity is equivalently expressed, for any \(c>0\), as
\[
\lambda-[\lambda-c(u-\psi)]_+=0.
\]
The induced active set is \(\mathcal A_c=\{\lambda-c(u-\psi)>0\}\), with \(u=\psi\) imposed there and \(\lambda=0\) on its complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An obstacle variational inequality is equivalently a primal-dual complementarity system whose positive-part equation directly defines the active and inactive regions.
knowledge_statements.title: Obstacle-Problem Active-Set Cross-Index

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the obstacle cross-index, but its pointwise order, positive-part map, multiplier space, and identification of the Hilbert space with its dual require an obstacle-specific source and precise function-space hypotheses.

children.title: Contact-Problem Active-Set Cross-Index
children.top_down_role: Navigation from active-set theory to unilateral and complementarity contact systems.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a real Hilbert space, \(B:V\to Q\) is the normal-gap operator, and \(g(u)=Bu-b\) is constrained by \(g(u)\ge0\).
The equilibrium equation is \(Au-f-B^*\lambda=0\), with contact pressure \(\lambda\ge0\) paired with \(g(u)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unilateral contact conditions are equivalent to the positive-part residual equation, and its sign partition identifies contact and noncontact regions for a primal-dual active-set or semismooth Newton iteration.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complementarity representation for frictionless unilateral contact with a fixed sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With the convention that positive \(g(u)it\) means separation and positive \(\lambda\) means compressive pressure, unilateral contact is
\[
Au-f-B^*\lambda=0,
\qquad g(u)\ge0,
\qquad \lambda\ge0,
\qquad \langle\lambda,g(u)\rangle=0.
\]
For any \(c>0\), the complementarity conditions are represented pointwise by
\[
\lambda-[\lambda-cg(u)]_+=0.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal A_c=\{\lambda-cg(u)>0\}\) is the candidate contact set, where the Newton active-set step imposes \(g(u)=0\); on \(\mathcal I_c=\Omega\setminus\mathcal A_c\), it imposes \(\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Frictionless unilateral contact becomes a positive-part complementarity equation whose sign test divides the domain into contact and noncontact regions.
knowledge_statements.title: Contact-Problem Active-Set Cross-Index

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The contact representation is plausible but unsupported. The expression “\(g(u)it\)” is corrupted, the space containing \(\lambda\) is not introduced, and the mechanical sign convention and pointwise positive-part formulation require a contact-specific source.

children.title: Semismooth Operator Equations
children.top_down_role: Abstract Banach-space settings and method variants for semismooth operator equations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: NCP/MCP equation reformulation of a bound-constrained variational inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise residual construction on free, lower-bounded, upper-bounded, and doubly bounded regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi\) be an NCP-function and let \(\phi_{[\alpha,\beta]}\) be an MCP-function for every compact interval. Define \(\Omega^f=\Omega\setminus(\Omega_a\cup\Omega_b)\), \(\Omega^l=\Omega_a\setminus\Omega_b\), \(\Omega^u=\Omega_b\setminus\Omega_a\), and \(\Omega^{lu}=\Omega_a\cap\Omega_b\), and set
\[
\Phi(u)(\omega)=\begin{cases}
F(u)(\omega),&\omega\in\Omega^f,\\
\phi(u(\omega)-a(\omega),F(u)(\omega)),&\omega\in\Omega^l,\\
-\phi(b(\omega)-u(\omega),-F(u)(\omega)),&\omega\in\Omega^u,\\
\phi_{[a(\omega),b(\omega)]}(u(\omega),F(u)(\omega)),&\omega\in\Omega^{lu}.
\end{cases}
\]
Then \(u\in L^2(\Omega)\) solves the associated bound-constrained variational inequality if and only if \(\Phi(u)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the original residual on free points, NCP residuals on singly bounded points, and an interval MCP residual on doubly bounded points. The resulting equation is equivalent to the bound-constrained variational inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi_{[\alpha,\beta]}\) is an MCP-function for every compact interval \([\alpha,\beta]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u\text{ solves the bound-constrained variational inequality}\iff\Phi(u)=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized Differential and Semismoothness of the Discrete Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the equation reformulation and discrete objects defined in the source notation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\mathbf u^h\), let \(\partial^\circ\mathbf\Pi^h(\mathbf u^h)\) consist of the matrices \(\mathbf B^h\in\mathbb R^{m^h\times m^h}\) defined by (9.27). Then \(\partial_C\mathbf\Pi^h(\mathbf u^h)\subseteq\partial^\circ\mathbf\Pi^h(\mathbf u^h)\), with equality if, for example, \(\pi\) or \(-\pi\) is regular. If \(\pi\) is semismooth, then \(\mathbf\Pi^h\) is \(\partial^\circ\mathbf\Pi^h\)-semismooth and semismooth in the usual sense. If \(\pi\) is \(\alpha\)-order semismooth and \(j^h\), hence \(\mathbf j^h\), is twice continuously differentiable with \(\alpha\)-Hölder-continuous second derivative, then \(\mathbf\Pi^h\) is both \(\alpha\)-order \(\partial^\circ\mathbf\Pi^h\)-semismooth and \(\alpha\)-order semismooth in the usual sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The discrete generalized differential contains the Clarke generalized Jacobian and equals it under the stated regularity condition. Semismoothness, including alpha-order semismoothness under the stronger differentiability hypothesis, passes from pi to the discrete reformulation.
assumptions_latex: \(\partial^\circ\mathbf\Pi^h(\mathbf u^h)\) consists of the matrices defined by (9.27).
For order-\(\alpha\) inheritance, \(\pi\) is \(\alpha\)-order semismooth and \(j^h\) is twice continuously differentiable with \(\alpha\)-Hölder-continuous second derivative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_C\mathbf\Pi^h(\mathbf u^h)\subseteq\partial^\circ\mathbf\Pi^h(\mathbf u^h)\), with equality under the stated regularity; moreover, \(\mathbf\Pi^h\) inherits semismoothness and, under the stronger hypotheses, \(\alpha\)-order semismoothness.

children.title: Semismooth Operators in Banach Spaces
children.top_down_role: Operator-level semismoothness and generalized differential structures.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are Banach spaces, \(U\subset X\) is open, and \(F:U\to Y\).
\(\mathcal G:U\rightrightarrows\mathcal L(X,Y)\) has nonempty values near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed remainder condition defines semismoothness relative to \(\mathcal G\); replacing \(o(\|h\|_X)\) by \(O(\|h\|_X^{1+\gamma})\), with \(\gamma\in(0,1]\), defines semismoothness of order \(\gamma\).

notation.meaning: Space of bounded linear operators from X to Y.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton-type semismoothness relative to an operator-valued generalized differential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mapping \(F\) is semismooth at \(x\in U\) relative to \(\mathcal G\) if \(F\) is locally Lipschitz near \(x\), directionally differentiable at \(x\), and
\[
\sup_{G\in\mathcal G(x+h)}
\frac{\|F(x+h)-F(x)-Gh\|_Y}{\|h\|_X}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{as }h\to0,
\]
where the quotient is considered only for nonzero \(h\) with \(x+h\in U\). A single-valued selection \(G(x+h)\in\mathcal G(x+h)\) is a Newton derivative when the same limit holds for that selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Banach-space operator is semismooth when every nearby generalized derivative linearizes its increment with an error negligible relative to the perturbation norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Semismooth Operators in Banach Spaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is an appropriate definition for the leaf, but Banach-space semismoothness and Newton differentiability have materially different variants. A dedicated source must verify the simultaneous local-Lipschitz, directional-differentiability, and supremum-over-all-generalized-derivatives formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semismoothness and generalized differential of the pointwise residual operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Application-specific function-space semismoothness result for an operator composed from a reduced gradient and a pointwise mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the problem assumptions, Assumptions 5.10(a),(b), with $Z=\{0\}$ and $F=j'$, hold for every $p\in[2,\infty]$, every $p'\leq p$ with $p'\in[2,\infty]$ if $n=1$, $p'\in[2,\infty)$ if $n=2$, or $p'\in[2,2n/(n-2)]$ if $n\geq3$, and every $r\in[1,p']$. If $\pi$ satisfies Assumptions 5.10(c),(d), then $\Pi$ is $\partial^\circ\Pi$-semismooth. Moreover, $\partial^\circ\Pi(u)$ consists of all $M\in\mathcal L(L^p,L^r)$ of the form $M=d_1I+d_2j''(u)$, where $d=(d_1,d_2)\in L^\infty(\Omega)^2$ and $d(x)\in\partial\pi(u(x),j'(u)(x))$ almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated dimension-dependent exponents, the reduced gradient satisfies the required composition hypotheses. If the pointwise mapping satisfies the remaining hypotheses, the induced function-space operator is semismooth, with generalized differentials formed from bounded pointwise combinations of the identity and reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pi\text{ is }\partial^\circ\Pi\text{-semismooth and }\partial^\circ\Pi(u)=\{d_1I+d_2j''(u):d\in L^\infty(\Omega)^2,\ d\in\partial\pi(u,j'(u))\text{ a.e.}\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semismoothness and generalized differential of an induced function-space operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded theorem for the operator defined in (5.15), under Assumption 5.10.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under Assumption 5.10, let \(\Pi:Z\times L^p(\Omega)^m\to L^r(\Omega)^m\) be the operator defined in (5.15). Then \(\Pi\) is locally Lipschitz continuous and \(\partial_C^\circ\Pi\)-semismooth. Its generalized differential consists of the operators \(M\in\mathcal L(Z\times L^p(\Omega)^m,L^r(\Omega)^m)\) satisfying \[M(v,w)=D_1w+D_2\bigl(F'(z,u)(v,w)\bigr),\] where \(D_i\in L^\infty(\Omega)^{m\times m}\) and \(D=(D_1\mid D_2)\) satisfies \[D(\omega)\in\partial_C\pi\bigl(u(\omega),F(z,u)(\omega)\bigr)\quad(\omega\in\Omega).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumption 5.10, the induced function-space operator is locally Lipschitz and semismooth. Its generalized differential consists of operators formed from the derivative of F and pointwise Clarke generalized derivatives of pi.
assumptions_latex: F:Z\times L^p(\Omega)^m\to L^r(\Omega)^m\text{ is continuously Fréchet differentiable}.
(z,u)\mapsto F(z,u)\in L^{p'}(\Omega)^m\text{ is locally Lipschitz continuous}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pi\text{ is locally Lipschitz and }\partial_C^\circ\Pi\text{-semismooth, and }\partial_C^\circ\Pi\text{ consists of the stated operators }M.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Convergence Rates of the Generalized Newton Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional local-rate theorem whose numbered approximation hypotheses are referenced but not expanded in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G:X\to Y$, with $X,Y$ Banach spaces, and let $(x^k)$ be generated by $M_k s^k=-G(x^k)$ and $x^{k+1}=x^k+s^k$. If $x^0$ is sufficiently close to a solution $\bar x$, then: (i) under condition (2.13), $x^k\to\bar x$ q-linearly with rate $\gamma$; (ii) under (2.14), or under (2.16) and (2.17), the convergence is q-superlinear; (iii) under (2.15), or under (2.16) and (2.18), the convergence has q-order $1+\alpha$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a generalized Newton sequence started sufficiently near a solution, condition (2.13) gives q-linear convergence with rate gamma; condition (2.14), or conditions (2.16) and (2.17), gives q-superlinear convergence; and condition (2.15), or conditions (2.16) and (2.18), gives convergence of q-order 1 plus alpha.
assumptions_latex: x^0\text{ is sufficiently close to }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{cases}(2.13)\Rightarrow x^k\to\bar x\text{ q-linearly with rate }\gamma,\\(2.14)\ \text{or}\ ((2.16)\wedge(2.17))\Rightarrow x^k\to\bar x\text{ q-superlinearly},\\(2.15)\ \text{or}\ ((2.16)\wedge(2.18))\Rightarrow x^k\to\bar x\text{ with q-order }1+\alpha.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong–Weak Closedness of the Generalized-Differential Graph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential closedness, and under separability net-based closedness, with strong convergence in the argument space and weak convergence in the operator space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose Assumption 3.32 holds. Let \((y_k)\subset Y\) and \((M_k)\subset\mathcal L(Y,L^r(\Omega))\) satisfy \(M_k\in\partial^\circ\Psi(y_k)\) for every \(k\), \(y_k\to y^*\) in \(Y\), and \(M_k\rightharpoonup M^*\) in \(\mathcal L(Y,L^r(\Omega))\). Then \(M^*\in\partial^\circ\Psi(y^*)\). If \(Y\) is separable, the same implication holds when the two sequences are replaced by nets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumption 3.32, if points converge strongly in Y and corresponding generalized-differential operators converge weakly in the operator space, then the limit operator belongs to the generalized differential at the limit point. If Y is separable, the same assertion holds for nets.
assumptions_latex: Y\text{ is separable for the extension from sequences to nets.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M^*\in\partial^\circ\Psi(y^*);\qquad Y\text{ separable}\Rightarrow\text{the analogous strong--weak implication holds for nets.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Superlinear Convergence of Newton's Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth specialization of generalized Newton iteration for Banach-space operator equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G:X\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable between Banach spaces, let $G(\bar x)=0$, and suppose $G'(\bar x)$ is continuously invertible. Then, for $x^0$ sufficiently close to $\bar x$, Newton's iteration $G'(x^k)s^k=-G(x^k)$, $x^{k+1}=x^k+s^k$, converges q-superlinearly to $\bar x$. If additionally $G'$ is Hölder continuous of order $\alpha$ near $\bar x$, the q-order is $1+\alpha$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an operator is continuously Fréchet differentiable and its derivative at a solution has a continuous inverse, Newton's method converges locally q-superlinearly. If the derivative is also Hölder continuous of order alpha near the solution, the convergence order is 1 plus alpha.
assumptions_latex: G:X\to Y\text{ is continuously Fréchet differentiable}
x^0\text{ is sufficiently close to }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^k\to\bar x\text{ q-superlinearly};\qquad G'\in C^{0,\alpha}\text{ near }\bar x\Rightarrow \operatorname{ord}_q(x^k)=1+\alpha.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized Newton Method

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_k s^k=-G(x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=x^k+s^k\quad(k=0,1,2,\ldots).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity conditions for an induced semismooth operator construction on L^p spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exists \(r\in[1,p)\cap[1,p')\) such that \(F:L^p(\Omega)\to L^r(\Omega)\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable, \(F:L^p(\Omega)\to L^{p'}(\Omega)\) is locally Lipschitz continuous, and \(\phi:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\) is Lipschitz continuous and semismooth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For some r strictly below both p and its conjugate exponent p′, F is continuously Fréchet differentiable into L^r and locally Lipschitz into L^{p′}, while φ is Lipschitz and semismooth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\in C^1\!\left(L^p(\Omega),L^r(\Omega)\right),\quad F:L^p(\Omega)\to L^{p'}(\Omega)\text{ is locally Lipschitz},\quad \phi:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\text{ is Lipschitz and semismooth}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity assumptions on G and ψ
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-space assumptions used for an induced semismooth operator construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exist exponents \(1\le r\le r_i<q_i\le\infty\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), such that: \(G:Y\to\prod_{i=1}^mL^{r_i}(\Omega)\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable; for every \(y\in Y\), there are an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(y\) and a constant \(L_G(U)\) such that \(\sum_{i=1}^m\|G_i(y_1)-G_i(y_2)\|_{L^{q_i}}\le L_G(U)\|y_1-y_2\|_Y\) for all \(y_1,y_2\in U\); and \(\psi:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is semismooth and satisfies \(|\psi(x_1)-\psi(x_2)|\le L_\psi\|x_1-x_2\|_1\) for all \(x_1,x_2\in\mathbb R^m\), with \(L_\psi>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For suitable exponents, G is continuously Fréchet differentiable into the product of the L^{r_i} spaces and locally Lipschitz into the product of the L^{q_i} spaces, while ψ is globally Lipschitz in the 1-norm and semismooth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\in C^1\!\left(Y,\prod_iL^{r_i}(\Omega)\right),\quad G:Y\to\prod_iL^{q_i}(\Omega)\text{ is locally Lipschitz},\quad \psi\text{ is globally Lipschitz and semismooth}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent generalized-Jacobian characterizations of semismoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The residual limsup expressions are norm estimates; the source's displayed vector numerators are interpreted accordingly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G:\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R^m\), with \(\Omega\) open, be B-differentiable near \( ar x\in\Omega\). The following are equivalent: (i) \(G\) is semismooth at \( ar x\); (ii) \[\lim_{\substack{x	o ar x,\,x
e ar x\H\in\partial G(x)}} rac{\|G'( ar x;x- ar x)-H(x- ar x)\|}{\|x- ar x\|}=0;\] (iii) \[\lim_{\substack{x	o ar x,\,x
e ar x\H\in\partial G(x)}} rac{\|G(x)+H( ar x-x)-G( ar x)\|}{\|x- ar x\|}=0.\] If \(G\) is strongly semismooth at \( ar x\), then \[\limsup_{x	o ar x,\,x
e ar x} rac{\|G(x)-G( ar x)-G'( ar x;x- ar x)\|}{\|x- ar x\|^2}<\infty\] and \[\limsup_{\substack{x	o ar x,\,x
e ar x\H\in\partial G(x)}} rac{\|G(x)+H( ar x-x)-G( ar x)\|}{\|x- ar x\|^2}<\infty.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a map that is B-differentiable near the reference point, semismoothness is equivalent both to first-order agreement between its directional derivative and every nearby generalized Jacobian and to a vanishing normalized generalized-Jacobian linearization residual. Strong semismoothness gives quadratic-order bounds for the directional and generalized-Jacobian residuals.
assumptions_latex: G:\Omega\to\mathbb R^m\text{ is B-differentiable near }\bar x\in\Omega
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Semismoothness is equivalent to the two first-order residual limits, and strong semismoothness implies both quadratic residual bounds.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Semismooth Remainder Implies Discrete-Gradient Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the unit sphere \(S_1\), source-defined set \(D_0\), and source-defined subdifferential \(\partial f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be semismooth at \(\mathbf x\), and define \(o(\lambda,\mathbf g)=f(\mathbf x+\lambda\mathbf g)-f(\mathbf x)-\lambda f'(\mathbf x;\mathbf g)\) for \(\lambda>0\) and \(\mathbf g\in S_1\). If \(\lambda^{-1}o(\lambda,\mathbf g)\to0\) uniformly in \(\mathbf g\) as \(\lambda\downarrow0\), then for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists \(\lambda_0>0\) such that \(D_0(\mathbf x,\lambda)\subseteq\partial f(\mathbf x)+B(\mathbf0;\varepsilon)\) for all \(\lambda\in(0,\lambda_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a function is semismooth at x and its directional first-order remainder is uniformly little-o of the step length over unit directions, then every sufficiently small-scale discrete gradient lies within any prescribed neighborhood of the subdifferential at x.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\text{ is semismooth at }\mathbf x
o(\lambda,\mathbf g)=f(\mathbf x+\lambda\mathbf g)-f(\mathbf x)-\lambda f'(\mathbf x;\mathbf g)
\lambda^{-1}o(\lambda,\mathbf g)\to0\text{ uniformly for }\mathbf g\in S_1\text{ as }\lambda\downarrow0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\varepsilon>0\;\exists\lambda_0>0\;\forall\lambda\in(0,\lambda_0),\quad D_0(\mathbf x,\lambda)\subseteq\partial f(\mathbf x)+B(\mathbf0;\varepsilon).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Product, Sum, and Composition Calculus for Semismooth Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure rules for generalized-differential semismoothness between Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $X,Y,Z,Y_1,Y_2$ be Banach spaces. (a) If $G_i:X\to Y_i$ is $\partial G_i$-semismooth at $x$ for $i=1,2$, then $(G_1,G_2):X\to Y_1\times Y_2$ is semismooth at $x$ relative to the product differential formed from $\partial G_1$ and $\partial G_2$. (b) If $G_i:X\to Y$ is $\partial G_i$-semismooth at $x$ for $i=1,2$, then $G_1+G_2$ is $(\partial G_1+\partial G_2)$-semismooth at $x$. (c) Let $G_1:Y\to Z$ be $\partial G_1$-semismooth at $G_2(x)$ and $G_2:X\to Y$ be $\partial G_2$-semismooth at $x$. If $\partial G_1$ is bounded near $G_2(x)$ and $G_2$ is Lipschitz continuous near $x$, then $G_1\circ G_2$ is $\partial G$-semismooth at $x$, where
\[
\partial G(x)=\{M_1M_2:M_1\in\partial G_1(G_2(x)),\ M_2\in\partial G_2(x)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semismooth operators are closed under paired products and sums. They are also closed under composition when the outer generalized differential is locally bounded and the inner operator is locally Lipschitz; the composite models are products of outer and inner model operators.
assumptions_latex: G_i:X\to Y_i\text{ is }\partial G_i\text{-semismooth at }x\ (i=1,2)\text{ in (a)}
G_i:X\to Y\text{ is }\partial G_i\text{-semismooth at }x\ (i=1,2)\text{ in (b)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (G_1,G_2)\text{ and }G_1+G_2\text{ are semismooth relative to their product and sum differentials, respectively};\quad G_1\circ G_2\text{ is }\partial G\text{-semismooth at }x,\ \partial G(x)=\{M_1M_2:M_1\in\partial G_1(G_2(x)),\ M_2\in\partial G_2(x)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuous Fréchet Differentiability Implies Semismoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding of classically smooth Banach-space operators into generalized-differential semismoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X,Y$ be Banach spaces and let $G:X\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable near $x$. Define the singleton-valued generalized differential by $\{G'\}(z)=\{G'(z)\}$. Then $G$ is $\{G'\}$-semismooth at $x$. If, additionally, $G'$ is Hölder continuous of order $\alpha>0$ near $x$, then $G$ is $\{G'\}$-semismooth of order $\alpha$ at $x$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuously Fréchet differentiable operator is semismooth relative to its singleton derivative. Hölder continuity of the derivative of order alpha yields semismoothness of order alpha.
assumptions_latex: G:X\to Y\text{ is continuously Fréchet differentiable near }x
G'\text{ is Hölder continuous of order }\alpha>0\text{ near }x\text{ for the second conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is }\{G'\}\text{-semismooth at }x;\qquad G'\in C^{0,\alpha}\text{ near }x\Longrightarrow G\text{ is }\{G'\}\text{-semismooth of order }\alpha\text{ at }x.
