knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semismoothness of a Reduced-Gradient Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-space semismoothness of an operator composed from a pointwise mapping and a PDE reduced gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that the operator \(y\in H_0^1(\Omega)\mapsto\varphi(y)\in H^{-1}(\Omega)\) is three times continuously differentiable. Then \(F=j'\) satisfies Assumptions 5.12(a),(b) with \(Z=\{0\}\), \(\alpha=1\), and \(r=2\), for every \(p\in(2,\infty]\) and every \(p'\le p\) such that \(p'\in(2,\infty]\) if \(n=1\), \(p'\in(2,\infty)\) if \(n=2\), and \(p'\in(2,2n/(n-2)]\) if \(n\ge3\). If additionally \(\pi\) satisfies Assumptions 5.12(c),(d), then \(\Pi(u)=\pi(u,j'(u))\) is \(\beta\)-order \(\partial^\circ\Pi\)-semismooth, where \(\beta\) is given by Theorem 3.50, and \(\partial^\circ\Pi(u)\) consists of all \(M\in\mathcal L(L^p,L^2)\) having the form specified in (9.13).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three-times continuous differentiability of the state operator implies the required reduced-gradient regularity over the stated dimension-dependent exponent ranges. If the remaining assumptions on pi hold, the composition Pi is beta-order semismooth and has the generalized differential described by formula (9.13).
assumptions_latex: y\in H_0^1(\Omega)\mapsto\varphi(y)\in H^{-1}(\Omega)\text{ is three times continuously differentiable}
\pi\text{ satisfies Assumptions 5.12(c),(d) for the semismoothness conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F=j'\text{ satisfies Assumptions 5.12(a),(b) with }Z=\{0\},\ \alpha=1;\quad \Pi(u)=\pi(u,j'(u))\text{ is }\beta\text{-order }\partial^\circ\Pi\text{-semismooth, with }\partial^\circ\Pi(u)\text{ given by (9.13).}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semismoothness Relative to a Generalized Differential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semismoothness of continuous operators between Banach spaces relative to a nonempty family of bounded linear models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $X,Y$ be Banach spaces, let $G:X\to Y$ be continuous, and let $\partial G:X\rightrightarrows\mathcal L(X,Y)$ have nonempty values. The operator $G$ is $\partial G$-semismooth at $x\in X$ if
\[
\sup_{M\in\partial G(x+d)}\lVert G(x+d)-G(x)-Md\rVert_Y=o(\lVert d\rVert_X)
\quad\text{as }\lVert d\rVert_X\to0.
\]
For $\alpha>0$, $G$ is $\partial G$-semismooth of order $\alpha$ at $x$ if
\[
\sup_{M\in\partial G(x+d)}\lVert G(x+d)-G(x)-Md\rVert_Y=O(\lVert d\rVert_X^{1+\alpha})
\quad\text{as }\lVert d\rVert_X\to0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous operator is semismooth relative to a generalized differential at x when the worst linearization remainder over models selected at x+d is little-o of the size of d. It is semismooth of order alpha when that remainder is of order the size of d raised to 1+alpha.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is }\partial G\text{-semismooth at }x\iff \sup_{M\in\partial G(x+d)}\lVert G(x+d)-G(x)-Md\rVert_Y=o(\lVert d\rVert_X),\quad G\text{ is of order }\alpha\iff \sup_{M\in\partial G(x+d)}\lVert G(x+d)-G(x)-Md\rVert_Y=O(\lVert d\rVert_X^{1+\alpha}).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semismoothness of composite superposition operators with an integrability gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions for function-space semismoothness when the inner map is locally Lipschitz into a strictly stronger Lebesgue space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) be measurable with \(0<|\Omega|<\infty\), let \(\psi:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) be Lipschitz continuous and semismooth, let \(Y\) be a Banach space, and let \(1\le q<p\le\infty\). is \(\partial\Psi_G\)-semismooth, where \(\partial\Psi_G\) is the pointwise-selection differential defined for the composite operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lipschitz semismooth finite-dimensional function composed pointwise with a continuously differentiable Banach-space map is semismooth into Lq when the inner map is locally Lipschitz into a strictly stronger Lp space.

G:Y\to L^q(\Omega)^m\text{ is continuously Fréchet differentiable}
G\text{ maps }Y\text{ locally Lipschitz continuously into }L^p(\Omega)^m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Psi_G\text{ is }\partial\Psi_G\text{-semismooth}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cartesian-product rule for semismooth mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of generalized-differential semismoothness, including its order, under finite vector assembly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\subset Y\) be open, \(\bar y\in V\), and let \(f_i:V\to Z_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be respectively semismooth (or \(\alpha\)-order semismooth) at \(\bar y\) relative to \(\partial^*f_i:V\rightrightarrows\mathcal L(Y,Z_i)\). Put \(Z=\prod_{i=1}^mZ_i\), \(f=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)\), and let \((\prod_i\partial^*f_i)(u)\) consist of the operators \(M:v\mapsto(M_1v,\ldots,M_mv)\) with \(M_i\in\partial^*f_i(u)\). If \(\varnothing\ne\partial^*f(u)\subset(\prod_i\partial^*f_i)(u)\) for every \(u\in V\), then \(f\) is respectively semismooth (or \(\alpha\)-order semismooth) at \(\bar y\) relative to \(\partial^*f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mapping formed by finitely many semismooth components is semismooth, with the same available order, for any nonempty generalized differential contained pointwise in the product of the component generalized differentials.
assumptions_latex: V\subset Y\text{ is open},\quad \bar y\in V
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f=(f_1,\ldots,f_m):V\to\prod_{i=1}^mZ_i\text{ is }(\alpha\text{-order})\ \partial^*f\text{-semismooth at }\bar y.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth mappings are semismooth relative to their derivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous or Hölder continuity of the derivative yields semismoothness relative to its singleton-valued representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:V\subset Y\to Z\) be differentiable on a neighborhood \(V\) of \(y\). If \(f'\) is continuous near \(y\), then \(f\) is \(\{f'\}\)-semismooth at \(y\). If \(f'\) is \(\alpha\)-Hölder continuous near \(y\), where \(0<\alpha\le 1\), then \(f\) is \(\alpha\)-order \(\{f'\}\)-semismooth at \(y\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f'\text{ continuous near }y\Rightarrow f\text{ is }\{f'\}\text{-semismooth at }y;\qquad 0<\alpha\le1,\ f'\text{ \(\alpha\)-Hölder near }y\Rightarrow f\text{ is \(\alpha\)-order }\{f'\}\text{-semismooth at }y.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composition rule for semismooth mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chain rule preserving generalized-differential semismoothness and its order under local Lipschitz and boundedness conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\subset X\) and \(V\subset Y\) be open, \(\bar x\in U\), and \(\bar y=f_1(\bar x)\). Suppose \(f_1:U\to Y\) is Lipschitz continuous near \(\bar x\) and respectively semismooth (or \(\alpha\)-order semismooth) there relative to \(\partial^*f_1\); \(f_2:V\to Z\) is respectively semismooth (or \(\alpha\)-order semismooth) at \(\bar y\) relative to \(\partial^*f_2\); \(\partial^*f_2\) is bounded near \(\bar y\); and \(f_1(U)\subset V\). Define \(f=f_2\circ f_1\) and \((\partial^*f_2\circ\partial^*f_1)(u)=\{M_2M_1:M_1\in\partial^*f_1(u),\ M_2\in\partial^*f_2(f_1(u))\}\). If \(\varnothing\ne\partial^*f(u)\subset(\partial^*f_2\circ\partial^*f_1)(u)\) for every \(u\in U\), then \(f\) is respectively semismooth (or \(\alpha\)-order semismooth) at \(\bar x\) relative to \(\partial^*f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composition of semismooth mappings is semismooth, with the same available order, when the inner mapping is locally Lipschitz, the outer generalized differential is locally bounded, the range condition holds, and the chosen generalized differential is contained pointwise in the products of component generalized differentials.
assumptions_latex: U\subset X,\ V\subset Y\text{ are open},\quad \bar x\in U,\quad \bar y=f_1(\bar x)
f_1:U\to Y\text{ is Lipschitz near }\bar x\text{ and }(\alpha\text{-order})\ \partial^*f_1\text{-semismooth at }\bar x
\partial^*f_2\text{ is bounded near }\bar y,\quad f_1(U)\subset V
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_2\circ f_1\text{ is }(\alpha\text{-order})\ \partial^*f\text{-semismooth at }\bar x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal and mixed coderivative chain rules for a linear-operator composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coderivative formulas for \((f\circ G)(x)=\{f(x,y):y\in G(x)\}\), including the condition upgrading the normal inclusion to equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G:X\rightrightarrows Y\) and \(f:X\times Y\to Z\) act between Banach spaces, and define \((f\circ G)(x)=\bigcup_{y\in G(x)}\{f(x,y)\}\). Suppose near \(\bar x\) that \(f(x,\cdot)\in\mathcal L(Y,Z)\), that \(f(\bar x,\cdot)\) is injective with closed range, and that \(x\mapsto f(x,\cdot)\) is strictly differentiable at \(\bar x\). For \(\bar y\in G(\bar x)\), set \(\bar z=f(\bar x,\bar y)\). Then, for every \(z^*\in Z^*\),
\[D_M^*(f\circ G)(\bar x,\bar z)(z^*)=\nabla_x f(\bar x,\bar y)^*z^*+D_M^*G(\bar x,\bar y)\big(f(\bar x,\cdot)^*z^*\big),\]
\[D_N^*(f\circ G)(\bar x,\bar z)(z^*)\subset\nabla_x f(\bar x,\bar y)^*z^*+D_N^*G(\bar x,\bar y)\big(f(\bar x,\cdot)^*z^*\big).\]
If \(\operatorname{rge}f(\bar x,\cdot)\) is weak-star-extensible in \(Z\), the latter inclusion is an equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a set-valued mapping followed by an operator-valued composition whose second argument is locally linear, injective at the reference point, and has closed range, the mixed coderivative satisfies an exact chain rule and the normal coderivative satisfies the corresponding inclusion. Weak-star extensibility of the reference operator's range upgrades the normal inclusion to equality.
assumptions_latex: G:X\rightrightarrows Y,\quad f:X\times Y\to Z,\quad X,Y,Z\text{ Banach}
f(\bar x,\cdot)\text{ is injective and has closed range in }Z
x\mapsto f(x,\cdot)\in\mathcal L(Y,Z)\text{ is strictly differentiable at }\bar x
\bar y\in G(\bar x),\quad \bar z=f(\bar x,\bar y)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall z^*\in Z^*:\ D_M^*(f\circ G)(\bar x,\bar z)(z^*)=\nabla_x f(\bar x,\bar y)^*z^*+D_M^*G(\bar x,\bar y)(f(\bar x,\cdot)^*z^*),\quad D_N^*(f\circ G)(\bar x,\bar z)(z^*)\subset\nabla_x f(\bar x,\bar y)^*z^*+D_N^*G(\bar x,\bar y)(f(\bar x,\cdot)^*z^*),\text{ with equality in the second relation if }\operatorname{rge}f(\bar x,\cdot)\text{ is weak-star-extensible in }Z.

Consider the referenced problem with \(\beta_l<\beta_r\). Let \(f:L^2(\Omega)\to\mathbb R\) be continuously Fréchet differentiable and satisfy condition (2.24), and set \(\theta=1/\alpha\). Then the reformulated optimality operator \(\Phi:L^2(\Omega)\to L^2(\Omega)\) is \(\partial\Phi\)-semismooth, where
\[\partial\Phi(u)=\left\{M=I+\frac{g}{\alpha}H'(u):g\in L^\infty(\Omega),\ g(x)\in\partial^{cl}P_{[\beta_l,\beta_r]}\!\left(-\frac1\alpha H(u)(x)\right)\ \text{a.e.}\right\},\]
and
\[\partial^{cl}P_{[\beta_l,\beta_r]}(t)=\begin{cases}\{0\},&t<\beta_l\text{ or }t>\beta_r,\\ \{1\},&\beta_l<t<\beta_r,\\ [0,1],&t\in\{\beta_l,\beta_r\}.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the referenced problem assumptions and regularity condition, the projection-based L2 optimality operator is semismooth. Its generalized differential is the identity plus the derivative of H multiplied by a measurable selection from the Clarke differential of interval projection, which equals 0 outside the interval, 1 in its interior, and [0,1] at either endpoint.
assumptions_latex: f:L^2(\Omega)\to\mathbb R\text{ is continuously Fréchet differentiable and satisfies condition (2.24)}
\Phi\text{ is the optimality operator in the referenced reformulation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi\text{ is }\partial\Phi\text{-semismooth with }\partial\Phi(u)=\left\{I+\frac{g}{\alpha}H'(u):g(x)\in\partial^{cl}P_{[\beta_l,\beta_r]}(-H(u)(x)/\alpha)\text{ a.e.}\right\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Local Boundedness and Nonsingularity Lemma
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A neighborhood stability result for compact-valued upper-semicontinuous matrix mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $J:\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be compact-valued and upper semicontinuous, where $\Omega$ is open. If $\bar x\in\Omega$ and every $H\in J(\bar x)$ is nonsingular, then there exist $\kappa,\delta>0$ such that $\mathbb B(\bar x,\delta)\subseteq\Omega$ and $$\sup_{\substack{x\in\mathbb B(\bar x,\delta)\\H\in J(x)}}\max\{\|H\|,\|H^{-1}\|\}\leq\kappa.$$ In particular, every $H\in J(x)$ is nonsingular for every $x\in\mathbb B(\bar x,\delta)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a compact-valued upper-semicontinuous matrix mapping contains only nonsingular matrices at a point, then on some neighborhood all its matrices remain nonsingular, and both the matrices and their inverses are uniformly bounded.
assumptions_latex: J:\Omega\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\text{ is compact-valued and upper semicontinuous}
\forall H\in J(\bar x),\ H\text{ is nonsingular}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\kappa,\delta>0:\ \sup_{\substack{x\in\mathbb B(\bar x,\delta)\\H\in J(x)}}\max\{\|H\|,\|H^{-1}\|\}\leq\kappa.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semismoothness and generalized differential of a projected residual operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded function-space regularity result for the residual operator used by a semismooth Newton method without smoothing steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:L^2(\Omega)\to L^2(\Omega)\) be continuously differentiable, let Assumption 4.1 hold, and define \(\Phi(u)=u-S(u)\), with \(S\) as in (4.2). Then \(\Phi\) is locally Lipschitz continuous and \(\partial^\circ\Phi\)-semismooth, and \(\partial^\circ\Phi(u)\) consists of all \(M\in\mathcal L(L^2,L^2)\) of the form \(M=I+\lambda^{-1}d\cdot G'(u)\), where \(d\in L^\infty(\Omega)\) and \(d(\omega)\in\partial P_{[a(\omega),b(\omega)]}(-\lambda^{-1}G(u)(\omega))\) for \(\omega\in\Omega\). If \(F'\) is \(\alpha\)-order Hölder continuous for \(\alpha\in(0,1]\), then \(\Phi\) is \(\beta\)-order semismooth, with \(\beta\) as given in Theorem 3.50.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumption 4.1, the residual operator Phi, defined as the identity minus S, is locally Lipschitz and semismooth. Its generalized differential consists of the identity plus the scaled composition of G prime with a bounded multiplication function selected pointwise from the generalized derivative of the interval projection. If F prime is Hölder continuous of order alpha, Phi has the corresponding semismoothness order beta specified by Theorem 3.50.
assumptions_latex: F'\text{ is }\alpha\text{-order Hölder continuous for some }\alpha\in(0,1]\quad\text{(for the final order claim only)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi\text{ is locally Lipschitz and }\partial^\circ\Phi\text{-semismooth, with }\partial^\circ\Phi(u)=\left\{I+\lambda^{-1}d\cdot G'(u):d\in L^\infty(\Omega),\ d(\omega)\in\partial P_{[a(\omega),b(\omega)]}(-\lambda^{-1}G(u)(\omega))\text{ for }\omega\in\Omega\right\};\text{ under the additional Hölder assumption, }\Phi\text{ is }\beta\text{-order semismooth as in Theorem 3.50.

children.title: Banach-Space Semismooth Newton Method
children.top_down_role: The basic semismooth Newton family for Banach-space operator equations.

assumptions_latex: \(F:U\subset X\to Y\) is semismooth relative to \(\mathcal G\), and the equation is \(F(x)=0\).
For each iterate, an operator \(G_k\in\mathcal G(x_k)\) is selected and the linear equation \(G_ks=-F(x_k)\) is solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the iteration reaches \(F(x_k)=0\), it returns a root. Local superlinear convergence requires semismoothness at a root and uniformly bounded inverses of the selected generalized derivatives near that root.

notation.meaning: Selected generalized derivative at the current iterate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact local semismooth Newton iteration for a Banach-space operator equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in U\) and a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), repeat while \(\|F(x_k)\|_Y>\varepsilon\): choose \(G_k\in\mathcal G(x_k)\), solve
\[
G_ks_k=-F(x_k),
\]
and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), provided \(x_k+s_k\in U\). Stop and return \(x_k\) when the residual tolerance is met. If \(x_*\) is a root, \(F\) is semismooth at \(x_*\), and all admissible \(G\in\mathcal G(x)\) near \(x_*\) are invertible with uniformly bounded inverses, then sufficiently close iterates converge superlinearly to \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a generalized derivative, solve the linearized operator equation, and add the correction; uniform local invertibility and semismoothness yield superlinear local convergence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The iteration fits the algorithm leaf, but the superlinear convergence assertion needs a source confirming the precise semismoothness notion, admissible generalized differential, neighborhood invariance, and uniform inverse hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Convergence of the Residual-Stopping Smoothed Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence and conditional identification of a terminating root with the reference solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f:V\subset Y\to Z$ be an operator between Banach spaces, with $V$ open, generalized differential $\partial^*f:V\rightrightarrows\mathcal L(Y,Z)$, and a solution $\bar y\in V$. Suppose Assumption 3.12 holds at every iteration in which steps 2--4 of Algorithm 3.14 are executed. If $f$ is $\partial^*f$-semismooth at $\bar y$, then there exists $\delta>0$ such that every $y_0\in\bar y+\delta B_Y$ causes the algorithm either to terminate at a solution $y^*=y_k\in\bar y+\delta B_Y$ or to generate $(y_k)\subset V$ converging $q$-superlinearly to $\bar y$ in $Y$. If a terminating solution also satisfies $\|y^*-\bar y\|_Y\le C_S\|y^*-\bar y\|_{Y_0}$ and admits $M_*\in\partial^*f(y^*)\cap\mathcal L(Y_0,Z)$ with $\|M_*^{-1}\|_{Z,Y_0}\le C_{M^{-1}}$, then $y^*=\bar y$. If, additionally, $f$ is $\alpha$-order $\partial^*f$-semismooth at $\bar y$ for $0<\alpha\le1$, then the $q$-order is at least $1+\alpha$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the iteration-wise regularity and smoothing assumptions, the residual-stopping method locally either terminates at a nearby root or converges q-superlinearly to the reference root. A terminating root equals the reference root under the additional smoothing comparison and inverse-regularity conditions. Alpha-order semismoothness yields order at least 1 plus alpha.
assumptions_latex: f:V\subset Y\to Z,\quad V\text{ open},\quad Y,Z\text{ Banach spaces}
\bar y\in V\text{ solves the operator equation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\delta>0\ \forall y_0\in\bar y+\delta B_Y:\quad \bigl[f(y^*)=0,\ y^*\in\bar y+\delta B_Y\bigr]\ \text{on termination, or}\quad y_k\xrightarrow[q\text{-superlinearly}]{Y}\bar y;\quad \left.\begin{array}{c}\|y^*-\bar y\|_Y\le C_S\|y^*-\bar y\|_{Y_0}\\ M_*\in\partial^*f(y^*)\cap\mathcal L(Y_0,Z)\\ \|M_*^{-1}\|_{Z,Y_0}\le C_{M^{-1}}\end{array}\right\}\Rightarrow y^*=\bar y;\qquad \alpha\text{-order semismoothness}\Rightarrow \operatorname{ord}_q\ge1+\alpha.

children.title: Banach-Space Inexact Semismooth Newton
children.top_down_role: Function-space semismooth Newton methods with approximate local solves.

assumptions_latex: \(F:U\subset X\to Y\) is semismooth near a root, and selected \(G_k\in\mathcal G(x_k)\) have uniformly bounded inverses.
The forcing terms satisfy \(0\le\eta_k<1\); for superlinear convergence, \(\eta_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For sufficiently close initialization, the residual-controlled inexact iteration is locally convergent. It is superlinearly convergent when \(\eta_k\to0\), subject to the stated semismoothness and uniform inverse bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-forced inexact semismooth Newton iteration in Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in U\), at iteration \(k\) select \(G_k\in\mathcal G(x_k)\) and compute \(s_k\in X\) such that
\[
r_k:=G_ks_k+F(x_k),
\qquad
\|r_k\|_Y\le\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|_Y.
\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) and stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|_Y\le\varepsilon\). Uniformly bounded inverse operators and forcing terms bounded strictly below one give the local contraction mechanism; the stronger condition \(\eta_k\to0\), together with semismoothness, yields superlinear local convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Newton equation may be solved approximately when its linear residual is controlled by a forcing fraction of the nonlinear residual; vanishing forcing terms recover superlinear convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Banach-Space Inexact Semismooth Newton

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inexact Newton residual condition fits the leaf. However, forcing terms merely bounded below one do not by themselves state a quantitatively sufficient contraction condition for the general Banach-space formulation; the local and superlinear claims require a dedicated source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence guarantee for Algorithm 3.16 under the cited regularity and inexact-operator assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f:V\subset Y\to Z$ be an operator between Banach spaces, with $V$ open and generalized differential $\partial^*f:V\rightrightarrows\mathcal L(Y,Z)$. Let $\bar y\in V$ solve the operator equation, suppose $f$ is Lipschitz continuous near $\bar y$, and suppose Assumptions 3.12 and 3.17(a) hold with the same operators $M_k$. If $f$ is $\partial^*f$-semismooth at $\bar y$, then there exists $\delta>0$ such that every $y_0\in\bar y+\delta B_Y$ makes Algorithm 3.16 either terminate with $y_k=\bar y$ or generate $(y_k)\subset V$ converging $q$-superlinearly to $\bar y$ in $Y$. If, additionally, $0<\alpha\le1$, $f$ is order-$\alpha$ $\partial^*f$-semismooth at $\bar y$, and Assumption 3.17(b) holds, then the $q$-order is at least $1+\alpha$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting sufficiently near the solution, Algorithm 3.16 either reaches that solution or converges to it q-superlinearly. Order-alpha semismoothness and the order-alpha operator approximation condition give q-order at least one plus alpha.

\bar y\in V\text{ solves the operator equation}
f\text{ is Lipschitz continuous near }\bar y

children.top_down_role: Projected inexact semismooth Newton methods in Banach spaces.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset X\) is nonempty and admits a continuous retraction \(P_C:X\to C\), and \(F:U\to Y\) is semismooth on a neighborhood of \(C\cap U\).
At \(x_k\in C\), an inexact correction satisfies \(\|G_ks_k+F(x_k)\|_Y\le\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|_Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iterate lies in \(C\). Any returned point satisfies the residual stopping test, while local convergence requires compatibility of the retraction, the constrained solution, and the generalized linearizations.

notation.meaning: Retraction or projection onto the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving projection of an inexact operator Newton trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(x_0\in C\cap U\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and forcing terms \(\eta_k\in[0,1)\). While \(\|F(x_k)\|_Y>\varepsilon\), select \(G_k\in\mathcal G(x_k)\), compute \(s_k\) satisfying
\[
\|G_ks_k+F(x_k)\|_Y\le\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|_Y,
\]
and update
\[
x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k+s_k).
\]
Stop when the residual tolerance is met. Because \(P_C(X)\subset C\), feasibility is preserved. A convergence assertion additionally requires local regularity of the constrained equation and stability of \(P_C\) near its solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute an inexact generalized Newton correction and retract the trial point onto the feasible set, thereby preserving feasibility at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Inexact Operator Newton

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasibility-preserving update fits the projected-algorithm leaf, but an arbitrary continuous retraction is too broad for a sourced projected Newton method. The intended projection geometry and compatibility conditions require specification and evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected Inexact Newton Method for an NCP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected and smoothed inexact Newton iteration for a function-space nonlinear complementarity problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(u_0\in\mathcal K\). At iteration \(k\), choose an invertible \(B_k\in\mathcal L(L^r(\Omega),L^r(\Omega))\), solve \(B_ks_k=-\Phi(u_k)\), and set \(u_{k+1}^0=u_k+s_k\). Apply the smoothing map \(u_{k+1}^1=S_k(u_{k+1}^0)\in L^p(\Omega)\), and then set \(u_{k+1}=P_{\mathcal K}(u_{k+1}^1)\). If \(u_{k+1}=u_k\), stop with \(u^*=u_{k+1}\); otherwise increment \(k\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a point in K, compute an inexact Newton correction in L^r, smooth the trial point into L^p, and project it onto K. Stop when the projected iterate is unchanged; otherwise repeat.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_{k+1}=P_{\mathcal K}\!\left(S_k\!\left(u_k-B_k^{-1}\Phi(u_k)\right)\right),\qquad u_{k+1}=u_k\Rightarrow u^*=u_{k+1}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Convergence and Terminal-Solution Identification for the Second Inexact Operator Newton Variant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence and conditional identification of a terminal solution for Algorithm 3.19.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f:V\subset Y\to Z$ be an operator between Banach spaces, with $V$ open and generalized differential $\partial^*f:V\rightrightarrows\mathcal L(Y,Z)$. Let $\bar y\in V$ solve the operator equation, suppose $f$ is Lipschitz continuous near $\bar y$, and suppose Assumptions 3.12 and 3.17(a) hold with the same $M_k$ at every iteration where steps 2--4 are executed. If $f$ is $\partial^*f$-semismooth at $\bar y$, then there exists $\delta>0$ such that every $y_0\in\bar y+\delta B_Y$ makes Algorithm 3.19 either terminate at a solution $y^*=y_k\in\bar y+\delta B_Y$ or generate $(y_k)\subset V$ converging $q$-superlinearly to $\bar y$ in $Y$. If termination occurs in step 1 and $f(y^*)=0$, $\|y^*-\bar y\|_Y\le C_S\|y^*-\bar y\|_{Y_0}$, and there exists $M_*\in\partial^*f(y^*)\cap\mathcal L(Y_0,Z)$ with $\|M_*^{-1}\|_{Z,Y_0}\le C_{M^{-1}}$, then $y^*=\bar y$. If, additionally, $0<\alpha\le1$, $f$ is order-$\alpha$ $\partial^*f$-semismooth at $\bar y$, and Assumption 3.17(b) holds, then the $q$-order is at least $1+\alpha$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting sufficiently near the reference solution, Algorithm 3.19 either terminates at a nearby solution or converges q-superlinearly to the reference solution. A solution found in step 1 equals the reference solution under the stated norm-comparison and inverse-regularity conditions. The stronger order-alpha hypotheses give q-order at least one plus alpha.
assumptions_latex: f:V\subset Y\to Z\text{ acts between Banach spaces and }V\text{ is open}
\bar y\in V\text{ solves the operator equation}
f\text{ is Lipschitz continuous near }\bar y
\text{Assumptions 3.12 and 3.17(a) hold with the same }M_k\text{ whenever steps 2--4 are executed}
\text{For step-1 identification: }f(y^*)=0,\ \|y^*-\bar y\|_Y\le C_S\|y^*-\bar y\|_{Y_0},\ M_*\in\partial^*f(y^*)\cap\mathcal L(Y_0,Z),\ \|M_*^{-1}\|_{Z,Y_0}\le C_{M^{-1}}
\text{For the order claim: }0<\alpha\le1,\ f\text{ is order-}\alpha\ \partial^*f\text{-semismooth, and Assumption 3.17(b) holds
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\delta>0\ \forall y_0\in\bar y+\delta B_Y:\ \text{Algorithm 3.19 terminates at a solution in }\bar y+\delta B_Y\text{ or }y_k\to\bar y\text{ q-superlinearly in }Y;\quad \text{the step-1 conditions imply }y^*=\bar y;\quad \operatorname{qord}\ge1+\alpha\text{ under the additional assumptions}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection and Local Stability Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions imposed on the projection in the projected inexact semismooth Newton method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mapping \(P_{\mathcal K}\) is a metric projection onto \(\mathcal K\): for every \(y\in Y\), \[\|P_{\mathcal K}(y)-y\|_Y=\min_{v\in\mathcal K}\|v-y\|_Y.\] Moreover, there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar y\) in \(Y\) and a constant \(L_P>0\) such that \[\|P_{\mathcal K}(y)-\bar y\|_Y\le L_P\|y-\bar y\|_Y\qquad(y\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every point is mapped to a nearest point in the constraint set. Near the reference point, the projected point satisfies the stated one-point stability bound relative to that reference point.
assumptions_latex: P_{\mathcal K}\text{ is a mapping onto }\mathcal K
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall y\in Y,\ \|P_{\mathcal K}(y)-y\|_Y=\min_{v\in\mathcal K}\|v-y\|_Y,\qquad \exists U\ni\bar y\ \exists L_P>0\ \forall y\in U,\ \|P_{\mathcal K}(y)-\bar y\|_Y\le L_P\|y-\bar y\|_Y.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Convergence of Projected Inexact Semismooth Newton
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local feasible convergence and convergence order for Algorithm 3.22 in Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:V\subset Y\to Z\) be an operator between Banach spaces, with \(V\) open and generalized differential \(\partial^*f:V\rightrightarrows\mathcal L(Y,Z)\). Let \(\mathcal K\subset Y\) be closed and convex with projection \(P_{\mathcal K}\), and let \(\bar y\in V\cap\mathcal K\) solve (3.19). Suppose that \(f\) is Lipschitz continuous on \(\mathcal K\) near \(\bar y\) and that Assumptions 3.12, 3.17(a), and 3.21 hold. If \(f\) is \(\partial^*f\)-semismooth at \(\bar y\), then there exists \(\delta>0\) such that, for every \(y_0\in(\bar y+\delta B_Y)\cap\mathcal K\), Algorithm 3.22 either terminates with \(y_k=\bar y\) or generates a sequence \((y_k)\subset V\cap\mathcal K\) converging q-superlinearly to \(\bar y\) in \(Y\). If, additionally, \(f\) is \(\alpha\)-order \(\partial^*f\)-semismooth at \(\bar y\), where \(0<\alpha\le1\), and Assumption 3.17(b) holds, then the q-order of convergence is at least \(1+\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the cited regularity, method, and projection assumptions, every sufficiently close feasible starting point either reaches the reference solution finitely or produces feasible iterates converging q-superlinearly to it. Alpha-order semismoothness together with Assumption 3.17(b) yields q-order at least 1+alpha.
assumptions_latex: Y,Z\text{ are Banach spaces and }V\subset Y\text{ is open}
\mathcal K\subset Y\text{ is closed and convex with projection }P_{\mathcal K}
f\text{ is Lipschitz continuous on }\mathcal K\text{ near }\bar y
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\delta>0\ \forall y_0\in(\bar y+\delta B_Y)\cap\mathcal K:\ \bigl(\exists k,\ y_k=\bar y\bigr)\lor\bigl((y_k)\subset V\cap\mathcal K\text{ and }y_k\to\bar y\text{ q-superlinearly in }Y\bigr);\quad \bigl(0<\alpha\le1,\ f\text{ is }\alpha\text{-order semismooth, Assumption 3.17(b)}\bigr)\Rightarrow q\text{-order}\ge1+\alpha.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity and Smoothing Conditions for Projected Operator Newton
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative uniform-invertibility hypotheses and the smoothing estimate for the projected function-space Newton iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar u\in\mathcal K\) solve (3.1). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Either the selected generalized derivatives have uniformly bounded inverses on L^r, or every generalized derivative near the solution within K does. The smoothing maps must uniformly control the L^p error by the unsmoothed trial point's L^r error.

children.top_down_role: Function-space regularity routes beyond direct generalized differential invertibility.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are Banach spaces and the problem is the generalized equation \(0\in F(x)+Q(x)\), with \(F:X\to Y\) and \(Q:X\rightrightarrows Y\).
At a solution \(x_*\), a linearization \(G_*\) of \(F\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong metric regularity of the linearized generalized equation supplies a locally single-valued Lipschitz solution map for perturbed inclusions, providing a regularity route that does not require \(G_*:X\to Y\) itself to be invertible.

notation.meaning: Set-valued part of the generalized equation.
Reference linearization of the single-valued part.
Localized solution mapping of the linearized inclusion.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong metric regularity of a linearized generalized equation as an alternative Newton regularity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the linearized solution mapping
\[
S(y):=\{x\in X:y\in F(x_*)+G_*(x-x_*)+Q(x)\}.
\]
The linearized generalized equation is strongly metrically regular at \((x_*,0)\) when neighborhoods \(U\) of \(x_*\) and \(V\) of \(0\) exist such that \(S(y)\cap U\) is a singleton for every \(y\in V\), and the resulting mapping \(s:V\to U\) is Lipschitz. This condition replaces direct invertibility of \(G_*\) by stable local solvability of the complete linearized inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric regularity requires the perturbed linearized inclusion to have a unique Lipschitz-localized solution, even when the linear operator alone is not invertible.
knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Operator Regularity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the alternative-regularity leaf and resembles strong metric regularity of the complete linearized generalized equation, but the exact localization, base point, and perturbation convention need an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Upper Semicontinuity and Pointwise Invertibility Imply Neighborhood Invertibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implication between alternative regularity conditions for semismooth operator equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(y\mapsto\partial^*f(y)\subset\mathcal L(Y_0,Z)\) is upper semicontinuous at \(\bar y\) and there exists \(C_{M^{-1}}>0\) such that every \(M\in\partial^*f(\bar y)\) is invertible with \(\lVert M^{-1}\rVert_{Z,Y_0}\le C_{M^{-1}}\), then Assumption 3.25 holds. In particular, the cited semismooth-Newton theorems remain valid when Assumption 3.12(a) is replaced by this upper-semicontinuity and pointwise-invertibility condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper semicontinuity of the generalized differential at the solution, together with a common inverse bound for all generalized derivatives there, implies the uniform neighborhood invertibility condition. The cited results may therefore use this condition in place of Assumption 3.12(a).
assumptions_latex: \(y\mapsto\partial^*f(y)\subset\mathcal L(Y_0,Z)\text{ is upper semicontinuous at }\bar y\)
\(\exists C_{M^{-1}}>0\;\forall M\in\partial^*f(\bar y):\ M\text{ is invertible and }\lVert M^{-1}\rVert_{Z,Y_0}\le C_{M^{-1}}\)

children.title: Generalized Differentials for Superposition Operators
children.top_down_role: Newton derivative constructions for pointwise operator mappings.

assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)\) is a measure space and \(1\le p,q\le\infty\).
The scalar map \(\phi:\Omega\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is measurable in its first argument and admits measurable generalized derivative selections \(a(\omega,t)\).
For each relevant \(u\), multiplication by \(a(\cdot,u(\cdot))\) defines a bounded operator from \(L^p(\Omega)\) to \(L^q(\Omega)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generalized differential candidate for the superposition operator at \(u\) consists of multiplication operators generated by admissible measurable pointwise selections from the scalar generalized differential.

notation.meaning: Superposition operator induced by the scalar integrand.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise generalized derivatives lifted to bounded multiplication operators between Lebesgue spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
(\Phi(u))(\omega)=\phi(\omega,u(\omega))
\]
whenever the right-hand side belongs to \(L^q(\Omega)\). For an admissible measurable selection satisfying
\[
a(\omega,u(\omega))\in\partial_N\phi(\omega,u(\omega))
\quad\text{for almost every }\omega,
\]
define
\[
(M_a(u)h)(\omega)=a(\omega,u(\omega))h(\omega).
\]
Provided \(M_a(u)\in\mathcal L(L^p,L^q)\), the collection of all such multiplication operators is the pointwise-lifted generalized differential \(\mathcal G_\Phi(u)\) used in a Newton linearization of \(\Phi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise generalized derivative of a scalar nonlinearity lifts to a multiplication operator, provided the measurable selection acts boundedly between the chosen function spaces.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Differentials for Superposition Operators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiplication-operator representation fits the leaf, but \(\partial_N\) is not defined and no source establishes which scalar generalized differential, measurable-selection conditions, or growth bounds produce the asserted operator differential.

children.title: Semismoothness of Superposition Operators
children.top_down_role: Semismoothness regimes for pointwise nonlinear operators between function spaces.

assumptions_latex: \(1\le q<p<\infty\), \(\mu(\Omega)<\infty\), and \(\Phi:L^p(\Omega)\to L^q(\Omega)\) is induced by \(\phi(\omega,t)\).
The scalar maps are uniformly semismooth on bounded \(t\)-sets almost everywhere, with measurable derivative selections having growth sufficient to define bounded multipliers from \(L^p\) to \(L^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under these uniform remainder and growth conditions, the superposition operator is Newton semismooth from \(L^p(\Omega)\) to \(L^q(\Omega)\) relative to the pointwise multiplication operators.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A norm-gap sufficient regime for semismooth superposition operators on finite-measure domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(u,h\in L^p(\Omega)\), define the pointwise remainder
\[
r(u,h)=\Phi(u+h)-\Phi(u)-M_a(u+h)h,
\]
where \(M_a(u+h)\) is an admissible pointwise generalized derivative. If the scalar semismooth remainder is uniform on bounded scalar sets and the derivative growth provides an \(L^q\)-integrable domination for bounded \(L^p\)-sequences, then the norm gap \(q<p\) yields
\[
\sup_{M_a(u+h)\in\mathcal G_\Phi(u+h)}
\frac{\|r(u,h)\|_{L^q}}{\|h\|_{L^p}}\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{as }\|h\|_{L^p}\to0.
\]
Thus \(\Phi\) is semismooth from \(L^p\) to \(L^q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform pointwise semismoothness, suitable growth, and a strict integrability gap can lift scalar semismoothness to a superposition operator between Lebesgue spaces.
knowledge_statements.title: Semismoothness of Superposition Operators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property belongs in this leaf, but phrases such as “uniform on bounded scalar sets” and “growth provides an integrable domination” are not precise enough to verify the displayed supremum limit. Exact exponents and domination hypotheses require a source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semismoothness and generalized differential of the bound-constrained residual operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity transfer and pointwise generalized-differential representation for the NCP/MCP superposition operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under Assumption 5.1, \(\Phi:L^p(\Omega)\to L^r(\Omega)\) is locally Lipschitz continuous and \(\partial^\circ\Phi\)-semismooth, where \(\partial^\circ\Phi(u)\) consists of all operators
\[
M=d_1I+d_2F'(u),\qquad d_1,d_2\in L^\infty(\Omega),
\]
whose coefficients satisfy almost everywhere
\[
(d_1,d_2)(\omega)\in\begin{cases}
\{(0,1)\},&\omega\in\Omega^f,\\
\partial\phi(u(\omega)-a(\omega),F(u)(\omega)),&\omega\in\Omega^l,\\
\partial\phi(b(\omega)-u(\omega),-F(u)(\omega)),&\omega\in\Omega^u,\\
\partial\phi_{[a(\omega),b(\omega)]}(u(\omega),F(u)(\omega)),&\omega\in\Omega^{lu}.
\end{cases}
\]
Under Assumption 5.2, \(\Phi\) is \(\beta\)-order semismooth, where \(\beta>0\) is as specified by the applicable order-transfer theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bound-constrained complementarity residual is locally Lipschitz and semismooth. Its generalized differential consists exactly of multiplication-operator combinations of the identity and the derivative of F, with coefficients selected pointwise from the relevant complementarity-function generalized derivatives. The stronger assumptions yield positive-order semismoothness.
assumptions_latex: For the baseline conclusion, Assumption 5.1 holds, including \(r\in[1,p)\cap[1,p')\), continuous differentiability of \(F:L^p\to L^r\), local Lipschitz continuity of \(F:L^p\to L^{p'}\), and Lipschitz semismooth scalar complementarity data.
For the higher-order conclusion, Assumption 5.2 holds, including a locally \(\alpha\)-Hölder derivative and \(\alpha\)-order semismooth scalar complementarity data for some \(\alpha\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial^\circ\Phi(u)=\{d_1I+d_2F'(u): (d_1,d_2)\text{ satisfy the displayed pointwise selections}\},\quad\Phi\text{ is locally Lipschitz and semismooth; under Assumption 5.2 it is }\beta\text{-order semismooth.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Order semismoothness of the Fischer–Burmeister superposition operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded quantitative semismoothness result under a measure-decay condition near simultaneous degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Assumptions 3.38(a) and (b) hold, let \(\Phi\) be the operator with \(\phi=\phi^{FB}\), and let \(u\in L^p(\Omega)\). If there exists \(\gamma>0\) such that \[\operatorname{meas}\!\left(\{0<|u|+|F(u)|<\varepsilon\}\right)=O(\varepsilon^\gamma)\quad\text{as }\varepsilon\to0,\] then \(\Phi\) is \(\beta\)-order semismooth at \(u\), where \[\beta=\min\left\{\frac{\gamma v}{1+\gamma/q},\frac{\alpha\gamma v}{\alpha+\gamma v}\right\},\qquad q=\min\{p,p'\},\] and \[v=\begin{cases}\dfrac{q-r}{qr},&q<\infty,\\[2pt]\dfrac1r,&q=\infty.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the Fischer–Burmeister operator, Assumptions 3.38(a) and (b), together with gamma-order decay of the measure of the nearly degenerate set, imply beta-order semismoothness at u, with beta determined by alpha, gamma, and the integrability exponents.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi\text{ is }\beta\text{-order semismooth at }u,\qquad \beta=\min\left\{\frac{\gamma v}{1+\gamma/q},\frac{\alpha\gamma v}{\alpha+\gamma v}\right\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Entropy-Inverse Nemytskii Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the superposition operators generated by the pointwise inverse entropy transforms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R\) be bounded and measurable, and let \(m\) be continuous and bounded with \(m(t)\ge m_0>0\) for every \(t\in\Omega\). For the pointwise functions \(\phi\) and \(\widetilde\phi\), define
\[
H:\Sigma(m)\to L^1(\Omega),\qquad (Hv)(t):=\phi(t,v(t)),
\]
and
\[
\widetilde H:L^2(\Omega)\to L^1(\Omega),\qquad (\widetilde Hv)(t):=\widetilde\phi(t,v(t)).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The operators H and tilde-H are Nemytskii operators obtained by applying the entropy inverse phi or its zero extension pointwise. H is defined on Sigma(m), whereas tilde-H is defined on all of L2(Omega).
assumptions_latex: \phi\text{ and }\widetilde\phi\text{ are the entropy inverse transforms}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (Hv)(t)=\phi(t,v(t)),\qquad (\widetilde Hv)(t)=\widetilde\phi(t,v(t)).

children.title: Two-Norm Semismoothness
children.top_down_role: Semismoothness using distinct norms for perturbations and residuals.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a vector space equipped with a perturbation norm \(\|\cdot\|_X\), and \(Y\) is equipped with a residual norm \(\|\cdot\|_Y\).
\(F:U\subset X\to Y\) and \(\mathcal G(x)\subset\mathcal L(X,Y)\) is nonempty near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed mixed-norm remainder limit defines two-norm semismoothness. It permits a stronger norm to measure perturbations and a weaker norm to measure residuals, while Newton convergence additionally requires stability of the linear solves in these norms.

notation.meaning: Norm measuring nonlinear remainders and residuals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-norm Newton remainder condition for function-space mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mapping \(F\) is two-norm semismooth at \(x\in U\), relative to \(\mathcal G\), when
\[
\sup_{G\in\mathcal G(x+h)}
\frac{\|F(x+h)-F(x)-Gh\|_Y}{\|h\|_X}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{as }\|h\|_X\to0,
\]
for nonzero admissible perturbations \(h\). The domain norm controls the size of the Newton perturbation, whereas the codomain norm measures the linearization error. The two norms need not arise from the same function-space exponent or topology, but every \(G\) used in the quotient must act boundedly from \(X\) to \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-norm semismoothness measures perturbations in one norm and linearization errors in another, requiring the mixed-norm remainder to be little-o of the perturbation size.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Norm Semismoothness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits the leaf, but the statement may conflate ordinary semismoothness between distinct domain and codomain Banach spaces with the specialized two-norm framework, which commonly involves different topologies on the relevant function-space variables. A dedicated source is required before fixing the definition.

children.title: Semismooth Composite-Operator Rules
children.top_down_role: Composition and chain-rule structures for semismooth operators.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y,Z\) are Banach spaces, \(H:X\to Y\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable near \(\bar x\).
\(F:Y\to Z\) is Newton differentiable near \(H(\bar x)\), with Newton derivative selection \(G_F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\circ H\) is Newton differentiable at \(\bar x\) with derivative selection \(G_{F\circ H}(x)=G_F(H(x))H'(x)\).

notation.meaning: Newton derivative selection for the outer operator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Banach-space chain rule with a smooth inner operator and a semismooth outer operator.

source_refs.locator: 7.5 Semismooth Newton Methods p. 692
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\) near \(\bar x\), define \(G_{F\circ H}(x):=G_F(H(x))H'(x)\). Then
\[
\|(F\circ H)(x+h)-(F\circ H)(x)-G_{F\circ H}(x+h)h\|_Z=o(\|h\|_X)
\]
as \(h\to0\). Hence composition with a continuously Fréchet differentiable inner map preserves Newton differentiability. If the remainder for \(F\) is of order \(O(\|k\|_Y^{1+\alpha})\) and \(H'\) is locally Hölder continuous of order \(\alpha\), then the composite remainder has order \(O(\|h\|_X^{1+\alpha})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composing a semismooth outer operator with a continuously differentiable inner operator preserves Newton differentiability, with generalized derivative obtained by the operator chain rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Semismooth Composite-Operator Rules

source_witnesses.locator: 7.5 Semismooth Newton Methods p. 692

children.title: Superposition-Operator Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Loss of operator semismoothness through incompatible spaces, norms, or growth behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(1\le p<\infty\), \(\Omega=(-1,1)\), and \(N(u)=\max\{0,u\}\) acts from \(L^p(\Omega)\) to itself.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The usual active-set derivative \(G(v)h=\mathbf 1_{\{v>0\}}h\) does not make \(N:L^p(\Omega)\to L^p(\Omega)\) Newton differentiable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete same-norm obstruction for the positive-part superposition operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(u(t)=t\) and \(h_n(t)=-2t\mathbf 1_{(0,1/n)}(t)\). On \((0,1/n)\), one has \(u+h_n=-t<0\), so \(G(u+h_n)h_n=0\), while
\[
N(u+h_n)-N(u)-G(u+h_n)h_n=-t\mathbf 1_{(0,1/n)}(t).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{\|N(u+h_n)-N(u)-G(u+h_n)h_n\|_{L^p}}{\|h_n\|_{L^p}}=\frac12
\]
for every \(n\), although \(h_n\to0\) in \(L^p\). Thus the required Newton remainder is not little-oh in the same norm; a norm gap or stronger domain control is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive-part superposition operator can fail Newton differentiability when domain and range use the same Lebesgue norm, because errors concentrated near switching points do not decay relatively.
knowledge_statements.title: Superposition-Operator Failure Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed sequence correctly shows that the stated active-set selection fails the Newton remainder test at the chosen function. It does not by itself establish failure for every admissible generalized derivative, and the assertion that a norm gap or stronger domain control is essential is broader than the example. No source is supplied for the intended operator-level failure boundary.

For every \(c>0\), these conditions are also equivalent to \[u-P_K(u-cg)=0.\] The metric projection is the superposition operator \[(P_Kw)(\omega)=\min\{b(\omega),\max\{a(\omega),w(\omega)\}\}\] for almost every \(\omega\). children.top_down_role: Operator equations for general pointwise convex constraint sets.

assumptions_latex: \(U=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\), and \(C(\omega)\subset\mathbb R^m\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and measurably varying.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in g+N_K(u)\) is equivalent to \(u(\omega)=P_{C(\omega)}(u(\omega)-cg(\omega))\) almost everywhere.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the fiber constraint

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(u\in K\), the inclusion \(0\in g+N_K(u)\) is equivalent to
\[
u=P_K(u-cg).
\]
Because \(K\) is decomposable and its fibers are closed and convex, its metric projection is pointwise:
\[
(P_Kw)(\omega)=P_{C(\omega)}(w(\omega))
\]
for almost every \(\omega\). Therefore the mixed variational condition has the operator-equation form
\[
u(\omega)-P_{C(\omega)}(u(\omega)-cg(\omega))=0
\]
almost everywhere. For polyhedral fibers, generalized derivatives of this residual are determined by the faces active at each \(\omega\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decomposable pointwise convex constraint yields a projection equation evaluated independently in each fiber; polyhedral fibers additionally provide face-based generalized derivatives.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any fixed \(c>0\), define
\[
\mathcal F(y,u,p)=\bigl(E(y,u),\ D_y\mathcal L(y,u,p),\ u-P_K(u-cD_u\mathcal L(y,u,p))\bigr).

Then \(\mathcal F(y,u,p)=0\) is equivalent to

E(y,u)=0,\qquad D_y\mathcal L(y,u,p)=0,\qquad 0\in D_u\mathcal L(y,u,p)+N_K(u).

children.title: Operator-Elimination Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between reduced and coupled realizations.

assumptions_latex: \(Y,U,Z\) are Hilbert spaces, \(J:Y\times U\to\mathbb R\) and \(E:Y\times U\to Z\) are continuously Fréchet differentiable near \((\bar y,\bar u)\), and \(E(\bar y,\bar u)=0\).
The operator \(E_y(\bar y,\bar u):Y\to Z\) is a bounded linear isomorphism, so \(E(y,u)=0\) defines a continuously Fréchet differentiable local map \(y=S(u)\).
\(K\subset U\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, \(c>0\), and the reduced and full residuals are defined using the same projection \(P_K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Near \((\bar y,\bar u)\), the map \(u\mapsto(S(u),u,p(u))\), where \(p(u)\) is the unique adjoint solution, gives a one-to-one correspondence between zeros of the reduced and full residuals.

notation.meaning: unique adjoint associated with a control

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local equivalence obtained by eliminating uniquely solvable state and adjoint equations.

source_refs.locator: 7.2.2 Analysis of State and Adjoint Systems in the Neumann Problem p. 369
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The implicit-function relation gives \[S'(u)=-E_y(S(u),u)^{-1}E_u(S(u),u).\] Let \(p(u)\in Z\) be the unique solution of \[E_y(S(u),u)^*p(u)+J_y(S(u),u)=0.\] For \(j(u)=J(S(u),u)\), the reduced derivative is \[j'(u)=J_u(S(u),u)+E_u(S(u),u)^*p(u).\] Define \[R(u)=u-P_K(u-cj'(u))\] and let \(F_{\mathrm{full}}\) be the corresponding state-adjoint-projection residual. Then, locally, \[R(u)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F_{\mathrm{full}}(S(u),u,p(u))=0.\] Conversely, every nearby zero \((y,u,p)\) of \(F_{\mathrm{full}}\) satisfies \(y=S(u)\), \(p=p(u)\), and \(R(u)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertibility of the state linearization permits unique local elimination of state and adjoint variables, giving a one-to-one correspondence between nearby full KKT zeros and reduced stationary controls.
knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Elimination Correspondence

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2.2 Analysis of State and Adjoint Systems in the Neumann Problem p. 369
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

children.title: Operator-Equivalence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Functional or regularity regimes limiting equivalence between the realizations.

assumptions_latex: \(E(y,u)=y^2-u\) is considered on \(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\) at \((\bar y,\bar u)=(0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A locally single-valued differentiable control-to-state map does not exist at \((0,0)\), so reduced-full operator equivalence based on smooth elimination fails.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of elimination equivalence when the state equation is singular or multivalued.

source_refs.locator: 5.1.2 Necessary Conditions under Operator Constraints p. 9
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(u>0\), the equation \(E(y,u)=0\) has the two solutions \(y=\sqrt u\) and \(y=-\sqrt u\), whereas for \(u<0\) it has no real solution. Moreover,
\[
E_y(0,0)=0,
\]
so the implicit-function hypothesis required for a differentiable map \(y=S(u)\) fails. Neither branch has a bounded derivative as \(u\downarrow0\). Therefore a reduced residual based on smooth state elimination is not locally equivalent to the full operator system at \((0,0)\); branch selection, solvability, or singular adjoint equations must be handled separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a singular, branching state equation, no smooth single-valued state elimination exists, so reduced and full operator systems need not be locally equivalent.
knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Equivalence Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1.2 Necessary Conditions under Operator Constraints p. 9
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

children.title: Mixed-Problem Smoothing Families
children.top_down_role: Smoothing approaches tailored to coupled mixed operator systems.

assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\nu)\) is a finite measure space, \(a,b\in L^\infty(\Omega)\), and \(\mu>0\).
Pointwise complementarity means \(a(\omega)\ge 0\), \(b(\omega)\ge 0\), and \(a(\omega)b(\omega)=0\) for almost every \(\omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scalar function \(\phi_\mu\) is continuously differentiable for every \(\mu>0\), its superposition operator \(\Phi_\mu:L^\infty(\Omega)^2\to L^2(\Omega)\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable, and \(\Phi_\mu(a,b)\to\Phi_0(a,b)\) in \(L^2(\Omega)\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fischer-Burmeister smoothing applied pointwise, with an explicit function-space mapping in which scalar smoothness induces operator differentiability.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. Interior and Smoothing Methods p. 989
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\phi_\mu(s,t)=\sqrt{s^2+t^2+2\mu^2}-s-t\] and \[(\Phi_\mu(a,b))(\omega)=\phi_\mu(a(\omega),b(\omega)).\] For every \(\mu>0\), the scalar function \(\phi_\mu\) is continuously differentiable on \(\mathbb R^2\). On a finite measure space, the associated map \(\Phi_\mu:L^\infty(\Omega)^2\to L^2(\Omega)\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable. Moreover, \[\|\Phi_\mu(a,b)-\Phi_0(a,b)\|_{L^2}\le \sqrt{2}\,\mu\,\nu(\Omega)^{1/2},\] so \(\Phi_\mu(a,b)\to\Phi_0(a,b)\) in \(L^2(\Omega)\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\). The zero set of \(\phi_0\) is exactly the set of \((s,t)\) satisfying \(s\ge0\), \(t\ge0\), and \(st=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fischer-Burmeister smoothing gives a differentiable pointwise complementarity residual for positive smoothing parameters and converges to the exact complementarity residual as the parameter vanishes; an L-infinity to L2 norm choice makes the operator statement well defined.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Problem Smoothing Families

children.title: Mixed-Operator Regularity
children.top_down_role: Regularity structures governing Newton models for mixed systems.

assumptions_latex: \(F:X\to Y\) is locally Lipschitz between Banach spaces and is semismooth at a zero \(\bar x\).
\(\mathcal G(x)\subset\mathcal L(X,Y)\) is a nonempty generalized derivative model near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform bounded invertibility of every \(G\in\mathcal G(x)\) is the mixed-operator regularity condition supporting locally well-defined semismooth Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform generalized-Jacobian regularity for a mixed semismooth Newton residual.

source_refs.locator: 9.1.2 Pointwise FB regularity p. 809
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

source_refs.locator: 7.5 Semismooth Newton Methods p. 692
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Mixed-operator regularity at \(\bar x\) means that there exist a neighborhood \(V\) of \(\bar x\) and a constant \(M<\infty\) such that every \(G\in\mathcal G(x)\), with \(x\in V\), is a bounded linear isomorphism from \(X\) onto \(Y\) and
\[
\sup_{x\in V}\sup_{G\in\mathcal G(x)}\|G^{-1}\|_{\mathcal L(Y,X)}\le M.
\]
Under this condition, each Newton equation \(G_kd_k=-F(x_k)\) is uniquely solvable near \(\bar x\). Combined with semismoothness, the uniform inverse bound yields local superlinear convergence for sufficiently close initial iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-operator regularity requires every nearby generalized derivative to be invertible with uniformly bounded inverse, ensuring solvable Newton steps and supporting local superlinear convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Operator Regularity

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

The record also does not specify the approximation property linking the set-valued model G to semismoothness, yet concludes local superlinear convergence for Newton selections from that model. A Banach-space semismooth Newton source with the exact derivative convention and convergence hypotheses is required.

children.title: Smoothing-Induced Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Conditioning effects associated with smoothed mixed formulations.

assumptions_latex: \(F_\mu:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is differentiable, \(F_\mu(x_\mu)=0\), and \(A_\mu=F_\mu'(x_\mu)\) is nonsingular.
The Euclidean operator norm and its associated singular values are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\sigma_{\min}(A_\mu)\to0\) while \(\sigma_{\max}(A_\mu)\) stays bounded below, then \(\kappa_2(A_\mu)\to\infty\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the smoothed residual at its solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning of finite-dimensional Jacobians generated by a vanishing smoothing parameter.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. Interior and Smoothing Methods p. 989
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a solution \(x_\mu\) of the smoothed system, the local linear conditioning of a Newton step is
\[
\kappa_2(A_\mu)=\|A_\mu\|_2\|A_\mu^{-1}\|_2
=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A_\mu)}{\sigma_{\min}(A_\mu)}.
\]
Hence, if \(\sigma_{\max}(A_\mu)\ge c>0\) and \(\sigma_{\min}(A_\mu)\to0\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\), then \(\kappa_2(A_\mu)\to\infty\). Thus smoothing may produce differentiable residuals while simultaneously degrading the conditioning of their Newton systems near a degenerate complementarity limit. Uniform mixed-operator regularity prevents this mechanism by imposing a parameter-independent inverse bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As smoothing vanishes, a collapsing smallest singular value makes Newton systems increasingly ill-conditioned even though each smoothed residual remains differentiable.
knowledge_statements.title: Smoothing-Induced Conditioning

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Regularity Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure criterion for smoothed mixed systems whose blocks have incompatible function-space regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_\varepsilon:X_1\times X_2\to Y_1\times Y_2\) have solution \(z_\varepsilon^*\), and let \(M_\varepsilon(z)\) be a selected generalized derivative. Mesh-independent semismooth Newton analysis fails whenever, as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), at least one of the following occurs: \[\sup_{0<\lVert d\rVert_X\le t}\frac{\lVert F_\varepsilon(z_\varepsilon^*+d)-F_\varepsilon(z_\varepsilon^*)-M_\varepsilon(z_\varepsilon^*+d)d\rVert_Y}{\lVert d\rVert_X}\not\to0\] uniformly in \(\varepsilon\); \(M_\varepsilon(z)^{-1}\) is unbounded uniformly near \(z_\varepsilon^*\); or a block action required by \(M_\varepsilon\) is not bounded from \(X_j\) to its asserted residual space. These failures preclude uniform local Newton estimates in the chosen norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform Newton analysis fails if mixed-block remainders do not vanish uniformly, inverse derivatives become unbounded, or a derivative block is not bounded between the selected spaces.
assumptions_latex: \(X_1,X_2,Y_1,Y_2\) are Banach spaces with product norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No mesh- and regularization-independent local semismooth Newton estimate follows in the stated norms.

notation.meaning: Selected generalized derivative of the mixed residual.
Solution of the regularized mixed system.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semismoothness transfer for the first complementarity residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local remainder bounds and order-semismoothness transfer for a composed function-space residual on Lp.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the stated operator hypothesis with r=p, fix \widehat u\in L^p(\Omega), and define N,\widehat Z,\Phi_1 as in the associated complementarity construction. There is an open neighborhood V_p(\widehat u) on which G_{p,p} is Lipschitz with some modulus L_p>0 and \widehat Z_{p,2} is continuously Fréchet differentiable. For u,u+d\in V_p(\widehat u), set z=\widehat Z(u) and s=\widehat Z(u+d)-\widehat Z(u). Whenever M_{\Phi_1}(u+d)=I+M_N(\widehat Z(u+d))\widehat Z'_{p,2}(u+d), with the two operators selected from the corresponding generalized differentials, one has \|\Phi_1(u+d)-\Phi_1(u)-M_{\Phi_1}(u+d)d\|_2\leq\|N(z+s)-N(z)-M_N(z+s)s\|_2+\|\widehat Z(u+d)-\widehat Z(u)-\widehat Z'_{p,2}(u+d)d\|_2 and \|s\|_p\leq L_{\widehat Z}\|d\|_p, where L_{\widehat Z}=\|\sigma\lambda-1\|_\infty+\|\sigma\|_\infty L_p. Consequently \Phi_1 is semismooth on V_p(\widehat u). Moreover, for \alpha>0, if N is semismooth of order \alpha at \widehat Z(u) and G_{p,2} is semismooth of order \alpha at u, then \Phi_1 is semismooth of order \alpha at u.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally, the residual Phi1 inherits semismoothness from the negative-part map and the smooth or semismooth inner operator. Its linearization remainder is bounded by the two component remainders, and the inner increment is Lipschitz in the Lp norm.
assumptions_latex: F\ \text{satisfies the stated operator assumption with }r=p
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi_1\ \text{is semismooth on }V_p(\widehat u);\quad [N\ \text{and }G_{p,2}\ \text{are order-}\alpha\text{ semismooth at the corresponding points}]\Rightarrow[\Phi_1\ \text{is order-}\alpha\text{ semismooth at }u].

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between the complementarity problem, two pointwise-minimum residual equations, and an auxiliary Lp equation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Algorithmic mesh independence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General definition for algorithms applied to increasingly accurate finite-dimensional discretizations, with q-superlinear convergence as an illustrative rate-preservation case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathrm P)\) be an infinite-dimensional problem with algorithm \(A\), let \((\mathrm P_h)_{h>0}\) be finite-dimensional approximations whose accuracy increases as \(h\to0\), and let \(A_h\) be corresponding discrete algorithms. From corresponding initial points \(x^0\) and \(x_h^0\), suppose \(A\) and \(A_h\) generate \((x^k)\) and \((x_h^k)\). Mesh independence means that the convergence behavior of the discrete iterates approaches that of the infinite-dimensional iterates as \(h\to0\). In particular, if \(A\) is q-superlinearly convergent on a \(\delta\)-neighborhood of a solution, mesh independence entails that, for all sufficiently small \(h\), \(A_h\) has the same convergence rate on a \(\delta\)-neighborhood of the corresponding discrete solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an infinite-dimensional problem and a family of increasingly accurate finite-dimensional discretizations, an algorithm is mesh independent when the convergence behavior of its discrete versions increasingly matches that of the original algorithm as the mesh is refined. Thus, for example, local q-superlinear convergence on a fixed-radius neighborhood is inherited by sufficiently fine discrete problems on the corresponding neighborhoods.
assumptions_latex: (\mathrm P_h)\text{ is a finite-dimensional approximation of }(\mathrm P)
A_h\text{ is the discrete counterpart of }A
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{convbeh}(x_h^k)\to\operatorname{convbeh}(x^k)\text{ as }h\to0;\quad \text{in particular, q-superlinear convergence of }A\text{ on }B_\delta(x^*)\Rightarrow \exists h_0>0\ \forall h\in(0,h_0):A_h\text{ has the same rate on }B_\delta(x_h^*).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semismoothness transfer for the normalized complementarity residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Lipschitz, remainder, and order-semismoothness estimates for the second function-space residual on L2.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the stated operator hypothesis with r=2, fix \widehat u\in U=L^2(\Omega), and define N,Z,\Phi_2 as in the associated complementarity construction. If G is Lipschitz with modulus L on an open neighborhood V(\widehat u), then Z is Lipschitz there with constant \|1/\lambda\|_\infty L\leq L/\lambda_0, and Z_{2,2} is continuously Fréchet differentiable. For u,u+d\in V(\widehat u), set z=Z(u) and s=Z(u+d)-Z(u). Whenever M_{\Phi_2}(u+d)=I+M_N(Z(u+d))Z'_{2,2}(u+d), with the two operators selected from the corresponding generalized differentials, one has \|\Phi_2(u+d)-\Phi_2(u)-M_{\Phi_2}(u+d)d\|_2\leq\|N(z+s)-N(z)-M_N(z+s)s\|_2+\|Z(u+d)-Z(u)-Z'_{2,2}(u+d)d\|_2 and \|s\|_2\leq\|1/\lambda\|_\infty L\|d\|_2\leq(L/\lambda_0)\|d\|_2. Consequently \Phi_2 is semismooth on V(\widehat u). Moreover, for \alpha>0, if G_{2,2} is semismooth of order \alpha at u and N is semismooth of order \alpha at Z(u), then \Phi_2 is semismooth of order \alpha at u.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an L2 neighborhood where G is Lipschitz, the normalized inner map Z is Lipschitz with constant at most L divided by lambda0. The residual Phi2 has a componentwise remainder bound and inherits semismoothness, including its order, from N and G.
assumptions_latex: F\ \text{satisfies the stated operator assumption with }r=2
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Lip}(Z;V(\widehat u))\leq\|1/\lambda\|_\infty L\leq L/\lambda_0,\quad \Phi_2\ \text{is semismooth on }V(\widehat u),\quad [G_{2,2},N\ \text{are order-}\alpha\text{ semismooth}]\Rightarrow[\Phi_2\ \text{is order-}\alpha\text{ semismooth at }u].

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Semismoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform semismoothness of a family of discretized residual mappings at corresponding solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an index set \(H\), let \(F_h:X_h\to Y_h\), let \(x_h^*\) satisfy \(F_h(x_h^*)=0\), and let \(\mathcal D_h(x)\) be a nonempty set of admissible generalized derivatives. The family is uniformly semismooth at \((x_h^*)_{h\in H}\) if there exist \(r>0\) and a modulus \(\omega:[0,r]\to[0,\infty)\), independent of \(h\), with \(\omega(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that for every \(h\in H\), \(0<\lVert d\rVert_{X_h}\le r\), and \(M\in\mathcal D_h(x_h^*+d)\), \[\lVert F_h(x_h^*+d)-F_h(x_h^*)-Md\rVert_{Y_h}\le \omega(\lVert d\rVert_{X_h})\lVert d\rVert_{X_h}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete family is uniformly semismooth when one mesh-independent modulus bounds every admissible linearization remainder near the corresponding solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(X_h\) and \(Y_h\) are normed spaces for every \(h\in H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The semismoothness remainder is \(o(\lVert d\rVert_{X_h})\) uniformly over \(h\in H\).

notation.meaning: Admissible generalized derivatives of the discrete residual.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \bar u_h\in L^2(\Omega) be a solution of \mathrm{CP}(F_h), and let \bar z_h=Z(\bar u_h). For \omega\in\Omega, the following are equivalent: \bar u_h satisfies strict complementarity at \omega; \widehat Z_h(\bar u_h)(\omega)\neq0; and Z_h(\bar u_h)(\omega)\neq0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a discrete complementarity solution, strict complementarity at a point is equivalent to nonvanishing of each of the two stated complementarity transforms at that point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{SC}(\bar u_h,\omega)\iff \widehat Z_h(\bar u_h)(\omega)\neq0\iff Z_h(\bar u_h)(\omega)\neq0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise estimates for the remainder term defined in equation (6.19), used in uniform-semismoothness analysis.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform local assumptions for mesh-independent semismoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution consistency and mesh-uniform structural, Lipschitz, and derivative-continuity conditions across a discretization family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume there exist \(h_0>0\), \(\delta_0\in(0,1]\), \(p>2\), \(\lambda_0>0\), \(L_G>0\), \(C_{G'}>0\), and \(\kappa>0\), with the specified \(r\geq2\), such that: \(\bar u=\bar u_0\) solves \(CP(F)\), and \(\bar u_h\) solves \(CP(F_h)\) for every \(h\in\mathcal H\), \(h\leq h_0\); \[\|\bar u_h-\bar u\|_{L^2}\to0,\qquad \|G_h(\bar u_h)-G(\bar u)\|_{L^p}\to0\quad\text{as }\mathcal H\ni h\to0;\] Assumption 6.18 holds for every \(h\in\mathcal H\cup\{0\}\), \(h\leq h_0\), with \(\lambda_0\) and \(r\) independent of \(h\); and, for every such \(h\) and every \(u_h\in B_{h,\delta_0}(\bar u_h):=\{v_h\in U_h:\|v_h-\bar u_h\|_{L^2}<\delta_0\}\), \[\|G_h(u_h)-G_h(\bar u_h)\|_{L^p}\leq L_G\|u_h-\bar u_h\|_{L^2},\] \[\|[G_h]'_{r,2}(u_h)-[G_h]'_{r,2}(\bar u_h)\|_{L^r,L^2}\leq C_{G'}\|u_h-\bar u_h\|_{L^r}^{\kappa}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assume continuous and discrete complementarity solutions are consistent as the mesh is refined, the nonlinear operator values converge in L-p, the structural operator conditions hold uniformly in the mesh, and the nonlinear terms satisfy mesh-uniform local L2-to-Lp Lipschitz and Lr-to-L2 derivative Hölder bounds.
assumptions_latex: \bar u=\bar u_0\text{ solves }CP(F),\qquad \bar u_h\text{ solves }CP(F_h)\quad(h\in\mathcal H,\ h\leq h_0)
\|\bar u_h-\bar u\|_{L^2}\to0,\qquad\|G_h(\bar u_h)-G(\bar u)\|_{L^p}\to0\quad(\mathcal H\ni h\to0)
\text{Assumption 6.18 holds for }h\in\mathcal H\cup\{0\},\ h\leq h_0,\text{ with }\lambda_0,r\text{ independent of }h
\|G_h(u_h)-G_h(\bar u_h)\|_{L^p}\leq L_G\|u_h-\bar u_h\|_{L^2}\quad\forall u_h\in B_{h,\delta_0}(\bar u_h)
\|[G_h]'_{r,2}(u_h)-[G_h]'_{r,2}(\bar u_h)\|_{L^r,L^2}\leq C_{G'}\|u_h-\bar u_h\|_{L^r}^{\kappa}\quad\forall u_h\in B_{h,\delta_0}(\bar u_h)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{This solution-consistency and uniform local-regularity package is assumed across the discretization family.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural assumptions for discretized semismooth operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator decomposition and regularity conditions used in mesh-independent semismoothness analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_h\subset L^2(\Omega)\) and \(F_h:U_h\to U_h\). Assume that \[F_h(u_h)=\lambda_hu_h+G_h(u_h),\] where \(\lambda_h\in L^\infty(\Omega)\) satisfies \(\lambda_h\geq\lambda_0\) for a constant \(\lambda_0>0\), and, for some \(p\in(2,\infty]\), \(G_h:U_h\to U_h\cap L^p(\Omega)\) is locally Lipschitz continuous. For the specified \(r\geq2\), also assume that \(G_h:U_h\cap L^r(\Omega)\to U_h\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The discretized operator is assumed to be the sum of a uniformly positive multiplication term and a locally Lipschitz term whose values have higher integrability. On the specified L-r domain, the latter term is also continuously Fréchet differentiable.
assumptions_latex: p\in(2,\infty],\qquad G_h:U_h\to U_h\cap L^p(\Omega)\text{ is locally Lipschitz continuous}
r\geq2\text{ as specified},\qquad G_h:U_h\cap L^r(\Omega)\to U_h\text{ is continuously Fréchet differentiable}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{These are imposed structural and regularity conditions on }F_h\text{ and }G_h.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Growth Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-type semismoothness remainder with mesh-independent exponent, constant, and neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The family \((F_h,\mathcal D_h,x_h^*)_{h\in H}\) is in the uniform-growth regime of order \(1+\alpha\) if there exist \(\alpha\in(0,1]\), \(C>0\), and \(r>0\), all independent of \(h\), such that for every \(h\in H\), every \(d\) with \(\lVert d\rVert_{X_h}\le r\), and every \(M\in\mathcal D_h(x_h^*+d)\), \[\lVert F_h(x_h^*+d)-F_h(x_h^*)-Md\rVert_{Y_h}\le C\lVert d\rVert_{X_h}^{1+\alpha}.\] Thus uniform semismoothness holds with the common modulus \(\omega(t)=Ct^\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common power, constant, and radius bound all discrete linearization remainders, yielding uniform semismoothness.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D_h(x)\) is nonempty in the stated neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is uniformly semismooth with modulus \(\omega(t)=Ct^\alpha\).

notation.meaning: Mesh-independent remainder constant and neighborhood radius.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniform-Growth Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mesh-uniform semismoothness obtained despite mesh-dependent power-growth parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that for each \(h\in H\) there are \(C_h>0\), \(r_h>0\), and \(\alpha_h\in(0,1]\) giving a local bound \(\lVert R_h(d,M)\rVert_{Y_h}\le C_h\lVert d\rVert_{X_h}^{1+\alpha_h}\), where \(R_h(d,M)=F_h(x_h^*+d)-F_h(x_h^*)-Md\). The family is in the nonuniform-growth, mesh-uniform regime when no common positive lower bound on \(\alpha_h\), nor common upper bound on \(C_h\), is assumed, but there still exist \(r>0\) and \(\omega(t)\downarrow0\), independent of \(h\), such that \[\sup_{\substack{0<\lVert d\rVert_{X_h}\le t\\M\in\mathcal D_h(x_h^*+d)}}\frac{\lVert R_h(d,M)\rVert_{Y_h}}{\lVert d\rVert_{X_h}}\le\omega(t),\qquad 0<t\le r.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Meshwise power estimates may deteriorate, yet a separate common little-o modulus can still establish uniform semismoothness.
assumptions_latex: \(F_h(x_h^*)=0\) and the meshwise remainder bounds hold.
The displayed suprema are finite for \(0<t\le r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform semismoothness holds although the meshwise power-growth parameters are not uniform.
review_flags: The intended distinction from the growth-free regime is taxonomy-specific.
REQUEST_SOURCES: mesh-independence result with nonuniform growth parameters required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The common little-o modulus is mathematically sufficient for uniform semismoothness, but no evidence supports this named regime or its intended distinction from the growth-free sibling.

children.title: Growth-Free Regime
children.top_down_role: Mesh-independent semismoothness without growth conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Growth-Free Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential mesh-uniform semismoothness stated without any power or prescribed growth model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_h(d,M)=F_h(x_h^*+d)-F_h(x_h^*)-Md\). The family is in the growth-free regime if, for every sequence \(h_k\in H\), every \(d_k\in X_{h_k}\) with \(0<\lVert d_k\rVert_{X_{h_k}}\to0\), and every \(M_k\in\mathcal D_{h_k}(x_{h_k}^*+d_k)\), \[\frac{\lVert R_{h_k}(d_k,M_k)\rVert_{Y_{h_k}}}{\lVert d_k\rVert_{X_{h_k}}}\longrightarrow0.\] No estimate of the form \(C\lVert d\rVert^{1+\alpha}\), and no preassigned remainder-growth modulus, is included in the hypothesis. The sequential condition is the direct mesh-uniform semismoothness requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every vanishing sequence of discrete steps has a vanishing normalized remainder, with no power-growth assumption.
assumptions_latex: \(F_h:X_h\to Y_h\), \(F_h(x_h^*)=0\), and \(\mathcal D_h\) is locally nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normalized generalized linearization remainder converges to zero along every mesh-step sequence.

notation.meaning: Arbitrary admissible mesh, step, and derivative sequence.
