knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Growth Convergence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform local Newton convergence derived from uniform power-growth and inverse bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the uniform-growth remainder estimate of order \(1+\alpha\) holds with constants \(C,r\), and every \(M\in\mathcal D_h(x)\) for \(\lVert x-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}\le r\) is invertible with \(\lVert M^{-1}\rVert\le\kappa\), uniformly in \(h\). For the Newton update \(x_h^+=x_h-M^{-1}F_h(x_h)\), there is a mesh-independent radius \(\rho\in(0,r]\) such that, whenever \(\lVert x_h-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}\le\rho\), \[\lVert x_h^+-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}\le\kappa C\lVert x_h-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}^{1+\alpha}.\] Consequently, iterations initialized in this ball remain local and converge with mesh-independent order at least \(1+\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform power remainders and uniformly bounded inverse Newton derivatives give a common convergence neighborhood and order.
assumptions_latex: The uniform-growth condition holds with \(\alpha\in(0,1]\), \(C>0\), and \(r>0\).
All selected local Newton derivatives are invertible with inverse norm at most \(\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x_h^+-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}\le\kappa C\lVert x_h-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}^{1+\alpha}\) on a mesh-independent neighborhood.

notation.meaning: Uniform bound on inverse Newton derivatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniform-Growth Convergence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform superlinear convergence based on a common little-o remainder despite nonuniform power parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the nonuniform-growth regime supplies a mesh-independent modulus \(\omega(t)\to0\), and every selected derivative \(M\in\mathcal D_h(x)\) in a common neighborhood of \(x_h^*\) is invertible with \(\lVert M^{-1}\rVert\le\kappa\). Then the Newton update \(x_h^+=x_h-M^{-1}F_h(x_h)\) satisfies \[\lVert x_h^+-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}\le\kappa\omega(\lVert x_h-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h})\lVert x_h-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}.\] Hence a mesh-independent radius can be chosen so that the iteration is locally convergent, and the error quotient tends to zero uniformly in \(h\), even though meshwise power-growth constants or exponents need not be uniform.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common little-o remainder and uniform inverse bound yield mesh-independent superlinear convergence despite deteriorating meshwise power estimates.
assumptions_latex: The nonuniform-growth condition holds with a common modulus \(\omega\).
Selected Newton derivatives have uniformly bounded inverses on a common neighborhood.
Newton iterates remain in that neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Newton error quotient is bounded by \(\kappa\omega(\lVert x_h-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h})\) and tends to zero uniformly in \(h\).
review_flags: The theorem follows the abstract Newton estimate, but the named nonuniform-growth regime needs authoritative identification.
REQUEST_SOURCES: mesh-independent nonuniform-growth convergence theorem required.

children.title: Growth-Free Convergence Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Growth-Free Convergence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential mesh-independent superlinear convergence without a quantitative remainder-growth hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the growth-free sequential remainder condition and a common neighborhood in which every selected \(M\in\mathcal D_h(x)\) is invertible with \(\lVert M^{-1}\rVert\le\kappa\). Consider any sequence of meshes and Newton iterates \((h_k,x_k)\) with \(e_k=x_k-x_{h_k}^*\to0\), and choose \(M_k\in\mathcal D_{h_k}(x_k)\). For \(x_k^+=x_k-M_k^{-1}F_{h_k}(x_k)\), \[\frac{\lVert x_k^+-x_{h_k}^*\rVert_{X_{h_k}}}{\lVert e_k\rVert_{X_{h_k}}}\longrightarrow0.\] Thus local Newton convergence is mesh-uniformly superlinear in the sequential sense, although no power order or prescribed growth modulus is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct sequential remainder condition and a uniform inverse bound imply sequentially mesh-uniform superlinear Newton convergence without a rate model.
assumptions_latex: The growth-free remainder condition holds at \((x_h^*)_{h\in H}\).
Selected Newton derivatives have inverse norm at most \(\kappa\) in a common neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x_k^+-x_{h_k}^*\rVert_{X_{h_k}}/\lVert e_k\rVert_{X_{h_k}}\to0\).

children.title: Mesh-Dependent Convergence
children.top_down_role: Deterioration of local convergence behavior under mesh refinement.

knowledge_statements.title: Mesh-Dependent Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure to admit a common local convergence radius and uniformly vanishing Newton error quotient under refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a family of mesh indices, let \(T_h:X_h\to X_h\) be a semismooth Newton update, and let \(x_h^*\in X_h\) satisfy \(T_h(x_h^*)=x_h^*\). Local convergence is mesh-independent if there exist \(r>0\) and \(q:(0,r]\to[0,\infty)\), both independent of \(h\), with \(q(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that for every \(h\in H\) and every \(x\in X_h\) with \(0<\lVert x-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}\le r\), \[\lVert T_h(x)-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}\le q(\lVert x-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h})\lVert x-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}.\] Local convergence is mesh-dependent when no such common pair \((r,q)\) exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence is mesh-dependent when no positive mesh-independent neighborhood admits a common Newton error-quotient bound that vanishes as the error tends to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(X_h\) is a normed space for each \(h\in H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No mesh-independent radius and uniformly vanishing local error-quotient bound exist for the family \((T_h)_{h\in H}\).

notation.meaning: Family of mesh or discretization indices.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Discrete Activity Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of discrete active regions to converge to the function-space active region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s=\psi-y\) be the continuous slack and \(s_h=\psi_h-y_h\) its discrete counterpart on a common measure space \(\Omega\). Define \(A=\{\xi\in\Omega:s(\xi)=0\}\) and \(A_h=\{\xi\in\Omega:s_h(\xi)\le\tau_h\}\), where \(\tau_h\downarrow0\) is the discrete activity tolerance. A continuous-discrete activity mismatch persists if \[\limsup_{h\to0}\mu(A_h\mathbin{\triangle}A)>0.\] Such a mismatch prevents active-set indicators from converging in \(L^1(\Omega)\), because \(\lVert\mathbf1_{A_h}-\mathbf1_A\rVert_{L^1}=\mu(A_h\mathbin{\triangle}A)\), and can invalidate transfer of continuous generalized-derivative structure to discrete Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activity mismatch persists when the symmetric-difference measure between discrete and continuous active regions does not vanish.
assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu)\) is a finite measure space.
The continuous and discrete slacks have measurable representatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The discrete activity indicators do not converge to the continuous indicator in \(L^1(\Omega)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Mesh-Dependent Newton Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded inverse norms or condition numbers of selected discrete Newton operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_h\in\mathcal D_h(x_h)\) be the Newton operator selected near a discrete solution, represented in norms \(X_h\to Y_h\). Newton conditioning is mesh-dependent along a refining sequence if either some \(M_h\) is singular or \[\sup_{h}\lVert M_h\rVert_{X_h\to Y_h}\lVert M_h^{-1}\rVert_{Y_h\to X_h}=\infty.\] In particular, if \(\lVert M_h\rVert\) remains bounded while \(\lVert M_h^{-1}\rVert\to\infty\), residual perturbations \(\delta r_h\) may produce corrections satisfying \(\lVert\delta x_h\rVert_{X_h}\le\lVert M_h^{-1}\rVert\lVert\delta r_h\rVert_{Y_h}\) with an amplification factor diverging under refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Newton conditioning deteriorates when selected discrete derivatives become singular or their normwise condition numbers grow without bound as the mesh is refined.
assumptions_latex: \(M_h:X_h\to Y_h\) is a bounded linear selected Newton operator.
The norms used to compare conditioning are fixed consistently across the discrete family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is no mesh-independent bound on the conditioning of the selected Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity and quadratic convexity inequalities for the regularized objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural inequalities for the regularized objective on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If Assumptions 8.1, 8.11, and 8.14 hold, then for every \(z_1,z_2\in Z_f\), \[\left\langle J_\gamma'(z_1)-J_\gamma'(z_2),z_1-z_2\right\rangle_{Z^*,Z}\geq\alpha\lVert z_1-z_2\rVert_Z^2.\] Consequently, for every \(z_1,z_2\in Z_f\), \[J_\gamma(z_1)-J_\gamma(z_2)\geq\left\langle J_\gamma'(z_2),z_1-z_2\right\rangle_{Z^*,Z}+\frac{\alpha}{2}\lVert z_1-z_2\rVert_Z^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumptions 8.1, 8.11, and 8.14, the derivative of the regularized objective satisfies the stated alpha-monotonicity inequality on Z_f. The objective consequently satisfies the corresponding quadratic convexity inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left\langle J_\gamma'(z_1)-J_\gamma'(z_2),z_1-z_2\right\rangle_{Z^*,Z}\geq\alpha\lVert z_1-z_2\rVert_Z^2,\quad J_\gamma(z_1)-J_\gamma(z_2)\geq\left\langle J_\gamma'(z_2),z_1-z_2\right\rangle_{Z^*,Z}+\frac{\alpha}{2}\lVert z_1-z_2\rVert_Z^2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Standing assumptions for the state-constrained function-space problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Problem-setting assumptions supporting the state-constrained regularization and Newton analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \Omega\subset\mathbb R^d be a bounded open domain with sufficiently regular boundary. Let b\in Y_0, where Y_0\hookrightarrow L^2(\Omega) is Banach and \max\{0,v\}\in Y_0 for every v\in Y_0. Let Y\hookrightarrow Y_0 be reflexive with compact embedding Y\hookrightarrow L^2(\Omega), and let U be Hilbert. Let W be reflexive, A\in\mathcal L(Y,W), B\in\mathcal L(U,W), f\in W, and suppose C(y,u)=(Ay-Bu,y):Y\times U\to W\times Y is surjective. Assume either Y_0=Y or \exists\widetilde y\in Y\cap\operatorname{int}_{Y_0}\{y\in Y_0:y\le b\}. Let J\in C^2(Y\times U;\mathbb R). Writing Z=Y\times U, suppose \exists\alpha>0 such that \langle J'(z_1)-J'(z_2),z_1-z_2\rangle_{Z^*,Z}\ge\alpha\|z_1-z_2\|_Z^2 whenever z_i=(y_i,u_i) and Ay_i-Bu_i=f for i=1,2. Finally, J' is bounded on bounded subsets of Z.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The state-constrained problem is posed on the stated Banach and Hilbert spaces with compact embedding, a surjective block operator, an interior-feasibility alternative, and a twice continuously differentiable objective whose derivative is strongly monotone on the state-equation set and bounded on bounded sets.
assumptions_latex: \Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\text{ is bounded and open with sufficiently regular boundary}
b\in Y_0\hookrightarrow L^2(\Omega),\quad v\in Y_0\Rightarrow\max\{0,v\}\in Y_0
Y\hookrightarrow Y_0\text{ is reflexive},\quad Y\hookrightarrow L^2(\Omega)\text{ is compact},\quad U\text{ is Hilbert}
W\text{ is reflexive},\quad A\in\mathcal L(Y,W),\quad B\in\mathcal L(U,W),\quad f\in W
C(y,u)=(Ay-Bu,y):Y\times U\to W\times Y\text{ is surjective}
J'\text{ is bounded on bounded subsets of }Z
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{These are the standing assumptions for the state-constrained problem.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Decay Estimates for State-Constraint Violation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty-parameter estimates for the positive state-constraint violation in regularized problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume 8.1, 8.11, 8.14, and 8.23, and let \bar z=(\bar y,\bar u) and z_\gamma=(y_\gamma,u_\gamma), \gamma>0, be the unique solutions of (8.1) and (8.9). For v_\gamma^+=\max\{y_\gamma-b,0\},
\[
\|v_\gamma^+\|_{L^{1+\theta}}^{1+\theta}\le \frac{\langle J'(\bar z),\bar z-z_\gamma\rangle_{Z^*,Z}+\sigma\|y_\gamma-\bar y\|_{L^1}}{c_{\phi1}\gamma^\theta}
=O\!\left(\gamma^{-\theta}\|z_\gamma-\bar z\|_Z\right)=o(\gamma^{-\theta}).
\]
If additionally r\in[1+\theta,\infty], p>rd/(r+d), with rd/(r+d)=d when r=\infty, and v_\gamma^+\in Y_0 is uniformly bounded in W^{1,p}(\Omega), then, for
\[
\tau=\frac{pd(r-1-\theta)}{prd+(1+\theta)r(p-d)},
\]
there is C>0 such that
\[
\|v_\gamma^+\|_{L^r}\le C\|v_\gamma^+\|_{W^{1,p}}^\tau\|v_\gamma^+\|_{L^{1+\theta}}^{1-\tau}
=O\!\left(\gamma^{-\frac{\theta(1-\tau)}{1+\theta}}\|z_\gamma-\bar z\|_Z^{\frac{1-\tau}{1+\theta}}\right)
=o\!\left(\gamma^{-\frac{\theta(1-\tau)}{1+\theta}}\right)
\]
as \gamma\to\infty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumptions 8.1, 8.11, 8.14, and 8.23, the positive state-constraint violation has an L^(1+theta) estimate that is little-o of gamma^(-theta). If it is also uniformly bounded in the stated Sobolev space, interpolation gives the stated L^r estimate and its corresponding little-o decay rate.
assumptions_latex: \bar z\text{ and }z_\gamma\text{ are the unique solutions of (8.1) and (8.9).}
\text{For the second estimate: }r\in[1+\theta,\infty],\ p>rd/(r+d),\ v_\gamma^+\in Y_0,\ \sup_\gamma\|v_\gamma^+\|_{W^{1,p}}<\infty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|v_\gamma^+\|_{L^{1+\theta}}^{1+\theta}=O(\gamma^{-\theta}\|z_\gamma-\bar z\|_Z)=o(\gamma^{-\theta}),\quad \|v_\gamma^+\|_{L^r}=O\!\left(\gamma^{-\frac{\theta(1-\tau)}{1+\theta}}\|z_\gamma-\bar z\|_Z^{\frac{1-\tau}{1+\theta}}\right)=o\!\left(\gamma^{-\frac{\theta(1-\tau)}{1+\theta}}\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Refined Regularization Error Estimate Under Multiplier Decay
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A multiplier-conditioned refinement of the state-constrained regularization error estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Assumptions 8.1, 8.11, 8.14, 8.23, 8.29, and 8.33 hold. Let \(\bar z=(\bar y,\bar u)\) and \(z_\gamma=(y_\gamma,u_\gamma)\), \(\gamma>0\), denote the unique solutions of (8.1) and (8.9), respectively. Suppose that there exist \(\eta>\theta/(1+\theta)\) and \(\rho_\eta>0\) such that \[\|v_\gamma^+\|_{L^{1+\theta}}\le \rho_\eta\gamma^{-\eta}\qquad\text{for all }\gamma>0.\] Set \[\tau=\frac{pd(r-1-\theta)}{prd+(1+\theta)r(p-d)}.\] Then, for a suitable constant \(C>0\), \[\|z_\gamma-\bar z\|_Z\le C\left[\alpha^{-\frac1{2-\kappa}}\gamma^{\frac{\kappa-1}{2-\kappa}}+\alpha^{-\frac12}\gamma^{-\frac12}+\alpha^{-\frac12}\rho_\eta^{\frac{(1-\tau)(1+\theta)}{2(2\theta+\tau+1)}}\gamma^{-\frac{(1-\tau)(\theta+\eta(1+\theta))}{2(2\theta+\tau+1)}}\right].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the cited assumptions and the stated decay bound on the positive multiplier component, the unique state-constrained and regularized solutions satisfy the displayed refined three-term error estimate.
assumptions_latex: \bar z=(\bar y,\bar u)\text{ is the unique solution of (8.1).}
z_\gamma=(y_\gamma,u_\gamma)\text{ is the unique solution of (8.9) for }\gamma>0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists C>0:\quad \|z_\gamma-\bar z\|_Z\le C\left[\alpha^{-\frac1{2-\kappa}}\gamma^{\frac{\kappa-1}{2-\kappa}}+\alpha^{-\frac12}\gamma^{-\frac12}+\alpha^{-\frac12}\rho_\eta^{\frac{(1-\tau)(1+\theta)}{2(2\theta+\tau+1)}}\gamma^{-\frac{(1-\tau)(\theta+\eta(1+\theta))}{2(2\theta+\tau+1)}}\right]\quad(\gamma>0).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong gradient monotonicity implies uniform convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-convexity inequality on the affine state-equation set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Z_f=\{(y,u)\in Y\times U:Ay-Bu=f\}. If J is differentiable and there exists \alpha>0 such that \langle J'(z_1)-J'(z_2),z_1-z_2\rangle_{Z^*,Z}\ge\alpha\|z_1-z_2\|_Z^2 for all z_1,z_2\in Z_f, then for all z_1,z_2\in Z_f,\quad J(z_1)-J(z_2)\ge\langle J'(z_2),z_1-z_2\rangle_{Z^*,Z}+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|z_1-z_2\|_Z^2. knowledge_statements.title: State-Constraint Regularization Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution paths generated by smoothing the complementarity relation for a state inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E(y,u)=0\) be a state equation, let \(G(y,u,\lambda)=0\) collect stationarity equations, and impose the state constraint \(y\le\psi\) with multiplier \(\lambda\ge0\). Define \(\phi_\varepsilon(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2+2\varepsilon^2}-a-b\) for \(\varepsilon>0\), applied pointwise. The state-constraint regularization path is the parameterized solution set \[\mathcal P=\{(\varepsilon,y_\varepsilon,u_\varepsilon,\lambda_\varepsilon):\varepsilon>0,\ E(y_\varepsilon,u_\varepsilon)=0,\ G(y_\varepsilon,u_\varepsilon,\lambda_\varepsilon)=0,\ \phi_\varepsilon(\psi-y_\varepsilon,\lambda_\varepsilon)=0\}.\] A branch is a single-valued selection \(\varepsilon\mapsto(y_\varepsilon,u_\varepsilon,\lambda_\varepsilon)\); any limit as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) is expected to satisfy complementarity only when convergence and closedness are separately established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regularization path consists of state, control, and multiplier solutions obtained by replacing state-constraint complementarity with a parameterized smooth equation.
assumptions_latex: The pointwise expressions are defined in function spaces embedded into measurable functions on the underlying domain.
\(E\) and \(G\) have compatible state, control, multiplier, and residual spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P\) parameterizes the regularized state-constraint systems for \(\varepsilon>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Regularization-Path Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong stability of quadratic state-constraint penalty paths in Hilbert spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U,Y\) be Hilbert spaces, let \(S:U\to Y\) be bounded and linear, and let \(J:U\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, coercive, and strongly convex. Assume \(C=\{u\in U:S u\leq\psi\}\neq\varnothing\), with the inequality understood almost everywhere. For \(\gamma>0\), define
\[
u_\gamma=\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in U}\left[J(u)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\|(S u-\psi)_+\|_Y^2\right].
\]
If \(u_*\) minimizes \(J\) over \(C\), then \(u_\gamma\to u_*\) strongly in \(U\) as \(\gamma\downarrow0\), and \(\|(S u_\gamma-\psi)_+\|_Y=O(\sqrt\gamma)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic-penalty minimizers converge strongly to the unique state-constrained minimizer, while their state-constraint violation is at most order square root of the penalty parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, coercive, and strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_\gamma\to u_*\) strongly and \(\|(S u_\gamma-\psi)_+\|_Y=O(\sqrt\gamma)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Regularization Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel dual form of the quadratic positive-part state penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y=L^2(\Omega)\), let \(g\in Y\), and let \(Y_+=\{\mu\in Y:\mu\geq0\text{ a.e.}\}\). For every \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\frac{1}{2\gamma}\|g_+\|_Y^2
=
\sup_{\mu\in Y_+}\left\{\langle\mu,g\rangle_Y-\frac{\gamma}{2}\|\mu\|_Y^2\right\}.
\]
The supremum is attained uniquely at \(\mu_\gamma=\gamma^{-1}g_+\). Consequently, for \(g=S u-\psi\), quadratic state-constraint regularization is equivalent to adding a dual variable constrained by \(\mu\geq0\) and penalizing its squared norm by \(\gamma/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic positive-part penalty is the maximized dual pairing with a nonnegative multiplier minus a quadratic dual regularizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac{1}{2\gamma}\|g_+\|_Y^2=\sup_{\mu\in Y_+}\{\langle\mu,g\rangle_Y-\frac{\gamma}{2}\|\mu\|_Y^2\}\), with \(\mu_\gamma=\gamma^{-1}g_+\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian for a linear-quadratic elliptic boundary-control problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the integrated-by-parts Lagrangian on the state, boundary-control, and adjoint spaces and records its first-order state and control conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the elliptic control problem under consideration, define \(\mathcal L:H^1(\Omega)\times L^2(\Gamma)\times H^1(\Omega)\to\mathbb R\) by
\[
\mathcal L(y,u,p):=J(y,u)-\int_\Omega \nabla y\cdot\nabla p\,dx+\int_\Gamma \alpha(u-y)p\,ds.
\]
At a candidate pair \((\bar y,\bar u)\), the state stationarity condition is
\[
D_y\mathcal L(\bar y,\bar u,p)h=0\quad\forall h\in H^1(\Omega),
\]
and the admissible-control condition
\[
D_u\mathcal L(\bar y,\bar u,p)(u-\bar u)\ge 0\quad\forall u\in U_{ad}
\]
is equivalent to the problem's control variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian equals the objective minus the weak elliptic state term plus the boundary coupling term. Its derivative with respect to the state vanishes in every H¹ direction, while its derivative with respect to the control is nonnegative along every admissible displacement exactly when the control variational inequality holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_y\mathcal L(\bar y,\bar u,p)h=0\ \forall h\in H^1(\Omega),\qquad D_u\mathcal L(\bar y,\bar u,p)(u-\bar u)\ge0\ \forall u\in U_{ad}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \text{the control variational inequality}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adjoint identity for an elliptic Robin boundary-value problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded state–adjoint duality identity for distributed and boundary data in a linear elliptic equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $a_\Omega,v\in L^2(\Omega)$, $a_\Gamma,u\in L^2(\Gamma)$, $c_0,\beta_\Omega\in L^\infty(\Omega)$, and $\alpha,\beta_\Gamma\in L^\infty(\Gamma)$, with $c_0\geq0$ almost everywhere in $\Omega$ and $\alpha\geq0$ almost everywhere on $\Gamma$. Let $y$ and $p$ be weak solutions of
\[
-\Delta y+c_0y=\beta_\Omega v,\qquad \partial_\nu y+\alpha y=\beta_\Gamma u,
\]
and
\[
-\Delta p+c_0p=a_\Omega,\qquad \partial_\nu p+\alpha p=a_\Gamma,
\]
respectively. Then
\[
\int_\Omega a_\Omega y\,dx+\int_\Gamma a_\Gamma y\,ds
=
\int_\Omega \beta_\Omega pv\,dx+\int_\Gamma \beta_\Gamma pu\,ds.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For weak solutions of the paired elliptic Robin problems, pairing the state with the adjoint data equals pairing the adjoint state with the distributed and boundary inputs.
assumptions_latex: y\ \text{and }p\ \text{are weak solutions of the displayed Robin problems}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \int_\Omega a_\Omega y\,dx+\int_\Gamma a_\Gamma y\,ds=\int_\Omega \beta_\Omega pv\,dx+\int_\Gamma \beta_\Gamma pu\,ds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal–Dual Active-Set Strategy for Box-Constrained Elliptic Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-dimensional active-set realization of the projection optimality condition, interpretable as semismooth Newton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $S:L^2(\Omega)\to L^2(\Omega)$ be the Dirichlet Poisson solution operator and minimize $f(u)=\frac12\|Su-y_\Omega\|_{L^2}^2+\frac\lambda2\|u\|_{L^2}^2$ over $U_{ad}=\{u:u_a\le u\le u_b\ \text{a.e.}\}$. With adjoint $p$ and $\mu=-(\lambda^{-1}p+u)$, optimality is equivalent to $u=P_{[u_a,u_b]}(-\lambda^{-1}p)$. Given arbitrary $u_0,\mu_0\in L^2(\Omega)$, define $A_n^b=\{u_{n-1}+\mu_{n-1}>u_b\}$, $A_n^a=\{u_{n-1}+\mu_{n-1}<u_a\}$, and $I_n=\Omega\setminus(A_n^a\cup A_n^b)$. Solve the coupled state-adjoint-control system with $u=u_a$ on $A_n^a$, $u=u_b$ on $A_n^b$, and $u=-\lambda^{-1}p$ on $I_n$, and set $\mu_n=-(\lambda^{-1}p_n+u_n)$. Terminate when both active sets are unchanged. Replacing $\mu$ by $c\mu$ for $c>0$ leaves the optimal case distinction unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify lower-active, upper-active, and inactive regions using the control plus a multiplier, solve the resulting coupled linear system, and stop when the active sets stabilize. The active-set relations are equivalent to the projection optimality condition, and the method admits a semismooth-Newton interpretation.
assumptions_latex: S\text{ is the solution operator for }-\Delta y=u,\ y|_\Gamma=0
c>0\text{ when multiplier scaling is used}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u=P_{[u_a,u_b]}(-\lambda^{-1}p)\iff\text{the active/inactive relations hold};\quad A_n^a=A_{n-1}^a,\ A_n^b=A_{n-1}^b\Rightarrow u_n\text{ is optimal}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fréchet derivative of a Nemytskii operator on L-infinity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth function-space calculus under first-order boundedness and local Lipschitz assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x\mapsto\varphi(x,s)\) is measurable for every \(s\in\mathbb R\), \(y\mapsto\varphi(x,y)\) is differentiable for almost every \(x\), and the order-one boundedness and local Lipschitz conditions hold: \(|\varphi(x,0)|\) and \(|\varphi_y(x,0)|\) are essentially bounded, and for every \(M>0\) there is \(L(M)>0\) such that \(|\varphi_y(x,s)-\varphi_y(x,t)|\le L(M)|s-t|\) on \([-M,M]\). Then the associated Nemytskii operator \(\Phi\) is Fréchet differentiable on \(L^\infty(E)\), with \((\Phi'(y)h)(x)=\varphi_y(x,y(x))h(x)\) for almost every \(x\in E\) and every \(h\in L^\infty(E)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under first-order boundedness and local Lipschitz assumptions, the Nemytskii operator on L∞ is Fréchet differentiable, and its derivative is pointwise multiplication by φᵧ(x,y(x)).
assumptions_latex: x\mapsto\varphi(x,s)\text{ is measurable for every }s\in\mathbb R
\forall M>0\ \exists L(M)>0:\ |\varphi_y(x,s)-\varphi_y(x,t)|\le L(M)|s-t|\text{ for a.e. }x,\ s,t\in[-M,M]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi:L^\infty(E)\to L^\infty(E)\text{ is Fréchet differentiable},\qquad (\Phi'(y)h)(x)=\varphi_y(x,y(x))h(x)\text{ for a.e. }x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditioned Gradient Method for Box-Constrained Elliptic Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PDE-constrained specialization of conditional gradient using state and adjoint solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For $f(u)=\frac12\|y(u)-y_\Omega\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2+\frac\lambda2\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2$, where $-\Delta y=\beta u$, $y|_\Gamma=0$, and $u_a\le u\le u_b$ a.e., compute $y_n$ and the adjoint $p_n$ satisfying $-\Delta p_n=y_n-y_\Omega$ and $p_n|_\Gamma=0$. Choose $v_n\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in U_{ad}}\int_\Omega(\beta p_n+\lambda u_n)v\,dx$. Terminate if its linearized value does not improve that of $u_n$, or use the stated heuristic tolerance test. Otherwise choose $s_n\in(0,1]$ minimizing $f(u_n+s(v_n-u_n))$ and set $u_{n+1}=u_n+s_n(v_n-u_n)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration solves the state and adjoint equations, minimizes the reduced derivative over the box of admissible controls, performs exact line search along the feasible segment, and updates the control. The positive-tolerance stopping rule is heuristic rather than an exact optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_{n+1}=u_n+s_n(v_n-u_n)\in U_{ad},\qquad s_n\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in(0,1]}f(u_n+s(v_n-u_n)).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary-mean Friedrichs inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An H1 norm estimate using the gradient and the integral over a positive-measure boundary subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^N\) be a bounded Lipschitz domain with boundary \(\Gamma\), and let \(\Gamma_1\subset\Gamma\) be measurable with \(|\Gamma_1|>0\). Then there exists \(c(\Gamma_1)>0\), independent of \(y\), such that \[\|y\|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2\le c(\Gamma_1)\left(\int_\Omega|\nabla y|^2\,dx+\left(\int_{\Gamma_1}y\,ds\right)^2\right)\qquad\forall y\in H^1(\Omega).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bounded Lipschitz domain and a positive-measure boundary subset, the H1 norm is controlled by the gradient energy together with the squared boundary integral over that subset.
assumptions_latex: \Omega\subset\mathbb R^N\text{ is a bounded Lipschitz domain with boundary }\Gamma
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists c(\Gamma_1)>0\ \forall y\in H^1(\Omega):\quad \|y\|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2\le c(\Gamma_1)\left(\int_\Omega|\nabla y|^2\,dx+\left(\int_{\Gamma_1}y\,ds\right)^2\right)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity, local domination, and coercivity assumptions for semilinear elliptic nonlinearities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural assumptions on the interior and boundary nonlinearities used in the semilinear elliptic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\Omega\) and \(\mathcal A\) satisfy Assumption 4.2. For every \(y\in\mathbb R\), \(d(\cdot,y)\) on \(\Omega\) and \(b(\cdot,y)\) on \(\Gamma\) are measurable; for almost every spatial point, they are continuous and monotone increasing in \(y\). For every \(M>0\), there exist \(\psi_M\in L^r(\Omega)\), with \(r>N/2\), and \(\phi_M\in L^s(\Gamma)\), with \(s>N-1\), such that \(|d(x,y)|\le\psi_M(x)\) for a.e. \(x\in\Omega\) and \(|b(x,y)|\le\phi_M(x)\) for a.e. \(x\in\Gamma\) whenever \(|y|\le M\). In addition, either there are \(E_d\subset\Omega\) of positive measure and \(M_d,\lambda_d>0\) such that \(d(x,y_1)<d(x,y_2)\) for all \(x\in E_d\) and \(y_1<y_2\), and \((d(x,y)-d(x,0))y\ge\lambda_d|y|^2\) for all \(x\in E_d\) and \(|y|>M_d\); or there are \(E_b\subset\Gamma\) of positive measure and \(M_b,\lambda_b>0\) satisfying the analogous strict-monotonicity and coercivity conditions for \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonlinearities are spatially measurable, continuous and monotone in the state variable, locally dominated by sufficiently integrable functions, and at least one is strictly increasing and quadratically coercive for large state values on a set of positive measure.
assumptions_latex: \forall y\in\mathbb R,\ d(\cdot,y)\text{ and }b(\cdot,y)\text{ are measurable}
d(x,\cdot)\text{ and }b(x,\cdot)\text{ are continuous and monotone increasing for a.e. }x
\bigl[(i)\text{ interior strict monotonicity and large-state coercivity}\bigr]\lor\bigl[(ii)\text{ boundary strict monotonicity and large-state coercivity}\bigr]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&|d(x,y)|\le\psi_M(x)\ \text{a.e. on }\Omega,\quad |b(x,y)|\le\phi_M(x)\ \text{a.e. on }\Gamma\quad(|y|\le M),\\&\text{and either the stated strict-monotonicity and coercivity conditions hold on }E_d,\\&\text{or their boundary analogues hold on }E_b.\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order differentiability of the semilinear elliptic state operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For the semilinear elliptic state operator E:Y\times U\to W under its standing model hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global and local optimal controls for a reduced PDE-control problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition using the control-to-state map, with local optimality measured in the L^r(Ω) norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_{ad}\) be the admissible-control set and \(y(u)\) the state associated with \(u\). A control \(\bar u\in U_{ad}\), with associated state \(\bar y=y(\bar u)\), is optimal if \[J(y(\bar u),\bar u)\le J(y(u),u)\qquad\forall u\in U_{ad}.\] It is locally optimal in \(L^r(\Omega)\) if there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that the same inequality holds for every \(u\in U_{ad}\) satisfying \(\|u-\bar u\|_{L^r(\Omega)}\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An admissible control is globally optimal when its reduced objective value is no greater than that of every admissible control. It is locally optimal in L^r(Ω) when this comparison holds for all admissible controls within some positive L^r-radius.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J(y(\bar u),\bar u)\le J(y(u),u)\ \forall u\in U_{ad}\quad\text{or locally for all }u\in U_{ad}\text{ with }\|u-\bar u\|_{L^r(\Omega)}\le\varepsilon\text{ for some }\varepsilon>0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Carathéodory, boundedness, and local Lipschitz conditions for a kernel
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measurability, boundedness-at-zero, and scalar-variable regularity conditions used in Nemytskii-operator theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varphi:E\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\): (i) the Carathéodory condition requires \(x\mapsto\varphi(x,y)\) to be measurable for every fixed \(y\), and \(y\mapsto\varphi(x,y)\) to be continuous for almost every fixed \(x\); (ii) the boundedness condition requires some \(K>0\) such that \(|\varphi(x,0)|\le K\) for almost every \(x\in E\); and (iii) local Lipschitz continuity with respect to \(y\) requires that for every \(M>0\) there be \(L(M)>0\) such that \(|\varphi(x,y)-\varphi(x,z)|\le L(M)|y-z|\) for almost every \(x\in E\) and all \(y,z\in[-M,M]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Carathéodory condition combines measurability in x with almost-everywhere continuity in y. The boundedness condition bounds φ(x,0) almost everywhere, while local Lipschitz continuity requires a uniform almost-everywhere Lipschitz bound in y on each bounded interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&x\mapsto\varphi(x,y)\text{ is measurable for every }y,\quad y\mapsto\varphi(x,y)\text{ is continuous for a.e. }x;\\&\exists K>0:\ |\varphi(x,0)|\le K\text{ for a.e. }x;\\&\forall M>0\ \exists L(M)>0:\ |\varphi(x,y)-\varphi(x,z)|\le L(M)|y-z|\text{ for a.e. }x,\ y,z\in[-M,M].\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distributional Costate Equation with a Radon-Measure Source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the measure-driven adjoint equation used by the semilinear elliptic optimal-control system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu\in C_0(\Omega)^*\), a finite signed Radon measure, \(p\in W_0^{1,1}(\Omega)\) solves \[-\Delta p+\phi'(y_u)p=\mu\ \text{ in }\Omega,\qquad p=0\ \text{ on }\partial\Omega\] in the distributional sense if \[\int_\Omega\bigl(-\Delta z+\phi'(y_u)z\bigr)p\,d\omega=\int_\Omega z\,d\mu\qquad\text{for every }z\in\mathcal D(\Omega).\] Since \(\mathcal D(\Omega)\) is dense in \(C_0(\Omega)\), \(-\Delta p\) extends uniquely to \(C_0(\Omega)\) as \(\mu-\phi'(y_u)p\), so the equation also holds in \(C_0(\Omega)^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A W_0^{1,1} costate solves the elliptic adjoint equation with a finite signed Radon-measure right-hand side when it satisfies the stated test-function identity. The Laplacian then has a unique extension to the dual of C_0, where the same equation remains valid.
assumptions_latex: \mu\in C_0(\Omega)^*\text{ is a finite signed Radon measure}
z\in\mathcal D(\Omega)\text{ in the defining identity}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -\Delta p+\phi'(y_u)p=\mu\text{ holds distributionally and, via the unique extension, in }C_0(\Omega)^*.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Well-Posedness of the Measure-Driven Elliptic Costate Equation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to the distributional Dirichlet costate equation \(-\Delta p+\phi'(y_u)p=\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(t\in[1,n/(n-1))\), the measure-driven elliptic equation \[-\Delta p+\phi'(y_u)p=\mu\ \text{ in }\Omega,\qquad p=0\ \text{ on }\partial\Omega\] has a unique solution \(p\in W_0^{1,t}(\Omega)\). Moreover, for each such \(t\) there exists \(c_t>0\) such that \[\|p\|_{W^{1,t}(\Omega)}\le c_t\|\mu\|_{C_0(\Omega)^*}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every exponent from 1 up to but excluding n divided by n minus 1, the elliptic costate equation with Radon-measure data has a unique W_0^{1,t} solution, whose Sobolev norm is bounded linearly by the measure norm.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity, monotonicity, and control-bound assumptions for semilinear elliptic optimal control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assumptions for semilinear elliptic distributed or boundary control, with the control domain E equal to Ω or Γ as appropriate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^N\) be a bounded Lipschitz domain. Let \(d,\varphi:\Omega\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\), \(b:\Gamma\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\), and \(\psi:E\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\), where \(E\in\{\Omega,\Gamma\}\), be measurable in \(x\), twice differentiable in their scalar argument for almost every \(x\), and satisfy the stipulated boundedness and local Lipschitz conditions of order \(2\). In particular, there are \(K>0\) and, for each \(M>0\), \(L(M)>0\) such that \(|\varphi(x,0)|+|\varphi_y(x,0)|+|\varphi_{yy}(x,0)|\le K\) almost everywhere and \(|\varphi_{yy}(x,y_1)-\varphi_{yy}(x,y_2)|\le L(M)|y_1-y_2|\) for all \(y_1,y_2\in[-M,M]\). Assume \(d_y(x,y)\ge0\) for almost every \(x\in\Omega\) and \(b_y(x,y)\ge0\) for almost every \(x\in\Gamma\), for every \(y\in\mathbb R\). Moreover, suppose there exist positive-measure sets \(E_d\subset\Omega\), \(E_b\subset\Gamma\) and constants \(\lambda_d,\lambda_b>0\) such that \(d_y(x,y)\ge\lambda_d\) on \(E_d\times\mathbb R\) and \(b_y(x,y)\ge\lambda_b\) on \(E_b\times\mathbb R\). Finally, let \(u_a,u_b,v_a,v_b\in L^\infty(E)\) satisfy \(u_a\le u_b\) and \(v_a\le v_b\) almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The domain is bounded and Lipschitz; the state, boundary, objective, and control integrands have the stated measurability, twice-differentiability, boundedness, and local Lipschitz properties. The state and boundary nonlinearities are nondecreasing and are uniformly increasing on positive-measure subsets. The control bounds are essentially bounded and ordered almost everywhere.

d,\varphi,b,\psi\text{ are measurable in }x\text{ and twice differentiable in their scalar argument a.e.}
d,\varphi,b,\psi\text{ satisfy the boundedness and local Lipschitz conditions of order }2
d_y(x,y)\ge0\text{ a.e. in }\Omega\text{ and }b_y(x,y)\ge0\text{ a.e. on }\Gamma\text{ for all }y\in\mathbb R
\exists E_d\subset\Omega,E_b\subset\Gamma\text{ of positive measure and }\lambda_d,\lambda_b>0:\ d_y\ge\lambda_d\text{ on }E_d\times\mathbb R,\ b_y\ge\lambda_b\text{ on }E_b\times\mathbb R
u_a,u_b,v_a,v_b\in L^\infty(E),\quad u_a\le u_b,\quad v_a\le v_b\text{ a.e.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distributed and Boundary Hamiltonians for Semilinear Elliptic Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hamiltonian functions for distributed and boundary controls in a semilinear elliptic optimal-control problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

\[
H^{\Omega}(x,y,v,p_{0},p)=p_{0}\varphi(x,y,v)-d(x,y,v)p,

knowledge_statements.title: Black-Box Elliptic Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced semismooth Newton iteration using elliptic state and adjoint solution operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S:U\to Y\) be the bounded linear solution operator of an elliptic state equation, let \(U_{ad}=\{u:a\leq u\leq b\}\), and let \(\alpha>0\). Define \(p(u)=S^*(S u-y_d)\) and
\[
F(u)=u-P_{[a,b]}(-\alpha^{-1}p(u)).
\]
Given \(u^0\), iteration \(k\) evaluates the state \(S u^k\), the adjoint \(p(u^k)\), and a pointwise generalized derivative \(\chi_k\in\partial P_{[a,b]}(-\alpha^{-1}p(u^k))\). It solves
\[
\left(I+\alpha^{-1}\chi_k S^*S\right)\delta u^k=-F(u^k),\qquad u^{k+1}=u^k+\delta u^k,
\]
and stops when \(F(u^k)=0\) within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each reduced Newton step calls black-box state and adjoint solvers, identifies projection activity, and solves the resulting generalized control-space Newton equation.
assumptions_latex: \(S:U\to Y\) is a bounded linear elliptic solution operator.
The selected generalized Newton operator is invertible near the solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies the reduced projection equation \(u=P_{[a,b]}(-\alpha^{-1}S^*(S u-y_d))\) to the prescribed tolerance.

notation.meaning: pointwise projection onto the admissible interval
pointwise generalized derivative of the projection

knowledge_statements.title: All-at-Once Elliptic Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled primal-dual active-set Newton system for box-constrained elliptic control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A y-Bu=f\) be a linear elliptic state equation and consider a quadratic tracking objective with control cost \(\alpha\|u\|^2/2\) and bounds \(a\leq u\leq b\). Retain \(x=(y,p,u,\lambda_a,\lambda_b)\) and impose
\[
Ay-Bu-f=0,\quad A^*p+y-y_d=0,\quad \alpha u+B^*p-\lambda_a+\lambda_b=0,
\]
with \(0\leq u-a\perp\lambda_a\geq0\) and \(0\leq b-u\perp\lambda_b\geq0\). From \(x^k\), choose generalized derivatives of complementarity functions, solve the coupled generalized Jacobian equation \(G_k\delta x^k=-F(x^k)\), update \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\delta x^k\), and stop when the KKT residual meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The all-at-once method Newton-linearizes the state, adjoint, stationarity, and bound-complementarity equations while retaining every primal and dual variable.
assumptions_latex: A nonsingular generalized KKT Jacobian is selected near the solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned variables satisfy the coupled state, adjoint, stationarity, and bound-complementarity system to tolerance.

notation.meaning: selected generalized Jacobian of the coupled KKT residual

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Elliptic Newton Architectures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic equivalence of reduced and all-at-once finite-element Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let conforming finite-element discretization yield
\[
K y-Bu=f,\qquad K^{\mathsf T}p+M(y-y_d)=0,
\]
where \(K\) is nonsingular, and let \(M_u\) be the control mass matrix. Eliminating \(y\) and \(p\) from an all-at-once Newton linearization produces the reduced control Hessian
\[
H_h=\alpha M_u+B^{\mathsf T}K^{-\mathsf T}M K^{-1}B.
\]
For a diagonal free-set mask \(D\), the reduced active-set equation has coefficient \(D H_hD+(I-D)\). Conversely, introducing state and adjoint increments recovers a sparse saddle-point system whose Schur complement in the free control variables is precisely the restriction of \(H_h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-element reduced and all-at-once Newton systems are algebraically equivalent: eliminating state and adjoint variables yields the reduced active-set Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is the nonsingular discrete elliptic operator.
\(M\) and \(M_u\) are symmetric positive definite mass matrices.
\(D\) is the diagonal indicator of free control degrees of freedom.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The free-control Schur complement of the all-at-once system equals the corresponding restriction of \(H_h\).

knowledge_statements.title: Elliptic Newton-System Solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structure-exploiting direct and preconditioned iterative solution of active-set Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), let the elliptic active-set linearization be \(J_k\delta x=-r_k\), with state, adjoint, free-control, and active-control blocks. First eliminate active-control increments using their identity equations. The remaining system may be solved either by block factorization using elliptic solves with \(K\) and \(K^{\mathsf T}\), or by a Krylov method with block preconditioner \(P_k\). If the preconditioned Schur complement satisfies
\[
c\langle P_kv,v\rangle\leq\langle J_kv,v\rangle\leq C\langle P_kv,v\rangle
\]
for constants \(0<c\leq C\) independent of mesh size and the current active set, then the symmetric preconditioned iteration count for a fixed residual reduction is uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate active variables and exploit elliptic block solves; uniform spectral equivalence of the preconditioner gives mesh- and active-set-independent iteration counts.
assumptions_latex: The inactive Newton system is symmetric positive definite, or is reduced to such a Schur complement.
The spectral-equivalence constants are independent of mesh and active set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A fixed relative residual reduction requires a number of preconditioned symmetric Krylov iterations bounded independently of the mesh and active set.

knowledge_statements.title: Obstacle Dual Newton Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-space complementarity equation for a lower-obstacle variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be a Hilbert space, let \(A:V\to V^*\) be bounded, coercive, and invertible, and let \(K=\{y\in V:y\geq\psi\}\). The obstacle variational inequality
\[
\langle Ay-f,v-y\rangle\geq0\qquad\text{for every }v\in K
\]
is equivalent, whenever the pointwise order and multiplier pairing are defined, to
\[
y=A^{-1}(f+\lambda),\qquad y-\psi\geq0,
\quad\lambda\geq0,
\quad\langle\lambda,y-\psi\rangle=0.
\]
Eliminating \(y\) gives the dual nonsmooth equation
\[
\min\{A^{-1}(f+\lambda)-\psi,\lambda\}=0,
\]
where the minimum is pointwise; its generalized Newton derivative selects contact and noncontact regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the obstacle state produces a multiplier-space minimum equation whose generalized derivative identifies contact and noncontact regions.
assumptions_latex: \(A:V\to V^*\) is bounded, coercive, and invertible.
The obstacle cone and dual multiplier cone admit the displayed pointwise complementarity representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The obstacle variational inequality is equivalent to \(\min\{A^{-1}(f+\lambda)-\psi,\lambda\}=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Obstacle Regularized-Dual Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semismooth Newton iteration for a quadratically regularized obstacle multiplier equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:V\to V^*\) be an invertible elliptic operator and let \(\gamma>0\). Define the regularized dual residual
\[
F_\gamma(\lambda)=\lambda-\gamma^{-1}\bigl(\psi-A^{-1}(f+\lambda)\bigr)_+.
\]
Starting from \(\lambda^0\), set \(y^k=A^{-1}(f+\lambda^k)\), choose \(\chi_k(x)\in\partial(\cdot)_+(\psi(x)-y^k(x))\), and solve
\[
\left(I+\gamma^{-1}\chi_kA^{-1}\right)\delta\lambda^k=-F_\gamma(\lambda^k),
\qquad \lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\delta\lambda^k.
\]
Stop when \(\|F_\gamma(\lambda^k)\|\) is below tolerance. The associated state is \(y^k=A^{-1}(f+\lambda^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Newton steps solve a multiplier-space equation formed by the positive-part regularization of obstacle complementarity and repeated elliptic solution.
assumptions_latex: The selected generalized Newton operator is invertible near the regularized solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies \(\lambda=\gamma^{-1}(\psi-A^{-1}(f+\lambda))_+\) to tolerance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing-regularization convergence of dual solutions and their associated obstacle states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\bar u$ and $\bar u_\lambda$ be the solutions of the unregularized dual problem (9.48) and regularized dual problem (9.49), respectively. knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Obstacle Active Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual active-set iteration for a discretized lower-obstacle problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A_hy-f_h-\lambda=0\) be the discrete equilibrium equation, with \(y-\psi_h\geq0\), \(\lambda\geq0\), and \(\lambda_i(y_i-\psi_{h,i})=0\). Given \((y^k,\lambda^k)\) and \(c>0\), define
\[
\mathcal A_k=\{i:\lambda_i^k-c(y_i^k-\psi_{h,i})>0\},
\qquad \mathcal I_k=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\mathcal A_k.
\]
Compute \((y^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1})\) from
\[
A_hy^{k+1}-f_h-\lambda^{k+1}=0,
\quad y_i^{k+1}=\psi_{h,i}\ (i\in\mathcal A_k),
\quad\lambda_i^{k+1}=0\ (i\in\mathcal I_k).
\]
Stop when the active set is unchanged and the residual tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The discrete method predicts contact nodes, fixes the obstacle there, sets multipliers to zero elsewhere, and solves the resulting linear system.
assumptions_latex: \(A_h\) is the discrete coercive obstacle operator.
The active-set linear systems are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, the iterate satisfies discrete equilibrium and obstacle complementarity to tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Element Complementarity Representations of Obstacle Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter-dependent piecewise-linear finite-element representations of rigid- and compliant-obstacle membrane problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\alpha_h\) be the continuous piecewise-linear interpolant of an admissible boundary function and define
\[
\Omega_h(\alpha):=\{(\xi_1,\xi_2)\in\mathbb R^2\mid 0<\xi_2<1,\ 0<\xi_1<\alpha_h(\xi_2)\}.
\]
Using a triangular mesh and continuous piecewise-linear nodal basis functions \(\{\varphi_k\}_{k=1}^m\), assemble
\[
(A_i)^{k\ell}:=\int_{\Omega_i}\nabla\varphi_k\cdot\nabla\varphi_\ell\,d\xi,
\qquad A(\alpha):=\sum_{i=1}^N A_i.
\]
With the parameter-dependent load \(f(\alpha)\) and nodal obstacle \(\chi(\alpha)\), the rigid-obstacle discretization is
\[
A(\alpha)u-f(\alpha)\geq0,
\quad u-\chi(\alpha)\geq0,
\quad\langle A(\alpha)u-f(\alpha),u-\chi(\alpha)\rangle=0.
\]
Equivalently, for \(K(\alpha):=\{y\in\mathbb R^m\mid y\geq\chi(\alpha)\}\),
\[
u\in K(\alpha),\qquad
\langle A(\alpha)u-f(\alpha),y-u\rangle\geq0
\quad\forall y\in K(\alpha).
\]
The change of variables \(v=u-\chi(\alpha)\) gives the fixed-set representation
\[
v\in\mathbb R_+^m,
\qquad\langle A(\alpha)v+A(\alpha)\chi(\alpha)-f(\alpha),y-v\rangle\geq0
\quad\forall y\in\mathbb R_+^m.
\]
For the compliant obstacle, the discretization is
\[
A(\alpha)u-f(\alpha)\geq0,
\quad u-G(\alpha,u)\geq0,
\quad\langle A(\alpha)u-f(\alpha),u-G(\alpha,u)\rangle=0,
\]
where
\[
G(\alpha,u):=k\bigl(f(\alpha)-A(\alpha)u\bigr)+\chi(\alpha).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Piecewise-linear boundary interpolation and triangular linear finite elements yield parameter-dependent stiffness, load, and obstacle data. The rigid-obstacle discretization has equivalent linear-complementarity and variational-inequality forms; shifting by the obstacle moves the feasible set to the fixed nonnegative orthant. The compliant-obstacle discretization is an implicit complementarity problem.
assumptions_latex: \alpha_h\text{ is the continuous piecewise-linear interpolant of an admissible boundary function}
\Omega_h(\alpha)\text{ is triangulated and continuous piecewise-linear nodal basis functions are used}
A(\alpha),f(\alpha),\chi(\alpha)\text{ are the resulting parameter-dependent discrete data}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The rigid-obstacle discretization has equivalent LCP and VI representations, whereas the compliant-obstacle discretization is an ICP.}

knowledge_statements.title: L1 Optimality Equations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soft-thresholding equation for quadratic PDE control with an L1 control penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U=L^2(\Omega)\), let \(S:U\to Y\) be bounded and linear, and consider
\[
\min_{u\in U}\frac12\|S u-y_d\|_Y^2+\frac\alpha2\|u\|_U^2+\beta\|u\|_{L^1(\Omega)},
\qquad \alpha>0,\quad\beta>0.
\]
With \(p=S^*(S u-y_d)\), first-order optimality is
\[
0\in p+\alpha u+\beta\,\partial\|u\|_{L^1(\Omega)}.
\]
Equivalently, almost everywhere,
\[
u=\operatorname{soft}(-\alpha^{-1}p,\beta/\alpha),
\qquad
\operatorname{soft}(z,t)=\operatorname{sign}(z)\max\{|z|-t,0\}.
\]
Thus the optimality system is the semismooth equation \(F(u)=u-\operatorname{soft}(-\alpha^{-1}S^*(S u-y_d),\beta/\alpha)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The L1-regularized PDE control condition is equivalent to a pointwise soft-thresholding fixed-point equation suitable for semismooth Newton iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimality is equivalent to \(u=\operatorname{soft}(-\alpha^{-1}S^*(S u-y_d),\beta/\alpha)\).

children.title: L1 Thresholding Active Sets
children.top_down_role: Active-set interpretations generated by L1 thresholding structure.

knowledge_statements.title: L1 Thresholding Active Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise active-set partition induced by the L1 soft-thresholding equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the optimality equation \(0\in p+\alpha u+\beta\partial|u|\), with \(\alpha,\beta>0\), define
\[
\mathcal A_+=\{x:p(x)<-\beta\},\qquad
\mathcal A_-=\{x:p(x)>\beta\},\qquad
\mathcal I=\{x:|p(x)|\leq\beta\}.
\]
Then, almost everywhere,
\[
u(x)=
\begin{cases}
-(p(x)+\beta)/\alpha,&x\in\mathcal A_+,\\
0,&x\in\mathcal I,\\
-(p(x)-\beta)/\alpha,&x\in\mathcal A_-.
\end{cases}
\]
Away from the threshold sets \(p=\pm\beta\), a generalized derivative of the soft-thresholding map equals one on \(\mathcal A_+\cup\mathcal A_-\) and zero on \(\mathcal I\), furnishing the Newton active-set mask.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjoint values beyond either L1 threshold determine signed nonzero controls; values inside the threshold interval identify the zero-control set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed partition determines \(u\) pointwise and supplies the generalized-derivative active-set mask.

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Bound-Constrained Flow Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection equation for pointwise box-constrained incompressible-flow control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U=L^2(\Omega)^d\), let \(a,b\in L^\infty(\Omega)^d\) satisfy \(a<b\) componentwise, and let \(y(u)\) be a locally differentiable incompressible-flow state. For
\[
j(u)=J(y(u))+\frac\alpha2\|u\|_U^2,
\qquad U_{ad}=\{u\in U:a\leq u\leq b\},
\]
let \(z(u)\) solve the adjoint flow equation and write the reduced gradient as \(g(u)=\alpha u+B^*z(u)\). For any \(c>0\), the variational inequality \(\langle g(u),v-u\rangle_U\geq0\) for every \(v\in U_{ad}\) is equivalent to
\[
F(u)=u-P_{[a,b]}(u-cg(u))=0.
\]
Pointwise generalized derivatives of the projection define the semismooth Newton active and free regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound-constrained flow optimality is a componentwise projection equation coupling the control with an adjoint-flow gradient and inducing Newton active sets.
assumptions_latex: The control-to-state map is locally differentiable at the considered feasible control.
The adjoint equation represents the derivative of the flow objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: First-order bound-constrained optimality is equivalent to \(u=P_{[a,b]}(u-c(\alpha u+B^*z(u)))\).

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Ball-Constrained Flow Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise Euclidean-ball feasibility and projection residual for distributed incompressible-flow controls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)\), let \(r\in L^\infty(\Omega)\) satisfy \(r(x)>0\) almost everywhere, and define \(U_{\mathrm{ad}}=\{u\in U:\|u(x)\|_2\le r(x)\text{ a.e.}\}\). For a reduced gradient \(g(u)\in U\) and \(\gamma>0\), first-order stationarity is equivalently expressed by the projection residual
\[F(u)=u-\Pi_{U_{\mathrm{ad}}}(u-\gamma g(u))=0,\]
where
\[(\Pi_{U_{\mathrm{ad}}}v)(x)=\min\!\left\{1,\frac{r(x)}{\|v(x)\|_2}\right\}v(x)\]
with the multiplier interpreted as \(1\) when \(v(x)=0\). A semismooth Newton step applies a selected generalized derivative of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ball feasibility is enforced pointwise, and stationarity becomes a zero of the control projection residual used by semismooth Newton.
assumptions_latex: \(g:U\to U\) is defined and Newton differentiable near the iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\) is stationary exactly when \(F(u)=0\).

notation.meaning: Metric projection onto the admissible control set.

knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint-Based Flow Derivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced first derivative obtained from the compressible-flow state equation and its adjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the state \(y=S(u)\) satisfy \(E(y,u)=0\), where \(E:Y\times U\to Z\) and \(J:Y\times U\to\mathbb R\) are Fréchet differentiable. If \(E_y(y,u):Y\to Z\) is invertible, define the adjoint \(p\in Z^*\) by
\[E_y(y,u)^*p=-J_y(y,u).\]
Then the reduced functional \(j(u)=J(S(u),u)\) has derivative
\[j'(u)h=J_u(y,u)h+\langle p,E_u(y,u)h\rangle_{Z^*,Z}\]
for every \(h\in U\). Thus gradient evaluations require one state solve and one adjoint solve, independently of the number of control directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the flow state and one adjoint equation; their residual derivatives give the reduced derivative in every control direction.
assumptions_latex: The displayed duality pairing is well defined.

knowledge_statements.title: Semismooth BFGS-Newton Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid generalized Newton iteration with a BFGS approximation of an unavailable smooth derivative block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(z_0\), a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(B_0\), and a residual \(F(z)=0\), choose at iteration \(k\) a generalized-Jacobian model \(G_k=A_k+B_k\), where \(A_k\) is assembled from semismooth terms. Compute \(d_k\) from
\[(A_k+B_k)d_k=-F(z_k),\qquad z_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_kd_k,\]
with \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) chosen by globalization. Set \(s_k=z_{k+1}-z_k\), \(q_k=F_s(z_{k+1})-F_s(z_k)\), and, when \(s_k^\top q_k>0\), update
\[B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^\top B_k}{s_k^\top B_ks_k}+\frac{q_kq_k^\top}{s_k^\top q_k}.\]
Stop when the prescribed residual tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each step combines an exact semismooth derivative block with a positive-definite BFGS approximation and a globalized residual solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration returns \(z_k\) when \(\|F(z_k)\|\) meets the chosen tolerance.

notation.meaning: Selected derivative of the semismooth residual part.
Residual component used to form secant pairs.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V_kd=-F_k\) be a generalized Newton equation whose variable indices are partitioned into an active set \(\mathcal A_k\) and a free set \(\mathcal I_k\). Suppose the active-set formulation replaces the active block rows by the prescriptions \(d_{\mathcal A_k}=b_{\mathcal A_k}\). Substitution into the free block rows gives
\[V_{\mathcal I_k\mathcal I_k}d_{\mathcal I_k}=-F_{k,\mathcal I_k}-V_{\mathcal I_k\mathcal A_k}b_{\mathcal A_k}.\]
After solving this system, reconstruct \(d\) by assigning its free components to \(d_{\mathcal I_k}\) and its active components to \(b_{\mathcal A_k}\). If \(V_{\mathcal I_k\mathcal I_k}\) is nonsingular, the reconstructed vector is the unique solution of these free Newton rows together with the prescribed active-variable equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prescribe the active components, solve the free Newton rows for the remaining components, and reconstruct the unique direction for that reduced active-set system.

children.title: Saddle-Point Newton Systems
children.top_down_role: Indefinite Newton systems arising from KKT and PDE optimality equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Point Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block KKT form of equality-constrained or PDE-constrained Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a symmetric primal Newton block and \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) the linearized constraint operator. The Newton increments satisfy the saddle-point system
\[\begin{pmatrix}H_k&A_k^\top\\A_k&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}d_x\\d_\lambda\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}r_{d,k}\\r_{p,k}\end{pmatrix}.\]
If \(A_k\) has full row rank and \(H_k\) is positive definite on \(\ker A_k\), the block matrix is nonsingular. Hence the primal and multiplier increments are uniquely determined despite the matrix being indefinite whenever \(m>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT linearization yields an indefinite two-by-two block system that is nonsingular under constraint qualification and reduced positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The saddle-point matrix is nonsingular and the Newton increment is unique.

notation.meaning: Primal Hessian or generalized Newton block.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the saddle-point nonsingularity criterion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and nonsingularity criterion fit the saddle-point leaf and are standard, but the record supplies no source locator. The substantive reduced-positive-definiteness criterion therefore requires an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), and
\[F(x,\lambda)=\bigl(r_d(x,\lambda),\Phi(a(x),\lambda)\bigr),\]
where \(a:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) has Jacobian \(A\) and \(\Phi\) acts componentwise. Suppose a generalized Jacobian selection has the block form
\[V=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^\top\\D_aA&D_\lambda\end{pmatrix},\]
with diagonal derivative selections \(D_a\) and \(D_\lambda\). If \(H=H^\top\), then \(V\) is symmetric exactly when \(D_aA=A\), since \(D_\lambda\) is diagonal. Consequently, complementarity weights for which \(D_aA\ne A\) produce a nonsymmetric generalized Newton matrix despite the symmetric primal block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a symmetric primal block and diagonal complementarity blocks, the Newton matrix is symmetric exactly when its weighted lower-left block equals the transpose of the upper-right block; otherwise it is nonsymmetric.

knowledge_statements.title: Assembled Generalized Jacobians
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit sparse matrix realization of one generalized-derivative selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a discretized semismooth residual \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(z_k)\). An assembled realization stores matrix entries satisfying
\[(V_k)_{ij}=e_i^\top V_ke_j,\qquad 1\le i,j\le n,\]
including the derivative selections fixed by the current active set. The generalized Newton direction is obtained from
\[V_kd_k=-F(z_k).\]
The assembly is consistent precisely when its matrix-vector product equals the selected derivative action \(V_kv\) for every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a generalized Jacobian, assemble all selected derivative blocks explicitly, and solve its linear system for the Newton direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Newton Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized Newton solve using derivative actions without storing the system matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(z_k\), residual \(F(z_k)\), and an oracle \(\mathcal V_k(v)=V_kv\) for a fixed selection \(V_k\in\partial F(z_k)\), apply a Krylov solver to
\[\mathcal V_k(d_k)=-F(z_k)\]
using only evaluations of \(\mathcal V_k\) and, when present, a preconditioner action. Terminate the inner solve when
\[\|\mathcal V_k(d_k)+F(z_k)\|\le\eta_k\|F(z_k)\|,\qquad 0\le\eta_k<1,\]
and update \(z_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_kd_k\). No entries of \(V_k\) need be assembled or stored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Krylov method accesses a fixed generalized Jacobian only through vector products and stops at a prescribed relative linear residual.
assumptions_latex: The oracle uses one fixed derivative selection throughout the inner solve.
\(V_k\) is nonsingular on the solved space.

knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint-Based Reduced Derivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced gradient and Hessian-vector action without explicitly forming the control-to-state derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E(y,u)=0\), \(j(u)=J(y(u),u)\), and let \(p\) solve \(E_y(y,u)^*p=-J_y(y,u)\). Then
\[j'(u)=J_u(y,u)+E_u(y,u)^*p.\]
For a direction \(h\), compute the incremental state \(w\) from \(E_yw=-E_uh\), differentiate the adjoint equation to obtain an incremental adjoint \(q\), and evaluate
\[j''(u)h=D_{(y,u)}\!\left(J_u+E_u^*p\right)[w,h]+E_u^*q.\]
Thus both reduced gradients and curvature actions are realized through state, adjoint, and incremental solves rather than an explicitly assembled reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State and adjoint solves provide the reduced gradient; incremental state and adjoint solves provide Hessian-vector products.
assumptions_latex: All displayed derivatives and duality actions are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed formulas realize \(j'(u)\) and \(j''(u)h\) without forming \(S'(u)\) or the reduced Hessian matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Factorization Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse direct solution of an assembled generalized Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an assembled nonsingular Newton matrix \(V_k\) and right-hand side \(b_k=-F(z_k)\), compute a permutation \(P_k\) and a stable sparse factorization, for example
\[P_kV_kP_k^\top=L_kU_k\]
for a general matrix, or a pivoted symmetric-indefinite factorization when applicable. Solve successively with the triangular factors and undo the permutation to obtain \(d_k\). Accept the linear solve when
\[\|V_kd_k-b_k\|\le\tau_k\|b_k\|.\]
The output is the direct-factorization Newton direction, up to pivoting and floating-point error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permute and factor the assembled Newton matrix, use triangular solves, and verify the resulting linear residual.
assumptions_latex: The factorization uses stable pivoting appropriate to the matrix class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed \(d_k\) satisfies the Newton system to the stated residual tolerance.

children.title: Krylov Newton Solves
children.top_down_role: Iterative solution of large generalized Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Krylov Newton Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioned iterative solution of large generalized Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At outer iteration \(k\), fix a generalized Newton matrix \(V_k\), choose a nonsingular preconditioner \(M_k\), and apply an appropriate Krylov method to
\[M_k^{-1}V_kd=-M_k^{-1}F(z_k).\]
Use conjugate gradients only when the preconditioned operator is symmetric positive definite; use a nonsymmetric method such as GMRES otherwise. Stop at the first \(d_k\) satisfying
\[\|V_kd_k+F(z_k)\|\le\eta_k\|F(z_k)\|,\qquad 0\le\eta_k<1.\]
Return \(d_k\) as the inexact Newton direction for the outer update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a matrix-compatible preconditioned Krylov method until the generalized Newton residual meets the forcing tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The selected \(V_k\) remains fixed during the Krylov solve.
The Krylov family matches the symmetry and definiteness of the preconditioned operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned direction satisfies the prescribed inexact Newton residual bound.

children.title: Multigrid Newton Solves

knowledge_statements.title: Multigrid Newton Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric or algebraic multigrid applied to a discretized semismooth Newton correction equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a Newton matrix hierarchy \(J_0,\ldots,J_L\), transfers \(P_\ell\) and \(R_\ell\), smoothers \(S_\ell\), residual \(r_L=-F(x)\), and initial correction \(d_L^{(0)}=0\), apply multigrid cycles to \(J_Ld_L=r_L\). Each cycle performs presmoothing, restricts the residual by \(r_{\ell-1}=R_\ell(r_\ell-J_\ell d_\ell)\), solves or recursively approximates \(J_{\ell-1}e_{\ell-1}=r_{\ell-1}\), corrects by \(d_\ell\leftarrow d_\ell+P_\ell e_{\ell-1}\), and postsmooths. Stop when \(\lVert r_L-J_Ld_L\rVert\leq\eta\lVert r_L\rVert\), and output \(x^+=x+d_L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply recursive smoothing, residual restriction, coarse correction, and prolongation until the Newton linear residual meets the prescribed relative tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(J_\ell\in\mathbb R^{n_\ell\times n_\ell}\) is nonsingular for \(0\leq\ell\leq L\).

abla J_k(u),vangle_k\left[\int_0^1\langle
abla^2J_k(u+t\gamma v)v,vangle_k\,dtight]^{-1}. Then -(1-\delta)\gamma\langle
abla J_k(u),vangle_k\le J_k(u)-J_k(u+\gamma v)\le-\gamma\langle

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recursive FAS V-Cycle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive operator definition of a one-coarse-call FAS V-cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $B_1(u_1^{(0)})\approx A_1^{-1}$. For each $k=2,\ldots,L$, start from $u_k^{(0)}$, compute $u_k^{(l)}=S_k(u_k^{(l-1)},f_k)$ for $l=1,\ldots,v_1$, and set $u_{k-1}^{(0)}=\widehat I_k^{k-1}u_k^{(v_1)}$. Define $u_{k-1}=B_{k-1}(u_{k-1}^{(0)})\bigl[I_k^{k-1}(f_k-A_k(u_k^{(v_1)}))+A_{k-1}(u_{k-1}^{(0)})\bigr]$, then set $u_k^{(v_1+1)}=u_k^{(v_1)}+I_{k-1}^k\bigl(u_{k-1}-\widehat I_k^{k-1}u_k^{(v_1)}\bigr)$. Finally compute $u_k^{(l)}=S_k(u_k^{(l-1)},f_k)$ for $l=v_1+2,\ldots,v_1+v_2+1$ and define $B_k(u_k^{(0)})f_k=u_k^{(v_1+v_2+1)}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting with an approximate level-one inverse, the recursive FAS V-cycle defines each finer-level solution operator by presmoothing, one recursive coarse full-approximation solve, prolongated coarse-grid correction, and postsmoothing.
assumptions_latex: I_k^{k-1},\ \widehat I_k^{k-1},\ I_{k-1}^k\text{ are the required interlevel transfer operators.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_k(u_k^{(0)})f_k=u_k^{(v_1+v_2+1)}\quad(k=2,\ldots,L)\text{ defines the recursive FAS V-cycle operator.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recursive multigrid approximate inverse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive operator form of a multigrid cycle, including the symmetric smoothing variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set $B_1=A_1^{-1}$. For $k\ge2$ and $f_k\in V_k$, perform $\nu_1$ updates
\[
u^{(l)}=u^{(l-1)}+R_k\bigl(f_k-A_ku^{(l-1)}\bigr),\quad l=1,\ldots,\nu_1.
\]
Set
\[
q=B_{k-1}I_k^{k-1}\bigl(f_k-A_ku^{(\nu_1)}\bigr),\qquad u^{(\nu_1+1)}=u^{(\nu_1)}+I_{k-1}^kq.
\]
Apply $\nu_2$ residual-correction postsmoothing updates and define $B_kf_k=u^{(\nu_1+\nu_2+1)}$; for a symmetric multigrid scheme use $R_k^{\top}$ in postsmoothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recursive approximate inverse first smooths, applies a coarse correction computed with the lower-level approximate inverse, then postsmooths; transpose smoothing is used after correction in the symmetric variant.
assumptions_latex: A_k,\ R_k,\ I_k^{k-1},\ I_{k-1}^k\text{ and }B_{k-1}\text{ are defined on the corresponding level spaces.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two uniform mesh-order bilinear-form estimates for projection and intergrid operators in the elliptic-control multigrid scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist constants \(C_{\mathcal P}\) and \(C_I\), independent of \(k\), such that
\[

\]
for \(\mathbf w,\mathbf v\in\mathcal V_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Levelwise energy contraction of multigrid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contraction theorem under smoothing and regularity-approximation assumptions; it does not assert a level-uniform contraction factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose that for every $k>1$, $R_k$ satisfies the smoothing bound
\[
C_R\frac{\|u\|_k^2}{\lambda_k}\le (R_ku,u)_k\le c(A_k^{-1}u,u)_k\qquad(\forall u\in V_k),
\]
with $C_R,c>0$ independent of $u$ and $k$, and that for some $0<\alpha\le1$ and $C_\alpha>0$ independent of $k$,
\[
\bigl(A_k(I_k-I_{k-1}^kP_{k-1})u,u\bigr)_k
\le C_\alpha\left(\frac{\|A_ku\|_k^2}{\lambda_k}\right)^\alpha
(A_ku,u)_k^{1-\alpha}\qquad(\forall u\in V_k).
\]
Under the stated symmetric positive-definite smoother setting, with $S_k=I_k-R_kA_k$ nonnegative and $A_kS_k=S_kA_k$, there exists for each level a constant $0<\delta_k<1$ such that
\[
(A_kM_ku,u)_k\le\delta_k(A_ku,u)_k\qquad\forall u\in V_k.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the smoother has the required spectral-energy bounds and the coarse space has the stated approximation property, then the multigrid error propagator is a strict contraction in the level energy inner product, with a possibly level-dependent factor below one.
assumptions_latex: R_k\text{ is symmetric positive definite, }S_k=I_k-R_kA_k\text{ is nonnegative, and }A_kS_k=S_kA_k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall k\ \exists\delta_k\in(0,1)\ \forall u\in V_k:\quad (A_kM_ku,u)_k\le\delta_k(A_ku,u)_k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recursive multigrid cycle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General multigrid iteration for the level-k linear system A_k u_k=f_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an initial approximation $u_k^{(0)}$, solve exactly when $k=1$. For $k>1$, apply $
u_1$ presmoothing steps $u_k^{(l)}=S(u_k^{(l-1)},f_k)$; form $r_k=f_k-A_ku_k^{(
u_1)}$ and restrict it as $r_{k-1}=I_k^{k-1}r_k$; initialize $u_{k-1}=0$ and apply $\gamma$ recursive multigrid calls to $A_{k-1}u_{k-1}=r_{k-1}$; correct by $u_k^{(
u_1+1)}=u_k^{(
u_1)}+I_{k-1}^ku_{k-1}$; then apply $
u_2$ postsmoothing steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a fine-grid approximation, the cycle presmooths, restricts the residual, approximately solves the coarse residual equation using gamma recursive cycles, prolongates the coarse correction, and postsmooths; the coarsest system is solved exactly.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Approximation Scheme Multigrid Cycle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A recursive FAS cycle for a hierarchy of nonlinear discrete equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial approximation $u_k^{(0)}$ for $A_k(u_k)=f_k$, solve exactly if $k=1$. Otherwise compute $v_1$ presmoothing iterates $u_k^{(l)}=S(u_k^{(l-1)},f_k)$; form $r_k=f_k-A_k(u_k^{(v_1)})$ and $r_{k-1}=I_k^{k-1}r_k$; set $u_{k-1}=\widehat I_k^{k-1}u_k^{(v_1)}$ and $f_{k-1}=r_{k-1}+A_{k-1}(u_{k-1})$; apply $\gamma$ recursive FAS calls to $A_{k-1}(u_{k-1})=f_{k-1}$; correct by $u_k^{(v_1+1)}=u_k^{(v_1)}+I_{k-1}^k\bigl(u_{k-1}-\widehat I_k^{k-1}u_k^{(v_1)}\bigr)$; and perform $v_2$ postsmoothing steps $u_k^{(l)}=S(u_k^{(l-1)},f_k)$ for $l=v_1+2,\ldots,v_1+v_2+1$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The FAS cycle smooths the fine-grid approximation, restricts its residual and approximation to construct a coarse nonlinear equation, recursively solves that equation, prolongates the difference between the corrected and restricted coarse approximations, and postsmooths; the coarsest equation is solved exactly.
assumptions_latex: I_k^{k-1},\ \widehat I_k^{k-1},\ I_{k-1}^k\text{ are residual-restriction, approximation-restriction, and prolongation operators.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_k^{(v_1+v_2+1)}\text{ is the approximation produced by one }\gamma\text{-cycle FAS application.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nested Iteration and Full Multigrid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines nested or cascadic iteration, full multigrid, and the FMG interpolator; also records the extract's Poisson-model complexity comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from a coarse working level \(\ell=K<M\), solve on level \(\ell\) and use \(u_{\ell+1}=\widetilde I_{\ell}^{\ell+1}u_\ell\) as the initial approximation on the next finer level. This coarse-to-fine initialization is nested or cascadic iteration. Combining nested iteration with a multigrid scheme defines the full multigrid (FMG) method, and \(\widetilde I_{\ell}^{\ell+1}\) is called the FMG interpolator. For the stated Poisson model problems, the extract gives complexity \(\mathcal O(n\log n)\) for plain multigrid and \(\mathcal O(n)\) for FMG.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coarse-grid solution is interpolated to initialize the solve on the next finer grid. This is nested or cascadic iteration; combined with multigrid cycles, it gives full multigrid, and the interpolation is called the FMG interpolator. For the stated Poisson model problems, the extract reports O(n log n) complexity for plain multigrid and O(n) for FMG.
assumptions_latex: \text{The complexity comparison is restricted to the stated Poisson model problems.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Coarse-to-fine interpolated initialization is nested iteration; combined with multigrid it defines FMG, with the stated Poisson-model complexity comparison.}

children.title: Active-Set-Aware Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Preconditioners adapted to changing active and free blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set-Aware Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block preconditioning after partitioning Newton variables into current active and free indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) and \(F\) be the current active and free index sets, and let \(\Pi_{A,F}\) permute variables accordingly. For a Newton matrix \(J\), an active-set-aware left preconditioner has the form \[M_{A,F}^{-1}=\Pi_{A,F}^{T}\begin{pmatrix}I_A&0\\0&\widehat J_{FF}^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\Pi_{A,F},\] or a block-triangular analogue retaining selected active-free couplings. Here \(\widehat J_{FF}\) is an inexpensive nonsingular approximation to the free block \(J_{FF}\). When the partition changes, the permutation and affected blocks are updated before applying \(M_{A,F}^{-1}\) to the Newton residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permute active and free variables, enforce the active block directly, and precondition the free Newton block with an inexpensive updated approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{A,F}^{-1}\) respects the current active-free partition and supplies a well-defined preconditioned Newton system.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the container, but the identity active block and claim that it enforces the active variables require a source and problem-specific justification.

children.title: Block Preconditioners

knowledge_statements.title: Block Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal and triangular preconditioners for a two-block Newton linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}\), let \(\widehat A\) and \(\widehat D\) be readily invertible nonsingular approximations of the diagonal blocks. Standard block preconditioners include \[P_D=\begin{pmatrix}\widehat A&0\\0&\widehat D\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_L=\begin{pmatrix}\widehat A&0\\C&\widehat D\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_U=\begin{pmatrix}\widehat A&B\\0&\widehat D\end{pmatrix}.\] Their inverses are applied by independent diagonal solves for \(P_D\), or by forward or backward block substitution for \(P_L\) and \(P_U\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled Newton matrix can be preconditioned using approximate diagonal blocks, optionally retaining one coupling block and applying block substitution.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{(n+m)\times(n+m)}\) has the displayed conforming block structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_D^{-1}K\), \(P_L^{-1}K\), and \(P_U^{-1}K\) are well-defined preconditioned block systems.
